A golden-brown, crisp breadcrumb crust tops the stuffing, offering a textural contrast. The peppers rest in a shallow pool of rich, deep red crushed tomato sauce, enhancing their natural color. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the top and around the plate, providing a pop of color and aromatic freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors. The presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space, evoking a casual yet refined bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping into the tomato sauce.
Accompanied by a simple green salad with a lemon-herb vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Arrange cut-side up in a large baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and chopped chili (if using). Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add ground chicken to the pan. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Stir in uncooked rice, 400g of crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice absorbs most liquid and is partially cooked.
Stir in most of the fresh chopped basil. Reserve some for garnish.
Spoon chicken and rice mixture evenly into bell pepper halves.
Pour remaining 400g crushed tomatoes around the stuffed peppers in the baking dish.
In a small bowl, combine breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan (if using). Sprinkle mixture over each stuffed pepper.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until peppers are tender and topping is golden brown. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with reserved fresh basil before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a minimum internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For softer peppers, par-boil them for 5 minutes before stuffing.

recipes.recipe_name: Puglian Octopus and Salt Cod Stew
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl, showcasing a rustic yet refined main course. Tender, braised octopus chunks, approximately 2-3 cm, are intertwined with flaky, pan-fried salt cod pieces, about 3-4 cm. Both seafood elements retain their distinct shapes and textures. The vibrant red-orange sauce, derived from cooked-down cherry tomatoes, generously coats the seafood. Dark, pitted black olives and bright green capers are scattered throughout, providing contrasting colors and briny notes. A final drizzle of luminous green extra virgin olive oil creates a glistening sheen. Fresh, coarsely chopped flat-leaf parsley is liberally sprinkled over the top, adding a burst of fresh green. The composition is organic and natural, allowing the rich textures and colors to speak for themselves. The plate maintains appropriate negative space, avoiding overcrowding. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and classic silver flatware, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting to highlight the dish's inviting warmth and authentic Italian character.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a glass of crisp local white wine.
instructions: Desalt salt cod: Rinse cod. Submerge in cold water. Change water every 8-12 hours for 2-3 days. Keep refrigerated.

Prepare octopus: In a large pot, combine octopus with enough cold water to cover. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer gently until tender, about 45-60 minutes. Test with a fork. Drain. Let cool. Cut octopus into 2-3 cm chunks.
Prepare aromatics: In a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven, heat 50 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Do not brown garlic.
Build flavor base: Add anchovy fillets to the skillet. Mash with a spoon until dissolved into the oil.
Add tomatoes and wine: Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften. Pour in white wine. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 minutes.

Combine and simmer: Add octopus chunks, black olives, and capers to the skillet. Stir gently. Add vegetable broth for saucy consistency. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover. Cook for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

Cook salt cod: Gently pat desalted salt cod dry. Cut into 3-4 cm pieces. In a separate pan, heat remaining 50 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add salt cod pieces. Pan-fry for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly golden and flaky.
Finish dish: Gently fold the pan-fried salt cod into the octopus and tomato stew. Cook for another 5 minutes, allowing flavors to combine. Taste. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve: Stir in fresh chopped parsley just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Potato Salad with Poached Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of the salad is elegantly presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone. The arrangement is organic and unforced, showcasing the distinct components. Shredded, tender poached chicken, with its pale white color, forms a soft base or is gently nestled amongst the vegetables. Firm, off-white 1.5 cm potato cubes, showing their natural skin, are interspersed with vibrant, soft red halved cherry tomatoes. Fresh, crisp mixed salad greens, in varying shades of green, are lightly tossed throughout, adding height and freshness. A few small, bright green dill or parsley leaves are scattered as a natural garnish. The plate is clean, with ample negative space around the mounded salad. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, natural overhead lighting. The background is minimalist, with a subtle hint of a potted plant or natural wood texture, emphasizing an eco-conscious, clean aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare brine: Dissolve 20g sea salt in 1 litre non-chlorinated water. Stir until fully dissolved.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Do not peel.
Wash cherry tomatoes. Halve larger tomatoes. Leave smaller ones whole.
Place potato cubes into a clean glass jar. Pour brine over potatoes. Ensure potatoes are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed. Cover loosely or use an airlock lid.
Place tomatoes into a separate clean glass jar. Pour brine over tomatoes. Ensure tomatoes are fully submerged. Cover loosely or use an airlock lid.

Ferment potatoes and tomatoes at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Burp jars daily. Taste after 3 days. Fermentation is complete when desired tanginess is reached. Refrigerate to slow fermentation.

Poach chicken: Place chicken breast in a small saucepan. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from water. Cool slightly.
Shred cooled chicken using two forks.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 30ml olive oil, juice from half a lemon, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, fermented potato cubes, and fermented cherry tomatoes. Add salad greens. Pour dressing over ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Portion salad onto individual starter plates. Garnish with fresh dill or parsley, if using. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure fermentation jars are clean and sanitized to prevent mold.
Fermentation time varies with temperature; warmer temperatures speed up the process.
The remaining lemon half can be zested over the finished dish for extra aroma.

recipes.recipe_name: Confit Bacalhau, Pomme Purée, Olive Caviar
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly confit portion of bacalhau, flaked into large, tender pieces, rests slightly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent to the fish, a single, elegant quenelle of velvety smooth potato puree provides a soft, creamy counterpoint. A delicate scattering of translucent olive oil caviar spheres glistens beside the puree, offering precise bursts of flavor. A small, vibrant pool of crimson smoked paprika oil is artfully drizzled nearby, adding a pop of color and aromatic depth. The composition is clean, architectural, and minimalist, with generous white space emphasizing the purity of each component. The dish is presented on a polished grey marble surface, accompanied by a single silver fork and knife on a crisp white linen napkin folded precisely into a triangle. Dramatic overhead lighting casts subtle shadows, highlighting the dish's refined textures.
instructions: Desalt the salt cod: Rinse cod thoroughly. Submerge cod in cold water for 24-48 hours. Change water every 8 hours. Ensure cod is fully desalted.

Prepare confit cod: Pat desalted cod dry. Place cod in a small saucepan. Cover completely with 500 ml olive oil. Heat gently over very low heat. Maintain oil temperature between 60-70°C. Cook for 25-30 minutes, or until cod flakes easily. Do not boil. Carefully remove cod. Let cool slightly. Gently flake into large pieces.

Prepare potato puree: Peel and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Place in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain potatoes thoroughly. Pass hot potatoes through a fine-mesh tamis or ricer into a clean pot. Add butter and milk. Stir vigorously until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare olive oil caviar: In a bowl, whisk 2g sodium alginate into 200 ml distilled water until fully dissolved. Let stand 30 minutes to remove air bubbles. In a separate bowl, dissolve 5g calcium chloride in 500 ml distilled water. Fill a syringe or dropper with high-quality olive oil. Slowly drip olive oil into the calcium chloride bath from a height. Small spheres will form. Use a slotted spoon to remove spheres. Rinse spheres gently in a bowl of clean water. Drain and set aside.

Prepare smoked paprika oil: In a small saucepan, combine 50 ml olive oil and smoked paprika. Heat gently over low heat for 5 minutes. Do not let it smoke. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth. Discard paprika solids. Keep oil warm.

Plate the dish: Place a quenelle or elegant swoosh of potato puree slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange a few large, flaky pieces of confit bacalhau next to the puree. Carefully place a small cluster of olive oil caviar spheres beside the cod. Drizzle a small amount of smoked paprika oil artfully around the components. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Caramelized Onions and Thyme
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of tender, braised chicken thigh is centrally placed on a clean, white round porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked to a rich golden-brown, is nestled in a generous bed of deeply caramelized onions, their amber and golden hues creating a vibrant contrast. A rich, glossy sauce, derived from the braising liquid, pools around the chicken and onions. Fresh green thyme sprigs are artfully placed on top of the chicken and scattered amongst the onions, providing a burst of color and freshness. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its succulent texture. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table, with a folded white linen napkin and classic silver flatware positioned to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors in a professional, inviting manner. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the rich sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette makes a classic accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter and sliced onions to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes until onions are deeply caramelized and tender.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half, about 5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock and 4 sprigs of thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove thyme sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and remaining fresh thyme sprigs before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Artichoke, Soppressata, and Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of deeply braised beef is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef, cut into substantial 4 cm cubes, is rich dark brown, incredibly tender, and glistening with a savory, unctuous sauce. Interspersed among the beef are tender quartered artichoke hearts, vibrant green, along with crisp, golden-brown diced bacon and reddish-orange diced soppressata, adding textural contrast and pops of color. The sauce, a rich, dark reduction, coats all components evenly. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh counterpoint. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a white linen napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce
Serve alongside creamy polenta or pasta
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Add diced bacon to the pot. Cook until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Add diced soppressata to the pot. Cook until slightly crisp. Remove soppressata and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer the covered pot to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender and easily pulls apart with a fork.
Remove pot from oven. Discard herb sprigs.
Stir in drained quartered artichoke hearts, cooked bacon, and cooked soppressata. Simmer on stovetop for 10 minutes to heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Garnish individual servings with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Cheesy Garlic Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Cheesy Garlic Mushroom Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The fettuccine is neatly twirled into a moderate mound in the center, coated in a creamy, golden-yellow cheddar sauce with visible slices of earthy brown mushrooms and flecks of minced garlic. Resting slightly overlapping on one side of the pasta mound are two thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken medallions, revealing their tender, white interior. A vibrant scattering of freshly chopped green parsley provides a fresh contrast over both the pasta and chicken. The overall composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, with standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its inviting textures and colors against a soft, blurred restaurant background.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Bake 10-12 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.
While chicken bakes, cook fettuccine in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Thinly slice mushrooms. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.
In the same pan used for chicken (or a clean large skillet), melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and turn golden. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour in chicken stock and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Grate cheddar cheese. Gradually add grated cheddar to the sauce, stirring constantly until melted and smooth. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Add drained fettuccine to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. Chop fresh parsley.
Slice rested chicken breasts diagonally into thick medallions. Do not fan.
Plate individual portions of pasta. Arrange sliced chicken medallions on top or beside the pasta. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomato-Bell Pepper Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Mediterranean Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomato-Bell Pepper Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The base features a generous mound of short pasta (e.g., rigatoni) tossed with a vibrant, rustic tomato-bell pepper ragout. The ragout showcases tender, sliced red and yellow bell peppers, quartered cremini mushrooms, and diced onions, all coated in a rich, slightly chunky tomato sauce. Two golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast pieces rest atop the pasta. Beside the pasta, a neat cluster of golden-crisp roasted potato wedges provides textural contrast. The dish is garnished with fresh, torn basil leaves, scattered artfully to add a pop of green. Natural, even lighting illuminates the plate, highlighting the varied textures and colors. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, with minimal, blurred background elements.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve or quarter small new potatoes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 125ml pasta water.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Slice bell peppers into strips. Quarter mushrooms. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté onion until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add garlic, bell pepper strips, and quartered mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften slightly. Stir in dried oregano and red pepper flakes (if using).
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
Return seared chicken breasts to the ragout. Simmer for 5 minutes, turning chicken once, to heat through. If needed, slice chicken breasts in half for easier serving.
Add cooked pasta to the ragout. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water if the sauce is too thick.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh torn basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single, generous portion in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled amidst saffron-infused rice. The rice is moist and free-flowing, not compacted, showcasing vibrant red and yellow bell pepper diced into 2 cm pieces, and earthy sliced mushrooms. Small bursts of red from diced tomatoes are visible. A light sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides a contrasting color and freshness. The composition is balanced and organic, allowing ingredients to naturally mingle. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A clean white linen napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background, creating an approachable yet refined visual.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up juices.
Offer a simple green salad on the side.
instructions: Dice chicken into 3-4 cm chunks.
Chop onion.
Mince garlic.
Slice mushrooms.
Dice bell peppers into 2 cm pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or braiser over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook to 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add onion, bell peppers, and mushrooms to skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add garlic, smoked paprika, and saffron threads. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to skillet. Stir well to coat rice grains. Cook for 2 minutes, toasting lightly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to skillet. Stir gently to combine.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly.
Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Tequila-Lime Glazed Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two golden-brown, roasted chicken thighs, presented whole, with crispy skin and a glossy, reddish-orange glaze. The chicken is placed slightly overlapping on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections, off-white or light gray in color. A small pool of the vibrant orange-chili glaze gathers around the chicken. Bright green, freshly chopped mint leaves are sprinkled generously over the chicken and plate. A few bright yellow lime wedges are casually placed beside the chicken. The chicken exhibits visible seared marks and succulent, juicy texture. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, showing subtle grain and wear. A casually folded beige cloth napkin is visible in the corner. Warm, soft lighting emanates from above, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The background is slightly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.

ingredients.name: Fresh red chili, deseeded and minced

instructions: Combine tequila, lime juice, 30 ml orange juice, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Add chicken thighs. Marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature or up to 4 hours refrigerated.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Remove chicken from marinade, shaking off excess. Reserve marinade.
Sear chicken, skin-side down, for 6-8 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken roasts, combine remaining 90 ml orange juice, orange zest, minced chili, honey, and reserved marinade in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until glaze thickens slightly.
Once chicken is cooked, remove from oven. Brush generously with the warm glaze.
Garnish with fresh chopped mint. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tequila-Lime Chicken with Chili-Mint Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, cooked to perfection, is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken has a crisp exterior, with tender meat visible if sliced into thick pieces. It is generously topped with vibrant chili-mint salsa, featuring small, uniform cubes of red Roma tomatoes, finely diced purple-red onion, and bright green minced jalapeño, fresh mint, and cilantro. Colors are vivid. A lime wedge rests beside the chicken. The plate has moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and a traditional Mexican ceramic bowl with white rice. Warm corn tortillas, wrapped in cloth, are nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. The background is a blurred, casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Serve with black beans
Serve with Mexican rice
instructions: Prepare chicken marinade: In a bowl, whisk together 60 ml tequila, 60 ml lime juice, 30 ml olive oil, minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, 5 g salt, and black pepper.
Marinate chicken: Add chicken thighs to the marinade. Ensure chicken is fully coated. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 2 hours.

Prepare chili-mint salsa: In a separate bowl, combine diced Roma tomatoes, finely diced red onion, minced jalapeño, chopped mint, chopped cilantro, 15 ml lime juice, 15 ml olive oil, and 2 g salt. Stir gently.
Cook chicken: Heat a large skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat. Remove chicken from marinade, discarding excess marinade.
Sear chicken: Place chicken thighs in the hot pan. Cook for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Chicken should be golden brown and cooked through.
Rest chicken: Transfer cooked chicken to a cutting board. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Plate and serve: Serve chicken whole or sliced into thick pieces. Top generously with chili-mint salsa.
notes: Do not marinate chicken for longer than 2 hours due to the acidity of the lime juice, which can start to 'cook' the chicken'.

recipes.recipe_name: Ethiopian Coffee & Cardamom Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, meticulously cut slice of the Ethiopian Coffee & Cardamom Entremet stands upright on a pristine, elegant porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The entremet reveals distinct, architectural layers: a rich, dark almond-cocoa sponge base, followed by a creamy, light brown Ethiopian coffee mousse, a pale, almost white vanilla-cardamom coconut crèmeux, another layer of coffee mousse, and finally, a top layer of the dark almond-cocoa sponge. The entire entremet is encased in a flawlessly smooth, reflective dark chocolate mirror glaze. A few precisely placed, golden-brown toasted almond slivers are delicately arranged on top of the glaze. The plate, predominantly white, provides abundant negative space, highlighting the dessert's sophisticated structure and contrasting textures. The setting is a pristine white marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle shadows, emphasizing the entremet's sculptural form. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the focus remains entirely on the dessert's refined artistry.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a 20 cm x 20 cm baking tray with parchment paper.
For the Vegan Almond-Cocoa Sponge: Whip aquafaba in a stand mixer until foamy. Gradually add 100g sugar, whipping until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold in almond flour, cocoa powder, cornstarch, and 2 ml vanilla extract. Spread batter evenly onto prepared tray.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely. Cut into two 8 cm x 18 cm rectangles.
For the Vanilla-Cardamom Coconut Crèmeux: In a saucepan, whisk 200 ml coconut cream, 50g sugar, 5g cornstarch, 1 ml vanilla, and cardamom.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened. Pour into a shallow dish, cover with plastic wrap touching the surface, and chill for 2 hours.
For the Ethiopian Coffee Mousse: In a saucepan, combine 300 ml coconut cream, 50g sugar, instant espresso powder, and 2g agar-agar. Bring to a simmer, whisking constantly, until agar-agar dissolves.
Remove from heat, cool to room temperature. Whip until light and airy.
To assemble the Entremet: Place one sponge rectangle in a 8 cm x 18 cm silicone mold or a loaf pan lined with plastic wrap.
Spread half of the coffee mousse over the sponge. Place the chilled crèmeux on top. Top with the remaining coffee mousse.
Place the second sponge rectangle on top. Freeze for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
For the Dark Chocolate Mirror Glaze: Chop dark chocolate. In a saucepan, combine 100 ml coconut cream, 50g sugar, water, and 2g agar-agar. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly.
Pour hot mixture over chopped chocolate. Let sit for 2 minutes, then whisk until smooth and glossy. Cool to 35°C.
Remove entremet from freezer. Place on a wire rack over a baking tray. Pour glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage.
Let excess glaze drip. Carefully transfer entremet to a serving plate. Allow to thaw in the refrigerator for 1-2 hours before serving.
Garnish with toasted almond slivers.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Thyme-Cayenne Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, whole and plump with a golden-brown crust, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, pale orange-hued creamy sauce, infused with thyme and a hint of cayenne, is generously spooned over and around the chicken. Beside the chicken, a neat arrangement of golden-roasted baby potato halves displays slightly crisp edges and tender interiors. Vibrant green blanched asparagus spears are carefully placed adjacent to the potatoes, adding a fresh color contrast. A small fresh thyme sprig garnishes the chicken, providing an aromatic and visual highlight. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by polished silverware and a folded cotton napkin, creating a professional yet approachable modern bistro aesthetic. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and appealing colors. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, ensuring the dish remains the focal point.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve or quarter baby potatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, pepper. Roast 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and half of the cayenne pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Transfer chicken to a plate. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan bottom. Cook 1 minute until reduced by half.
Stir in chicken stock, heavy cream, remaining cayenne pepper, and 3-4 thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet with the sauce. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 2-3 minutes to heat through.
While sauce simmers, blanch asparagus spears in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Plate one chicken breast per serving. Spoon generous amount of creamy sauce over chicken. Arrange roasted potatoes and blanched asparagus neatly alongside. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Sweet Basil & Coconut Bread Pudding Bites with Crispy Garlic-Chicken Crumble
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature squares of golden-brown Thai sweet basil and coconut bread pudding are meticulously arranged on a clean, elegant white porcelain rectangular platter. Each bite-sized pudding piece features a soft, custardy interior with visible specks of vibrant green Thai basil, contrasting with a lightly crisp, caramelized exterior. A delicate sprinkle of finely crushed, crispy garlic-chicken crumble adorns the top of each piece, offering a textural contrast and subtle savory counterpoint to the sweetness. A single, fresh, small Thai basil leaf is placed artfully on top of each pudding bite as a garnish. The arrangement on the platter is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the refined presentation. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting that highlights the food's natural colors and textures.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.

Boil chicken breast until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Cool completely. Shred finely. Spread shredded chicken on a baking sheet. Bake at 150°C for 20-25 minutes, or until very dry and slightly crispy. Alternatively, pan-fry until crispy.
Thinly slice garlic cloves. Heat vegetable oil in a small pan over medium-low heat. Fry garlic slices until golden and crispy. Remove garlic with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towel. Reserve oil.
Combine crispy chicken and fried garlic. Add 10g palm sugar and a small pinch of salt. Lightly crush into a coarse crumble. Set aside.
Cut bread into 2 cm cubes. Place in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk coconut milk, remaining 140g palm sugar, eggs, and a pinch of salt until well combined.
Coarsely chop 20g of Thai basil leaves. Stir chopped basil into the coconut milk mixture.
Pour the coconut milk mixture over the bread cubes. Gently toss to coat. Let soak for 10 minutes, pressing occasionally to ensure bread absorbs liquid.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the pudding is set and golden brown. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let the bread pudding cool completely in the dish. Once cool, cut into 6-9 uniform square or rectangular pieces.
Arrange pieces on a serving platter. Sprinkle each piece with the crispy garlic-chicken crumble. Garnish with a small fresh Thai basil leaf.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of rich, slow-simmered Classic Beef Ragu rests on a bed of wide, flat pappardelle pasta in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The ragu, a deep reddish-brown, is thick with finely diced beef, softened diced carrots, celery, and onions, all coated in a concentrated tomato sauce. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves is gently placed on top. The dish is presented on a worn, light wooden dining table, alongside a simple fork and a crumpled white linen napkin. A small bowl of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese sits nearby. The lighting is warm and natural, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The focus is on the hearty, comforting textures and inviting aroma of the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh pasta like pappardelle or tagliatelle.
Offer grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table.
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Dice onion, carrot, and celery into small cubes. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add beef mince. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and no pink remains. Drain excess fat. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic to the soffritto. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until wine is mostly evaporated.
Return browned beef to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Season with salt and black pepper.

Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 1.5 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until sauce is thick and flavors are well-developed. For richer flavor, simmer longer, up to 3 hours.
Just before serving, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most of the basil into the ragu. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve generous portions of ragu over cooked pasta. Garnish with remaining fresh basil.
notes: The longer the ragu simmers, the more developed and rich its flavors will become.
Adjust seasoning to taste throughout the cooking process.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto Cremoso al Pomodoro, Pancetta e Scamorza
recipes.visual_description: A modest, single portion of creamy, vibrant red-orange risotto is presented on a simple, rustic white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The risotto is free-flowing and naturally spread, showcasing its fluid consistency. Scattered generously over the top are golden-brown, crispy diced pancetta pieces, providing a textural contrast. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are casually placed on the risotto, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A simple, silver fork and spoon are casually placed beside the plate. A loosely folded, beige cloth napkin sits nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The background is minimal, hinting at a comfortable home setting with soft, natural shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a comforting main course.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano on the side for individual preference.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy and fat renders. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Toast the rice for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add tomato passata. Stir well to combine.
Begin adding hot vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to be almost absorbed before adding the next ladleful.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente. The risotto should be fluid, not dry.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter, grated scamorza, and Parmigiano Reggiano. Stir vigorously until cheese melts and risotto is creamy (mantecatura).
Stir in most of the crispy pancetta. Reserve some for garnish.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining crispy pancetta and fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure broth is hot before adding to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is key for creamy risotto.
Taste and adjust seasoning frequently.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, presented whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken has a crisp, well-developed crust and a tender appearance. Beside it, a neat arrangement of vibrant green roasted asparagus spears. A glossy, pale yellow lemon-herb pan sauce is elegantly spooned over the chicken and around the plate, showing specks of fresh green parsley. A fresh lemon wedge is placed to the side, and a small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the chicken. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, creating a clean, professional bistro atmosphere with a soft, unobtrusive background. The portion is a single, refined serving.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Trim woody ends from asparagus. Toss asparagus with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast asparagus for 10-12 minutes, or until tender-crisp.
While asparagus roasts, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and a crust forms.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
Reduce stock by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in cold butter, one cube at a time, until sauce is emulsified and glossy.
Stir in fresh lemon juice from one lemon and chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken breasts whole, alongside roasted asparagus. Spoon lemon-herb sauce generously over chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Coconut-Lemon Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of the creamy fruit salad is presented in a rustic, light-colored ceramic bowl. Whole, plump pitted cherries, some halved, are abundant, showcasing their deep ruby red hue. Interspersed are thin, translucent slices of red dates, adding a subtle warmth and chewiness. The fruits are gently coated in a pale yellow, velvety coconut-lemon cream, which glistens softly and pools invitingly at the bottom of the bowl. The textures are a delightful contrast of juicy fruit and smooth, rich cream. The bowl rests on a well-worn, natural wooden kitchen table, its surface showing character. A casually draped simple, off-white linen napkin sits beside the bowl. Soft, warm light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, inviting atmosphere typical of a homely family kitchen.
instructions: Pit the fresh cherries. Some can be halved for variety.
Pit the dried red dates. Slice them thinly.
Prepare a double boiler. In a heatproof bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, caster sugar, and lemon zest until pale and slightly thick.
Place the bowl over simmering water, ensuring the bottom does not touch the water. Continue whisking constantly.
Gradually whisk in the coconut cream and lemon juice.
Cook, whisking continuously, until the mixture thickens to a pourable custard consistency. It should coat the back of a spoon. Do not boil.
Remove the bowl from heat. Let the coconut-lemon cream cool completely, then chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
In a large bowl, gently combine the chilled coconut-lemon cream with the pitted cherries and sliced red dates.
Serve immediately in individual bowls.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Bread and Butter Pudding
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single portion of golden-brown bread and butter pudding served in a shallow white ceramic bowl. The brioche is cut into thick triangles, showing toasted, crisp edges and a soft, custard-soaked center. Plump, dark raisins are scattered throughout the layers. The surface is dusted with fine ground nutmeg and sparkling grains of demerara sugar. The pudding has a slight wobble, indicating a creamy, set custard texture. It sits on a rustic oak table with a simple linen napkin. A small silver spoon rests beside the bowl. Soft, warm kitchen lighting highlights the contrast between the crunchy bread peaks and the silky, pale yellow custard interior.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a side of chilled heavy cream
Accompany with a pot of English breakfast tea
Top with a spoonful of warm vanilla custard
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Grease a 1-liter baking dish with butter.
Spread softened butter on both sides of bread slices.
Cut bread into thick triangles.
Layer bread triangles in the dish.
Scatter raisins between the bread layers.
Whisk milk, cream, eggs, caster sugar, and vanilla in a bowl.
Pour the custard mixture over the bread.
Press bread down gently to submerge.
Let soak for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Sprinkle ground nutmeg and demerara sugar on top.
Bake for 35 minutes until the top is golden brown.
Ensure the custard is set with a slight wobble.
notes: Use stale bread for better custard absorption.
Do not overbake to keep the custard center creamy.
Substitute raisins with chocolate chips for a modern twist.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb, Mango & Coconut Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine slice of a multi-layered entremet stands elegantly on a round, white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The slice reveals distinct, clean horizontal layers: a golden-brown coconut dacquoise base, topped by a creamy, pale green kaffir lime and coconut mousse. Embedded within the mousse is a vibrant, translucent yellow mango and passion fruit gelee, which itself contains tiny, glistening dark amber cubes of candied lamb. The entire entremet is encased in a smooth, reflective white chocolate and coconut mirror glaze. The colors are sophisticated and harmonious: soft white, pale green, bright yellow, and deep amber. The textures are varied, promising a delightful mouthfeel. Garnishes are minimal and precise: a few fresh mango micro-cubes and a scattering of toasted coconut flakes are artfully placed on the plate beside the slice. The plate rests on a pristine white marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts soft shadows, enhancing the dessert's architectural precision. An ultra-minimalist background ensures maximum negative space, highlighting the culinary mastery.
instructions: Prepare Candied Lamb Insert: Dice lamb loin into 0.5cm cubes. Combine coconut water, 50g palm sugar, tamarind, star anise, cinnamon, ginger, and fish sauce in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add lamb. Braise gently for 1.5 hours until lamb is fork-tender. Remove lamb. Reduce liquid until syrupy. Toss lamb cubes in reduced syrup until coated and slightly caramelized. Spread on parchment paper to cool. Freeze in a 14cm ring for later assembly.

Prepare Coconut Dacquoise: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Whip egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add 70g granulated sugar, whip to stiff, glossy peaks. Gently fold in almond flour and desiccated coconut. Spread batter evenly in a 16cm circle on parchment. Bake 15-18 minutes until golden. Cool completely. Trim to fit a 16cm entremet ring.

Prepare Mango-Passion Fruit Gelee: Bloom 2g gelatin in cold water. Heat mango puree, passion fruit puree, and remaining 50g palm sugar until sugar dissolves. Squeeze excess water from gelatin; stir into warm puree until dissolved. Pour gelee over the frozen candied lamb insert. Freeze until firm.

Prepare Kaffir Lime & Coconut Mousse: Bloom 4g gelatin in cold water. Gently warm coconut cream with kaffir lime leaves (bruised) for 10 minutes; do not boil. Remove leaves. In a bowl, whisk egg yolks with a spoonful of warm coconut cream, then slowly whisk back into remaining warm cream. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened (nappe consistency). Squeeze excess water from gelatin; stir into warm custard until dissolved. Cool custard to 25°C. Gently fold in whipped cream.

Assemble Entremet: Place coconut dacquoise at the bottom of a 16cm entremet ring lined with acetate. Pour half of the Kaffir Lime & Coconut Mousse over the dacquoise. Gently place the frozen Mango-Passion Fruit Gelee with Candied Lamb insert on top, centered. Pour remaining mousse over the insert, smoothing the top. Freeze for at least 6 hours or overnight until solid.

Prepare White Chocolate & Coconut Mirror Glaze: Bloom remaining 2g gelatin. Combine white chocolate, glucose syrup, and condensed milk in a heatproof bowl. In a separate saucepan, heat coconut milk to a simmer. Pour hot coconut milk over chocolate mixture. Let sit 1 minute, then stir until smooth. Squeeze excess water from gelatin; stir into glaze until dissolved. Blend with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool glaze to 32-35°C.

Glaze & Garnish: Remove frozen entremet from ring and acetate. Place on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Pour glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip. Carefully transfer cake to a serving plate. Garnish with a few delicate fresh mango micro-cubes and a whisper of toasted coconut flakes.
Serve: Allow entremet to thaw in the refrigerator for at least 2-3 hours before serving for optimal texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb Consommé with Confit Lamb Belly and Chive Oil
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, deep white bone china soup bowl holds a single portion of crystal-clear, amber-golden lamb consommé. In the precise center, four to five perfectly cubed pieces of confit lamb belly are meticulously arranged. Each lamb cube is deep golden-brown, showcasing a crisp exterior and tender interior. A vibrant green chive oil is artfully drizzled in a few precise drops around the lamb, contrasting elegantly with the consommé. Delicate sprigs of bright green micro-chives are placed with architectural precision atop the lamb, adding freshness. The bowl rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, surrounded by abundant negative space. A crisp white linen napkin, folded precisely, sits nearby. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's refined simplicity and elegance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small, warm artisan bread roll.
Offer a fine, aged sherry as an accompaniment.

ingredients.name: lamb belly, skin on, cut into 4 portions

instructions: Prepare Lamb Stock: Place roasted lamb bones, carrots, celery, onion, water, peppercorns, bay leaves, and thyme in a large pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim any impurities from the surface. Simmer gently for 4-6 hours. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool completely. Refrigerate overnight. Remove any solidified fat from the surface.

Clarify Consommé: In a large pot, combine cold lamb stock with lamb mince, egg whites, diced carrot, celery, and onion. Whisk gently to combine. Place pot over medium heat. Stir constantly until raft forms and stock is hot but not boiling. Stop stirring. Create a small hole in the raft for steam to escape. Simmer very gently for 45-60 minutes, without disturbing the raft. The consommé should be crystal clear.

Strain Consommé: Carefully ladle the clear consommé through the hole in the raft into a separate bowl, passing it through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Do not press the raft. Season consommé with salt to taste. Keep warm.

Prepare Confit Lamb Belly: Preheat oven to 140°C. Season lamb belly portions generously with salt and pepper. Place lamb belly, duck fat, rosemary, and garlic in an ovenproof dish. Ensure lamb is submerged in fat. Cover dish tightly. Confit in the oven for 2.5-3 hours, or until very tender.

Crisp Confit Lamb Belly: Carefully remove lamb belly from duck fat. Let cool slightly. Cut each portion into small, precise 1.5 cm cubes. In a non-stick pan, sear lamb belly cubes over medium-high heat until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels.

Prepare Chive Oil: Blanch chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched chives with neutral oil and a pinch of salt until smooth and vibrant green. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter for a clear oil.

Plate and Serve: Ladle hot consommé into deep, warm soup bowls. Arrange 4-5 crispy confit lamb belly cubes precisely in the center of each bowl. Drizzle a few drops or a small swirl of chive oil around the lamb. Garnish with delicate micro-chives or micro-parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Achieving a truly clear consommé requires patience and careful temperature control during clarification.
The confit lamb belly can be prepared in advance and crisped just before serving.
Ensure all components are hot when serving to maintain optimal flavor and temperature.
traditional_techniques: Blanching and shocking for herb oil

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Roasted Butternut Squash Puree and Apple-Mustard Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef medallions is artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick, perfectly seared beef medallions, boasting a rich brown crust and a tender, medium-rare interior, are positioned prominently. Beside the beef, a vibrant orange, smooth butternut squash puree is elegantly dolloped or swiped across the plate. A glossy, rich brown apple-mustard jus is drizzled over the beef and subtly around the plate, creating a professional and appealing finish. Fresh green thyme sprigs are used as a simple, aromatic garnish. The composition maintains moderate negative space, ensuring the dish is the clear focal point. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a crisp white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting and refined presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel butternut squash. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and caramelized. Set aside.
While squash roasts, prepare beef. Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add beef medallions. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Remove beef from pan. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced shallots to the pan. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Deglaze the pan with beef stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Add diced apple and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, reducing the sauce by half. Stir in 30g butter until melted and incorporated. Season jus with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.

Transfer roasted squash to a food processor or blender. Add remaining 30g butter and 2 sprigs of fresh thyme leaves. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add a splash of hot water if needed for desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate, spoon a generous portion of butternut squash puree onto each white porcelain plate. Place two beef medallions beside the puree. Drizzle apple-mustard jus over the beef and around the plate. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Caramelized Onion Bruschetta
recipes.visual_description: The Beef and Caramelized Onion Bruschetta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. Each piece of toasted baguette is golden brown, topped generously with glistening, deep amber caramelized red onions. Small, seared beef medallions, showcasing a rich brown crust and tender pink interior, are placed atop the onions. Fresh green thyme leaves are delicately sprinkled for a vibrant color contrast. The arrangement is organic yet composed, with each bruschetta piece clearly defined. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the visual appeal of the elevated finger food. A simple white cotton napkin rests beside the plate, maintaining a casual, inviting bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Slice red onions thinly. Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions.
Cook onions slowly for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender, stirring occasionally. Add balsamic vinegar during the last 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from pan.
Pat beef tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in the same pan over high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef tenderloin for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Remove beef from pan. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Toast baguette slices in a toaster or oven until golden brown. Rub one side of each toasted slice with the cut garlic clove.
Slice rested beef into small, 1 cm thick medallions or small chunks.
Assemble bruschetta: Spoon caramelized onions onto each garlic-rubbed baguette slice. Top with 1-2 beef medallions or chunks. Garnish with small fresh thyme leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Asparagus & Fermented Garlic Pasta Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Asparagus & Fermented Garlic Pasta Salad is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a muted beige tone, showcasing a minimalistic and natural aesthetic. Short pasta, likely fusilli or orecchiette, is loosely mixed with vibrant green, tender-crisp asparagus pieces, cut into 2 cm lengths. The pasta and asparagus are lightly coated in a translucent dressing, hinting at the presence of finely minced fermented garlic. A scattering of fresh dill sprigs and a few toasted pumpkin seeds add subtle color and texture. The composition respects negative space, allowing each ingredient to be appreciated. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its organic beauty. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery, reinforcing an eco-conscious, ingredient-focused presentation.
instructions: Cook pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain. Rinse with cold water to cool. Drain thoroughly.
Trim woody ends from asparagus. Cut asparagus into 2 cm pieces.
Blanch asparagus pieces in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well.
Finely mince fermented garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, whisk together minced fermented garlic, olive oil, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cooled pasta and blanched asparagus to the bowl. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Fold in chopped fresh dill.
Serve immediately or chill. Garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds if desired.
notes: This salad celebrates seasonality and the unique depth of flavor from fermented ingredients. The blanching water from asparagus can be saved and used as a base for vegetable broth, minimizing waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken & Rice Croquettes with Gochujang Aioli
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-brown, uniformly cylindrical croquettes, each about 5 cm long, arranged invitingly on a clean white porcelain sharing platter. Their crispy, textured exterior hints at a tender, savory interior. A small, pristine white ramekin holds a vibrant, glossy red-orange gochujang aioli, strategically placed for dipping. The croquettes are garnished with finely sliced bright green scallions and a delicate sprinkle of black sesame seeds, adding color contrast and visual interest. Moderate negative space surrounds the elements, creating a balanced and professional composition. The platter rests on a simple light wooden table, with a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin beside it. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimal and subtly blurred, suggesting a casual, refined bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve these croquettes on a large communal platter for sharing, encouraging a relaxed, family-style dining experience.
Provide small individual plates and chopsticks or small forks for guests to serve themselves.
instructions: Boil chicken breast until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove and shred finely.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, cooled rice, 30g gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Form the mixture into 16 uniform cylindrical croquettes, approximately 5 cm long and 2 cm thick.
Set up a breading station: one plate with flour, one bowl with beaten eggs, and one plate with panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge each croquette in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, then roll in panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to ensure full coverage.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 170°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Remove fried croquettes with a slotted spoon and place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
For the gochujang aioli, combine mayonnaise, remaining 30g gochujang, and rice vinegar in a small bowl. Whisk until smooth.
Arrange the hot croquettes on a serving platter. Serve immediately with the gochujang aioli for dipping. Garnish with sliced green onions and black sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Orchard Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of Fermented Orchard Fruit Salad is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a creamy beige hue, set on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. The plate features ample white space, highlighting the natural beauty of the ingredients. Rustic 2 cm wedges of light-colored pear, some with their natural skin intact, are artfully arranged alongside plump, deep ruby-red fermented cherries. A glossy, dark amber molasses-cinnamon syrup is drizzled sparingly over the fruits, creating subtle glistening pools. Scattered lightly over the fruit are golden-brown toasted coconut flakes, adding a textural contrast. A few vibrant green, foraged mint leaves provide a fresh, natural accent. The composition is clean, minimalistic, and unforced, emphasizing the pure forms and colors of the fruit. The setting is illuminated by soft, natural light, with an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone subtly placed beside the plate. The background is clean and simple, with a hint of natural plant foliage providing an organic touch, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Fresh Mint or Lemon Balm leaves (optional, foraged)

instructions: Prepare fermented cherries: Wash cherries. Pit cherries carefully. Place pitted cherries into a clean glass jar.

Make brine: Dissolve sea salt in 250 ml filtered water. Pour brine over cherries in the jar. Ensure cherries are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small clean bag filled with water to keep cherries under brine.

Ferment cherries: Seal jar loosely. Store at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Check daily for small bubbles. Taste after 3 days; they should be tangy and slightly fizzy. Once desired tanginess is reached, refrigerate.

Prepare molasses-cinnamon syrup: Combine 60 ml molasses, 60 ml filtered water, and cinnamon stick in a small saucepan. Heat gently over low heat, stirring until molasses dissolves. Simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cinnamon stick steep in syrup as it cools. Remove cinnamon stick before serving.
Prepare pears: Wash pears. Do not peel if organic. Core pears. Cut pears into rustic 2 cm wedges or chunks.
Toast coconut flakes: Spread coconut flakes on a dry pan. Toast over medium-low heat until lightly golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Assemble salad: In a bowl, gently combine pear wedges and fermented cherries. Drizzle with cooled molasses-cinnamon syrup. Toss lightly to coat.
Serve: Divide fruit salad among four individual plates. Garnish with a few fresh mint or lemon balm leaves, if using. Sprinkle toasted coconut flakes over each serving.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Mustard Chicken and Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of One-Pot Mustard Chicken and Rice Pilaf rests on a simple, round, cream-colored ceramic plate. The dish features a golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, skin-on and bone-in, positioned slightly off-center. The rice pilaf, cooked to a tender, slightly moist consistency, forms a natural bed around the chicken. Diced carrots and onions are visibly mixed throughout the rice, adding pops of orange and white. A light dusting of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a fresh, aromatic contrast. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting. A standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate on a simple cloth napkin. The overall presentation is inviting, warm, and comforting, typical of a home-cooked family meal.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip the chicken and sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the rice until each grain is coated with the pan drippings. Pour in the chicken broth and Dijon mustard. Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits.
Bring the mixture to a boil. Carefully return the seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly with a lid. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the rice is tender and all liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove the pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Serve hot. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Roasted Vegetable Pasta Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Bell Pepper and Roasted Vegetable Pasta Salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Penne pasta, a neutral base, is interspersed with vibrant, diced roasted red and yellow bell peppers, tender half-moon zucchini slices, and halved cherry tomatoes, all slightly caramelized at the edges. Thinly sliced red onion adds a subtle purple hue. The salad is generously coated in a glossy, light-golden mustard vinaigrette, which clings to each component. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is organic yet balanced, showcasing the diverse textures and colors of the roasted vegetables. The plate is centered on a simple light wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it, under soft, natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's freshness and visual appeal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine diced bell peppers, sliced zucchini, thinly sliced red onion, and halved cherry tomatoes. Add 2 tablespoons of olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on the prepared baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool slightly.
Cook penne pasta according to package instructions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to stop cooking. Set aside.

While vegetables roast, prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together remaining olive oil, Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, dried oregano, dried basil, salt, and black pepper until emulsified.
In a large serving bowl, combine the cooled roasted vegetables and cooked pasta. Pour the dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Serve chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Asparagus Quinoa Salad with Lemon-Herb Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The Asparagus Quinoa Salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, set on a simple wooden table. Roasted asparagus pieces are artfully distributed among fluffy golden quinoa. Halved red cherry tomatoes, diced green cucumber, thinly sliced purple red onion, crumbled white feta, and dark Kalamata olive slices add vibrant color and varied textures. The salad is lightly coated with a glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette, reflecting natural light. Fresh chopped parsley and mint are sprinkled throughout, providing a final touch of green. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. Standard restaurant flatware and a folded cotton napkin rest beside the plate, completing a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty artisan bread.
Offer a side of hummus or tzatziki.
instructions: Rinse quinoa under cold water. Combine quinoa and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Trim woody ends from asparagus. Toss asparagus with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.

While quinoa cooks, prepare dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Slowly drizzle in 65 ml olive oil, whisking constantly until emulsified.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice half a red onion. Crumble feta cheese. Slice pitted Kalamata olives. Coarsely chop fresh parsley and mint.
In a large bowl, combine cooked quinoa, roasted asparagus (cut into 3 cm pieces), halved cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, sliced red onion, crumbled feta, and sliced Kalamata olives.
Pour lemon-herb vinaigrette over the salad. Add chopped parsley and mint. Gently toss to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately or chill for flavors to meld. Garnish with additional fresh herbs or a lemon wedge if desired.
notes: Ensure quinoa is fully fluffed and cooled slightly before mixing to prevent wilting other ingredients.
Adjust amount of red onion based on preference for pungency.
For best flavor, let the salad sit for at least 15 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Oatmeal and Apple Fritters with Creamy Egg White Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Two golden-brown, round Savory Oatmeal and Apple Fritters are neatly stacked off-center on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The fritters have a slightly irregular, rustic edge, showcasing the texture of the oats and small, soft-cooked apple pieces within. A generous pool of creamy, pale ivory sauce, subtly aerated from the incorporated egg whites, rests beside and beneath the fritters. The sauce has a smooth, rich consistency, contrasting with the crisp exterior of the fritters. A light sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped chives garnishes the top of the fritters and the sauce, adding a fresh color pop. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional yet approachable presentation in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Sauté minced shallot and garlic in a little olive oil over medium heat until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add rolled oats, vegetable broth, and cinnamon to the pan. Cook, stirring, until liquid is absorbed and oats are slightly tender, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Transfer the oat mixture to a large bowl. Add finely diced apple, all-purpose flour, baking powder, 2 egg whites, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly to combine.
Heat a thin layer of olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Form the oat mixture into 8-10 small patties (approximately 7-8 cm diameter).
Cook fritters for 4-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain on paper towels.
For the sauce, gently heat heavy cream in a small saucepan over low heat. Do not boil.
Stir in the mashed banana until well combined. Season with a pinch of salt.

In a separate bowl, whisk the remaining 2 egg whites until frothy. Gently fold the frothy egg whites into the warm cream-banana mixture. Stir gently until just combined. Do not cook further or boil the sauce.
To serve, arrange 2-3 fritters per plate. Spoon the creamy egg white sauce generously over and around the fritters. Garnish with fresh chopped chives.
notes: Ensure fritters are cooked through to a minimum internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Adjust sauce consistency with a little more cream or broth if too thick, or reduce slightly if too thin.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut-Crusted Crab Cakes with Pineapple-Lemon Salsa
recipes.visual_description: Two golden-brown, coconut-crusted crab cakes are neatly arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The crab cakes are round and plump, exhibiting a crisp, textured surface from the toasted coconut and panko. Adjacent to the crab cakes, a vibrant, chunky pineapple-lemon salsa is artfully spooned. The salsa bursts with color from diced yellow pineapple, crimson red onion, and bright red bell pepper, providing a fresh contrast. A small sprig of fresh cilantro or a delicate lemon wedge garnishes the plate, adding a touch of verdant green. The composition allows for moderate negative space, emphasizing the dish. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm, inviting ambiance. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the food while hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Gently flake crab meat into a large bowl. Remove any shell fragments.
Add 50 g panko breadcrumbs, egg, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, lemon zest, and parsley to the crab. Season with salt and black pepper.
Mix ingredients gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into 8 equal patties, about 2 cm thick.
Combine remaining 50 g panko breadcrumbs and shredded coconut in a shallow dish.
Dredge each crab cake in the panko-coconut mixture, pressing gently to coat evenly.
Place coated crab cakes on a plate. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to firm up.
For the salsa, combine diced pineapple, diced red onion, diced red bell pepper, minced jalapeño (if using), and lemon juice in a medium bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Cook crab cakes for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through.
Serve 2 crab cakes per plate. Top with a generous spoonful of pineapple-lemon salsa.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Salmon and Caviar Pasta Bites
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white Carrara marble slab serves as the elegant base for 10 perfectly formed canapés. Each small, al dente conchigliette pasta shell is meticulously filled with a smooth, pale pink smoked salmon mousse. Perched atop the creamy mousse is a glistening mound of premium black Osetra caviar, its dark pearls contrasting exquisitely with the salmon. A single vibrant green micro dill sprig is precisely placed on each caviar mound. The arrangement is organic and flowing, with ample negative space. Dramatic, focused lighting casts subtle shadows, highlighting the delicate textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the culinary artistry and luxury of the ingredients.
instructions: Cook pasta shells al dente. Drain well. Cool completely on a tray.
Combine smoked salmon, cream cheese, fresh dill, lemon zest, salt, and white pepper in a food processor. Process until smooth and creamy. Do not overmix.
Transfer the smoked salmon mousse to a piping bag fitted with a small, round tip.
Carefully pipe the mousse into each cooled pasta shell, filling it completely.
Arrange 8-12 filled pasta shells artfully on a large serving platter, ensuring ample negative space.
Top each filled shell with a small, precise spoon of caviar.
Garnish each canapé with a single sprig of micro dill or a small segment of chive.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Basil Relish and White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is centered on a round, matte off-white handcrafted ceramic plate. The chicken, a golden-brown breast or thigh piece, is presented whole, showcasing its seared crust. Beside the chicken, a generous dollop of creamy white bean puree or lightly mashed whole beans provides a soft, contrasting texture. A spoonful of vibrant, chunky fermented tomato-basil relish, showcasing its rich red and green hues, is artfully placed atop the chicken or nestled beside it. A few delicate, thin onion crisps are gently leaned against the chicken, adding height and a crisp texture. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered naturally on and around the dish. The plate rests on a light-colored reclaimed wood table surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a blurred natural green plant subtly visible, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato-Basil Relish: Roughly dice tomatoes. Combine with 10g sea salt and a few torn basil leaves in a clean jar. Cover with filtered water, ensuring tomatoes are submerged. Seal loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Once fermented, drain most liquid. Roughly chop fermented tomatoes. Stir in remaining fresh basil, a pinch of sugar, and a drizzle of olive oil. Set aside.

Prepare White Beans: Dice half the onion. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan. Sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened. Add drained white beans and 250ml vegetable stock. Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, until beans are heated through and liquid slightly reduced. Season with salt and pepper. Mash lightly with a fork for a creamier texture or leave mostly whole.

Prepare Onion Crisps: Thinly slice remaining half onion, including root ends and outer layers. Mince remaining garlic clove. Heat 30ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add sliced onion and minced garlic. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and crisp. This may take 15-20 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Season with a pinch of salt.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken pieces for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Place a serving of white beans onto a matte off-white ceramic plate. Arrange one whole seared chicken piece beside or on top of the beans.
