recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, coated in a vibrant green matcha-infused Panko crust, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented whole, showcasing its golden-brown crisp exterior and the distinct green hue. A creamy, pale ivory licorice-infused sauce is artfully spooned beneath and around the chicken. Alongside, blanched asparagus spears provide a contrasting fresh green. A delicate dusting of finely crushed 'Rainbow Dust' (100s and 1000s) is lightly scattered over the chicken and sauce, adding subtle pops of color without overwhelming the dish. A scattering of finely chopped chives garnishes the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating a refined yet approachable presentation. The entire plate is visible, with balanced negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up dredging stations: one plate with flour, one bowl with beaten egg, one plate with Panko mixed with matcha powder.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in matcha-Panko mixture. Press to adhere.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.

While chicken bakes, prepare sauce: In a small saucepan, combine cream cheese, chicken stock, and licorice root powder. Heat over medium-low heat, whisking until smooth and thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Blanch asparagus spears in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain.
Finely crush 100s and 1000s into a powder for the 'Rainbow Dust'.

To plate, spoon a pool of licorice cream sauce onto each plate. Place a pan-seared matcha chicken breast on top. Arrange asparagus spears beside the chicken. Lightly sprinkle the 'Rainbow Dust' over the chicken and sauce. Garnish with fresh chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Rib, Porcini Risotto, Confit Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single braised beef short rib, rich mahogany-brown and glistening, rests elegantly beside a pool of creamy, pale tan porcini risotto. The risotto is fluid, not mounded, with visible flecks of dark porcini. Scattered around are ruby-red confit cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly wrinkled, offering a burst of color. A vibrant green basil oil is artfully drizzled in organic lines across the plate, creating subtle contrast. The dish is presented on a round, matte white bone china plate with a delicate raised rim. The plate sits on a polished grey marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is placed to the side. The scene is lit with dramatic, soft professional lighting, casting gentle shadows that enhance texture and depth. The background is ultra-minimalist, creating abundant negative space to highlight the culinary artistry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of robust red wine, such as Barolo or Chianti Classico.
Offer freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette can accompany the rich dish.

ingredients.name: Beef Short Rib
ingredients.quantity: 1.2 kg, bone-in, cut into 4 large pieces

instructions: Season beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper. Sear in a heavy-bottomed pot with 30ml olive oil until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef.

Add 1 finely diced shallot and 1 minced garlic clove to the pot. Sauté until softened. Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Return beef to pot. Pour hot beef broth over ribs until almost covered. Bring to a simmer. Cover and braise in oven at 150°C for 3-4 hours, or until fork-tender.
Rehydrate dried porcini mushrooms in 250ml hot water for 20 minutes. Strain liquid, reserving it. Chop rehydrated porcini.

Preheat oven to 120°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with 2 thinly sliced garlic cloves, 30ml olive oil, pinch of salt, and chili flakes (if using). Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 45-60 minutes until softened and slightly shriveled.
In a separate pot, sauté remaining diced shallot and 1 minced garlic clove in 20ml olive oil until translucent. Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.

Pour in reserved porcini liquid. Stir until absorbed. Begin adding hot beef broth (from the braise, strained, or fresh) one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each ladle to be almost absorbed before adding the next. After 10 minutes, add chopped rehydrated porcini. Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, until rice is al dente and creamy.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.

Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with 50ml olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for clear oil.

Gently remove short ribs from braising liquid. Spoon a generous portion of risotto onto each plate. Place a braised short rib piece beside or on top of the risotto. Arrange confit cherry tomatoes around the dish. Drizzle basil oil artfully over the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken with Creamy Polenta and Bell Pepper Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared chicken breast, sliced into two thick, clean medallions, rests gracefully atop a creamy, golden pool of slow-cooked polenta. Beside the chicken, a vibrant, artfully composed cluster of roasted red bell pepper and burst cherry tomato pomodoro adds a contrasting splash of color and texture. The bell peppers are finely diced, and the tomatoes are halved, retaining their natural shape. A few delicate, fresh basil leaves are strategically placed for verdant accents. A small, precisely torn piece of fresh mozzarella melts slightly into the warm polenta, adding a subtle creamy note. The dish is presented on an elegant, matte white designer plate, with ample negative space. The setting features a polished grey marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle, and traditional silver flatware. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and rich colors against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a glass of dry white Italian wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer crusty artisanal bread on the side for dipping into the polenta and pomodoro.

ingredients.name: Fresh mozzarella, torn into small pieces

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve bell peppers, remove seeds. Place cut-side down on baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until skin is blistered. Transfer to bowl, cover tightly. Let steam for 10 minutes. Peel skins, finely dice roasted bell peppers. Set aside.

Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in large, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake 10-12 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, rest 5 minutes. Slice each breast into two thick medallions.

While chicken bakes, prepare polenta. Bring chicken stock to a gentle simmer in a large saucepan. Slowly whisk in fine-grain polenta, ensuring no lumps. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 25-30 minutes until polenta is creamy and smooth. Stir in butter and Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For bell pepper pomodoro, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Sauté diced shallot 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add halved cherry tomatoes and diced roasted bell peppers. Cook 5-7 minutes, gently mashing some tomatoes, until tomatoes burst and sauce thickens slightly. Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves, reserving a few for garnish. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate, spoon a generous pool of creamy polenta onto the center of each elegant plate. Arrange two thick-cut chicken medallions artfully on top of the polenta. Place a vibrant cluster of bell pepper pomodoro beside the chicken. Scatter a few small, precisely torn pieces of fresh mozzarella over the polenta and chicken. Garnish with reserved fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For the creamiest polenta, use fine-grain polenta and stir frequently during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Pork with Creamy Cheddar Grits
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Beer-Braised Pork with Creamy Cheddar Grits is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The base features a generous mound of golden-yellow, creamy cheddar grits, smooth and inviting. Nestled atop the grits are two to three substantial, fork-tender 5 cm chunks of deep mahogany, beer-braised pork. A rich, glossy braising liquid pools around the pork and over the grits. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley and golden-brown crispy diced bacon. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, conveying a warm, casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat pork chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot. Set aside.
Add diced bacon to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon. Leave rendered fat.
Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return pork to the pot. Add chicken stock. Liquid should mostly cover pork.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While pork simmers, prepare grits. Bring water to a boil in a separate saucepan. Slowly whisk in grits.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until grits are creamy and thick, about 10-15 minutes. Add more water if needed.
Stir shredded cheddar cheese, heavy cream, and butter into grits until melted and smooth. Season with salt.
Taste braising liquid. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Spoon creamy cheddar grits onto clean white porcelain dinner plates. Arrange braised pork chunks over grits.
Spoon rich braising liquid over pork and grits. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and crispy bacon bits.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Salami & White Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Salami & White Bean Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, perhaps in an earthy terracotta tone. The stew fills the bowl, showcasing thick chunks of browned salami, soft, diced carrots, and tender white beans in a rich, rustic red tomato broth. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast to the deep red and brown hues. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Alongside, a simple, torn piece of crusty Italian bread sits directly on the table. A casually placed, folded linen napkin completes the setting. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer grated Pecorino Romano cheese for sprinkling.

ingredients.name: Canned White Beans (Cannellini or Butter Beans)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add salami chunks. Cook until lightly browned and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Remove salami with a slotted spoon; set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add diced onions and diced carrots to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chopped tomatoes and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add drained and rinsed white beans. Return salami to the pot.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Stir occasionally.
Season with fresh black pepper and salt to taste. Salami adds significant salt, so taste before adding more.
Ladle hot stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Sun-Dried Tomato, and Spinach Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Creamy Chicken, Sun-Dried Tomato, and Spinach Pasta is served on a round, off-white ceramic plate. The pasta, coated in a rich, pale orange-hued creamy sauce, forms a comforting, unpretentious mound. Golden-brown, irregularly shaped chicken chunks, visibly seared, are nestled within. Bright green, wilted spinach leaves are scattered throughout, contrasting with deep red, roughly chopped sun-dried tomato pieces. Components are naturally overlapping, showcasing the dish's hearty texture. A light sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh parsley adds a final touch. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and standard metal fork rest beside it. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic to the same pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add spinach to the pan. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Add cooked pasta.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and reserved pasta water. Toss to combine. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly and coats pasta.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sheet Pan Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sheet Pan Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh sits prominently, with several golden-brown potato wedges arranged naturally around it. Thick-cut, caramelized red onion wedges and a few roasted whole garlic cloves are nestled among the potatoes. A few fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs are casually placed on top for garnish. The components touch and overlap slightly, creating a hearty, comforting presentation. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the roasted ingredients. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the food. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread to soak up pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash and pat chicken thighs dry. Season with half the salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2.5 cm wedges.
Peel and cut red onion into thick wedges.
Peel garlic cloves. Leave whole.
In a large bowl, toss potato wedges, onion wedges, and whole garlic cloves with olive oil, remaining salt, and pepper.
Add rosemary and thyme sprigs to the potato mixture. Toss to combine.
Spread potato mixture in a single layer on a large sheet pan.
Place seasoned chicken thighs on top of the vegetables.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken and vegetables. Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy.
Check internal temperature of chicken. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Pistachio Tatsoi Bites
recipes.visual_description: The Crispy Pistachio Tatsoi Bites are arranged casually on a rustic ceramic platter or a simple wooden board. Each tatsoi leaf, either whole or halved if very large, is coated in a golden-brown, textured crust of roughly chopped pistachios and panko breadcrumbs. Flecks of vibrant green parsley and crimson red pepper flakes are visible within the crust, contrasting with the dark green edges of the tatsoi leaves. The leaves are crisp and slightly curled from baking, showing a delicate crunch. Some pieces may overlap naturally, creating a generous, inviting pile. A small, simple ceramic bowl of a creamy vegan dip or a few lemon wedges are scattered for brightness. The setting is a well-used wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, natural light. Everyday ceramic plates with subtle imperfections are ready for serving. A casually draped cloth napkin completes the unpretentious, homely atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Roughly chop shelled pistachios. Finely chop fresh parsley.
In a shallow bowl, combine chopped pistachios, panko breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Lightly brush each tatsoi leaf on both sides with Dijon mustard.
Press each mustard-coated tatsoi leaf into the breadcrumb mixture. Ensure it is well coated.
Arrange coated tatsoi leaves in a single layer on the prepared baking tray. Do not overcrowd.
Drizzle the coated tatsoi leaves lightly with olive oil.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the coating is golden brown and crispy.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot and Pea Salad with Sous Vide Beef Tenderloin
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine white bone china plate, showcasing abundant negative space. A vibrant green swoosh of velvety pea puree anchors the composition. Artfully arranged alongside are 3-4 glazed baby carrots, some whole, some halved lengthwise, in varying hues of orange and purple. Two to three perfectly seared, small chunks of sous vide beef tenderloin, exhibiting a rich brown crust and tender pink interior, are strategically placed among the vegetables. A delicate cluster of fresh watercress and pea shoots, lightly dressed, adds height and a touch of vibrant green. The minimalist plating emphasizes natural, organic lines. A single sprig of micro-chervil precisely garnishes the beef. The setting features a luxurious, light-colored marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded precisely, and dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, highlighting the dish as the sole focal point.
instructions: Season beef tenderloin with salt, pepper, and fresh thyme sprigs. Vacuum seal the beef.
Cook beef in a sous vide water bath at 54°C for 2 hours.
Blanch fresh peas in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain immediately. Transfer peas to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Blend blanched peas with a splash of water until very smooth. Season with salt. Pass the puree through a fine-mesh sieve for a velvety texture.
Peel baby carrots. In a pan, melt butter. Add carrots, vegetable broth, and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer until carrots are tender and the liquid reduces to a glossy glaze.

For the vinaigrette, finely mince the shallot. In a small bowl, whisk shallot with white wine vinegar. Slowly drizzle in extra virgin olive oil while whisking continuously until emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove beef from the sous vide bag. Pat dry thoroughly. Sear quickly in a very hot pan with a small amount of oil for about 1 minute per side until a golden crust forms. Rest the beef for 5 minutes.
Cut the rested beef tenderloin into small, precise chunks.
To assemble, create a swoosh or dollop of pea puree on each plate. Artfully arrange 3-4 glazed baby carrots, some whole, some halved lengthwise, beside the puree.
Place 2-3 small beef chunks precisely among the vegetables. Lightly dress watercress and pea shoots with the vinaigrette.
Delicately arrange the dressed greens around the main components. Garnish with a single sprig of micro-chervil.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Garlic-Thyme Mushrooms and Sautéed Swiss Chard
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef is centrally plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The beef, presented as thick chunks, features a deep brown, seared crust with a visible tender pink interior. A rich, glossy mushroom-thyme sauce is generously spooned beneath and over the beef, showcasing sliced cremini mushrooms, small diced onions, and fresh thyme leaves. Beside the beef, a vibrant green mound of sautéed swiss chard sits neatly, showing its roughly chopped leaves and flecks of minced garlic. Fresh basil leaves are scattered over the beef and chard, adding a pop of bright green. The plate has appropriate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table surface with a casually placed cotton napkin and standard polished flatware, all under natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust cooking time for desired doneness.
Remove beef from skillet. Place on a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Add butter to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince 3 garlic cloves. Add minced garlic and leaves from 3 thyme sprigs to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly reduces and thickens, about 3-5 minutes. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Wash swiss chard thoroughly. Remove tough stems. Roughly chop the leaves.
In a separate pan, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Mince remaining 1 garlic clove. Add minced garlic to the pan and cook for 30 seconds.
Add chopped swiss chard to the pan. Sauté until wilted, about 3-5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested beef into thick chunks, if desired, or keep as medallions.
Plate beef chunks or medallions. Spoon mushroom-thyme sauce generously over the beef. Place sautéed swiss chard neatly beside the beef.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves and remaining fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Valrhona Guanaja Chocolate Soil, Blood Orange Gel, Aerated White Chocolate
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated, minimalist dessert presented on a large, pristine white bone china platter or a light grey veined marble surface. The composition features abundant negative space, allowing each element to stand out with architectural precision. At the base, dark, crumbly Valrhona Guanaja chocolate soil is scattered organically, creating a rich, earthy texture. Interspersed are small, abstract drops of vibrant, glossy blood orange gel, providing a stark color contrast and a subtle 'bloody' accent. Delicate, irregular cloud-like pieces of aerated white chocolate are strategically placed, their airy, porous texture offering a visual lightness. A single, perfectly preserved crystallized violet adorns each serving portion, adding a refined touch of color and a subtle floral note. The overall presentation is clean, elegant, and artfully composed, emphasizing textures, subtle color contrasts, and masterful execution of each component. Professional lighting creates dramatic shadows, enhancing the depth and visual intrigue of the dish.
instructions: For the Valrhona Guanaja Chocolate Soil: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Melt dark chocolate and butter together gently over a bain-marie or in a microwave. Stir until smooth.
In a separate bowl, combine almond flour, cocoa powder, and sea salt.
Pour melted chocolate mixture into dry ingredients. Mix until well combined and crumbly.
Spread mixture evenly onto the prepared baking tray. Bake for 10-12 minutes. The mixture should be dry and crumbly. Cool completely. Break into irregular soil-like pieces.
For the Blood Orange Gel: Combine blood orange juice, sugar, and agar-agar in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Boil for 1 minute to activate agar. Remove from heat.
Pour liquid into a shallow dish. Chill until firm, about 1-2 hours.
Once firm, cut gel into rough chunks. Blend in a high-speed blender until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultra-smooth texture. Transfer to a squeeze bottle or piping bag.
For the Aerated White Chocolate: Prepare an ice bath.
Gently melt white chocolate and cocoa butter together over a bain-marie or in a microwave. Stir until smooth and fully combined.
Pour warm chocolate mixture into a clean siphon. Charge with one nitrous oxide charger. Shake well.
Dispense aerated chocolate directly into the ice bath. The chocolate will solidify into irregular, cloud-like shapes. Remove from ice bath and gently pat dry.
To Assemble: On a large, premium white bone china platter or light grey veined marble surface, artfully scatter the Valrhona Guanaja Chocolate Soil, creating an organic, dark base.
Pipe or drizzle small, irregular drops of Blood Orange Gel over the chocolate soil, resembling abstract blood splatters.
Carefully place irregular pieces of Aerated White Chocolate amidst the soil and gel, mimicking ethereal, ghostly elements.
Garnish sparingly with 1-2 Crystallized Violets per serving area, adding a touch of delicate color and crunch. Serve immediately as a sophisticated sharing snack.
notes: Ensure all components are prepared and chilled before assembly for optimal texture and presentation.
The aerated white chocolate must be kept cold to maintain its ethereal texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Crémeux, Génoise, Raspberry Gel
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist sharing platter of white bone china or grey marble presents four individual, artfully composed chocolate bites. Each bite features a small, perfectly square piece of dark chocolate génoise, approximately 3x3 cm, serving as a delicate base. Upon this, a glossy, elongated quenelle of rich, dark chocolate crémeux rests elegantly, its surface reflecting light. Adjacent to the crémeux, a delicate, irregular shard of crisp cocoa nib tuile stands vertically, providing architectural height and textural contrast. A small, vibrant dot or a fine, organic line of bright ruby-red raspberry gel is strategically placed on the plate, adding a burst of color and a hint of acidity. The composition emphasizes negative space, with each element precisely positioned to create visual harmony and balance. The overall aesthetic is one of understated luxury and extreme precision, highlighting the quality of ingredients and the mastery of technique. The setting features a polished grey marble surface, with dramatic, focused lighting creating soft shadows, and a precisely folded white linen napkin in the background.
instructions: Prepare Chocolate Crémeux: Chop dark chocolate finely. Set aside.
Heat cream and milk in a saucepan until simmering. Do not boil.
Whisk egg yolks and 40g granulated sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour hot cream mixture into egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon (82-85°C). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve over chopped chocolate. Let sit 1 minute.
Stir gently from the center outwards until chocolate is fully melted and mixture is smooth and emulsified.
Pour crémeux into a shallow dish. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill 4 hours or overnight until firm.
Prepare Chocolate Génoise: Preheat oven to 170°C (fan-assisted 150°C). Line a 20x20 cm baking tray with parchment paper.
Whisk 3 large eggs and remaining 40g granulated sugar in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water. Whisk until warm (40°C) and sugar dissolves.
Remove from heat. Continue whisking with an electric mixer until mixture is very thick, pale, and forms a ribbon when lifted.
Sift flour and cocoa powder together. Gently fold into egg mixture in two additions.
Fold in melted butter until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared tray. Spread evenly. Bake 10-12 minutes, until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Cool génoise on a wire rack. Once cool, cut into 3x3 cm squares.
Prepare Raspberry Gel: Combine raspberry puree, 50ml water, and 30g powdered sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk pectin into the simmering puree. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a small container. Chill until set.
Once set, blend gel with an immersion blender until smooth and pipeable.
Prepare Cocoa Nib Tuiles: Melt 20g unsalted butter. Let cool slightly.
Whisk 1 egg white and 30g powdered sugar until smooth. Stir in 50g all-purpose flour and a pinch of salt.
Stir in melted butter and 10g cocoa nibs.
Preheat oven to 160°C (fan-assisted 140°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread small amounts of tuile batter very thinly onto the parchment paper using an offset spatula to create irregular, delicate shapes.
Bake 5-7 minutes, until edges are golden and crisp. Watch carefully as they burn quickly.
Remove from oven. Immediately transfer to a wire rack to cool and crisp.
Assemble: Spoon the smooth raspberry gel into a small piping bag.
On a sharing platter, arrange 4 génoise squares, spaced elegantly.
Using two spoons, form a smooth, elongated quenelle of chocolate crémeux and place it on top of each génoise square.
Pipe a small, artistic dot or a thin, organic line of raspberry gel adjacent to each crémeux quenelle.
Carefully place one delicate cocoa nib tuile shard upright next to each crémeux, creating height and visual interest. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Caribbean Braised Chicken with Rice and Stewed Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Caribbean braised chicken is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. A succulent, whole chicken thigh, with its rich, reddish-brown braising sauce, rests prominently. Alongside, a neat mound of fluffy white long-grain rice. Tender, dark green, roughly chopped Swiss chard is nestled around the chicken and rice, with vibrant red diced tomatoes from the sauce visible. The dish has natural, organic shapes, components touching harmoniously. A sprinkle of fresh green cilantro leaves garnishes the chicken and chard. A bright yellow lime wedge sits on the rim of the bowl. The bowl is placed on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table. A simple ceramic fork and a casually crumpled off-white linen napkin are beside the bowl, hinting at a homely, lived-in atmosphere. Warm, natural overhead lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the food. The entire plate is visible, with appropriate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of hot sauce or a simple green salad.
Offer extra lime wedges for squeezing over the dish.
Can be accompanied by fried plantains or avocado slices.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained
Swiss chard, stems removed, roughly chopped

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken thighs, skin-side down first, until golden and crisp. This takes 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, oregano, and cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes with their juice and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is submerged halfway. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
While chicken simmers, prepare the rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. Combine rice and 500 ml water in a medium saucepan. Add a pinch of salt.
Bring rice to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Add rinsed black beans and chopped Swiss chard to the chicken pot. Stir gently to combine. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, uncovered, until chard is tender and wilted. The sauce will thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve chicken and sauce over fluffy rice. Garnish with fresh cilantro and a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Earth & Sky
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of 'Sweet Earth & Sky' is presented on a large, matte white bone china plate, emphasizing minimalist elegance and abundant negative space. Three halved, perfectly roasted cherry tomatoes, their vibrant red skins slightly wrinkled and caramelized, are artfully placed in a gentle curve. Adjacent to them, a delicate scattering of dark, earthy mushroom crumble creates a striking textural contrast. Nestled within this composition are two to three glistening, amber-hued spheres of sweet chicken consommé gel, catching the light with their pristine clarity. A single, airy quenelle of bright white fromage blanc cloud is positioned to provide height and a soft, ethereal presence. The dish is subtly garnished with a single, fresh micro basil leaf, offering a pinpoint of vivid green. The overall impression is one of sophisticated simplicity, with harmonious colors and diverse textures inviting exploration.
instructions: Prepare Sweet Consommé Gel: Place chicken wings and bones in a large pot. Cover with 2 L filtered water. Bring to a simmer. Skim impurities. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 3 hours. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Cool broth completely. Refrigerate overnight. Skim all fat from chilled broth.

Clarify Consommé: Combine cold broth with 50g white sugar and split vanilla bean. Bring to a gentle simmer. Do not boil. Remove from heat. Let steep 30 minutes. Strain again through a coffee filter or cheesecloth-lined sieve for absolute clarity. You should have approximately 500 ml clarified sweet consommé. Discard vanilla bean.

Set Consommé Gel: Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. Squeeze excess water. Whisk gelatin into warm (not hot) clarified sweet consommé until fully dissolved. Pour consommé into a shallow dish. Chill for at least 4 hours, or until firmly set. Once set, cut into small, irregular cubes or use a small melon baller to create spheres.

Prepare Roasted Tomato Confit: Preheat oven to 160°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Arrange cut-side up on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, 20g white sugar, and a pinch of salt. Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until softened and slightly caramelized. A few minutes before removing from oven, drizzle with balsamic vinegar. Let cool.

Make Mushroom Crumble: Preheat oven to 150°C. Roughly chop dried shiitake mushrooms. Blend in a food processor until a coarse powder forms. In a bowl, combine mushroom powder, almond flour, remaining 30g white sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add cold, cubed butter. Rub with fingertips until a crumbly texture forms. Spread mixture on a baking tray. Bake for 15-20 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and crisp. Let cool completely.
Create Fromage Blanc Cloud: In a cold bowl, whisk fromage blanc with icing sugar until light and airy. Do not overmix.

Assemble Dish (per serving): On a large, minimalist white plate, place 3-4 roasted tomato confit halves in a natural, organic arrangement. Scatter a small, artful portion of mushroom crumble next to the tomatoes. Gently place 2-3 small cubes or spheres of sweet consommé gel. Using a small spoon, form one delicate quenelle of fromage blanc cloud and place it on the plate. Garnish with a single micro basil leaf. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Salami and Black Pepper Minestrone
recipes.visual_description: The Salami and Black Pepper Minestrone is presented in a classic white porcelain soup bowl, showcasing its rich, rustic character. The vibrant, reddish-orange tomato-based broth holds an abundance of finely diced vegetables – bright orange carrots, pale green celery, and verdant zucchini, all cut into uniform 5mm cubes. Small, al dente ditalini pasta and creamy white cannellini beans are evenly distributed throughout the hearty soup. Interspersed are small, savory chunks of rendered salami, adding a distinct meaty texture. A generous snowfall of freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese crowns the center, with a scattering of vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves providing a fresh aromatic contrast. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a slice of crusty Italian bread, all bathed in soft, natural light, evoking a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Dice salami into 5mm cubes. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced salami. Cook until slightly crispy and fat is rendered, about 5-7 minutes. Remove salami with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto base.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add cannellini beans and pasta. Cook according to pasta package directions until pasta is al dente, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in diced zucchini and most of the cooked salami. Simmer for another 3-5 minutes until zucchini is tender-crisp.
Season generously with freshly ground black pepper and salt to taste. The soup should have a prominent black pepper flavor.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with remaining crispy salami, fresh chopped parsley, and a generous grating of Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, use a high-quality, hard cured salami.
Adjust the amount of black pepper to your preference; this recipe emphasizes its flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo de Cerdo con Arroz Rojo y Papas Crujientes con Alioli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo de Cerdo con Arroz Rojo y Papas Crujientes con Alioli is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, set on a light wooden table. Two thick, pan-seared pork loin medallions, golden-brown and tender, are positioned slightly overlapping. Beside them, a neat mound of vibrant red Arroz Rojo, cooked with tomatoes, garlic, and onions. Scattered around are golden-crisp potato wedges, roasted tender inside and crunchy outside. A delicate drizzle of creamy garlic-cheese aioli artfully zigzags over the pork and potatoes. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of golden, toasted garlic breadcrumbs and a small sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley. The composition is balanced, showcasing rich colors and varying textures. The setting includes a folded white cotton napkin and simple modern flatware, bathed in natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately for best texture.
Offer additional aioli in a small ramekin on the side.
Pair with a light-bodied Spanish red wine or a refreshing sangria.
instructions: Prepare the Pork Loin: Slice pork loin into 8 equal medallions, about 2.5 cm thick. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge each medallion in flour, shaking off excess.

Sear Pork Medallions: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 63°C/145°F, rest to 66°C/150°F). Remove from skillet and set aside to rest.

Make Arroz Rojo: Dice half the onion and 2 garlic cloves finely. Grate or finely chop tomatoes. In the same skillet, add 15 ml olive oil. Sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 5 minutes. Add grated tomatoes and smoked paprika. Cook for 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens.

Cook Rice: Stir in rice to the tomato mixture. Toast for 2 minutes. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare Papas Crujientes: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Peel potatoes and cut into 2.5 cm wedges. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and crispy.
Make Garlic-Cheese Aioli: Mince remaining 4 garlic cloves. Grate Manchego cheese. In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, minced garlic, and grated Manchego. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well.
Prepare Garlic Breadcrumbs: Toast bread slices until golden. Process into coarse crumbs. Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs and toast until crispy and golden. Set aside.

Plate the Dish: Place two pork medallions on each plate. Spoon a portion of Arroz Rojo next to the pork. Arrange crispy potato wedges around the plate. Drizzle generously with garlic-cheese aioli. Garnish with toasted garlic breadcrumbs and fresh parsley leaves.
notes: Ensure pork is cooked to an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for safety, allowing it to rest to 66°C (150°F) for optimal juiciness.
Adjust the amount of garlic in the aioli to your preference for a milder or stronger flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Cheddar Oat Bites
recipes.visual_description: Individual golden-brown Broccoli and Cheddar Oat Bites are neatly arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Each bite, approximately 4 cm in diameter, boasts a crisp, golden-brown exterior from pan-frying, revealing an interior flecked with bright green, finely chopped broccoli florets and melted orange cheddar. The texture is visually appealing, showcasing the oats as a binder and adding a rustic element. Four to five bites are clustered slightly off-center, creating a balanced composition with ample negative space. A small sprig of fresh parsley is placed alongside, offering a vibrant green contrast. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table, illuminated by soft, natural light, with a casually folded grey linen napkin nearby. The background is minimal, keeping focus on the elevated snack.
instructions: Blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Drain very well. Cool completely.
Finely chop blanched broccoli. Press out any excess water using a clean cloth.
In a mixing bowl, combine chopped broccoli, grated cheddar, rolled oats, egg, diced onion, minced garlic, and all-purpose flour.
Season with salt and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Form the mixture into small, flat bites, approximately 3-4 cm in diameter.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Carefully place the bites in the hot pan. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer cooked bites to a wire rack to drain any excess oil.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Smoked Ham and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Hearty Smoked Ham and Potato Bake rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The golden-brown crust of the baked dish, rich with melted, bubbly cheddar cheese, covers a comforting blend of tender potato slices and savory smoked ham chunks. The potatoes are thinly sliced, layered evenly, while the ham is diced into robust 1.5 cm cubes, providing hearty texture. A few scattered flecks of fresh green chopped parsley provide a natural, functional garnish on top. The plate is positioned on a well-used wooden dining table, showing subtle signs of wear. Beside the plate, a casual cloth napkin and a standard fork are placed. Warm, cozy lighting, as if from overhead kitchen fixtures, illuminates the scene, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad and crusty bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Stir in half of the grated cheese until melted. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.
Arrange half of the potato slices in the prepared dish. Top with half of the diced ham and half of the sliced onion.
Pour half of the cheese sauce over the layers.
Repeat layers with remaining potatoes, ham, onion, and cheese sauce.
Sprinkle remaining grated cheese over the top.
Bake 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: To check for doneness, insert a knife into the center of the bake; it should slide in easily.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato Cinnamon Jam Crostini with Goat Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A clean white rectangular porcelain platter showcases an array of approximately 12-16 individual crostini. Each crostini features a crisp, golden-brown baguette slice, topped with a creamy layer of soft, stark white goat cheese. A generous dollop of rich, deep reddish-brown tomato cinnamon jam rests atop the cheese. The jam has a slightly rustic, chunky texture, revealing diced tomato and onion pieces. A single, vibrant green basil leaf elegantly crowns each crostini, providing a fresh color contrast. The platter sits on a light, distressed wooden table surface. A folded natural linen napkin is placed beside the platter. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating subtle shadows. The background is simple and uncluttered, suggesting a modern bistro environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as part of a mezze spread or antipasto platter.
instructions: Dice tomatoes and red onion. Mince garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, brown sugar, red wine vinegar, cinnamon stick, dried oregano, salt, and pepper.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 45-60 minutes. The jam should thicken and become spreadable. Add a splash of water if mixture becomes too dry. Remove cinnamon stick.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice baguette into 1 cm thick rounds. Arrange slices on a baking sheet. Drizzle lightly with remaining 15 ml olive oil.
Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Let cool slightly.
Spread a layer of softened goat cheese on each toasted crostini.
Spoon a generous amount of tomato cinnamon jam over the goat cheese.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: The jam can be made ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to a week.

recipes.recipe_name: Radicchio and Ricotta Cheesecake with Balsamic Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Radicchio and Ricotta Cheesecake stands elegantly on a clean white porcelain plate. The golden-brown biscuit crust forms a sturdy base. Above it, the creamy, pale ivory cheesecake filling is visible, subtly speckled with deep reddish-purple, finely shredded caramelized radicchio. The cheesecake slice has a smooth, firm texture. A glossy, dark amber balsamic glaze is artfully drizzled over the top, creating a delicate contrasting pattern. The plating is clean and refined, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a plain cotton napkin beside the plate, and a hint of the whole cheesecake on a stand in the background. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish.
instructions: Wash radicchio. Remove outer leaves. Quarter it. Remove core. Thinly slice.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a pan. Add sliced radicchio. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add brown sugar and red wine vinegar to radicchio. Cook until liquid evaporates and radicchio is caramelized, about 8-10 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside to cool.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Crush digestive biscuits finely. Mix with 75g melted butter.
Press biscuit mixture firmly into the bottom of an 18 cm springform pan. Bake for 10 minutes. Remove and let cool.
Reduce oven temperature to 150°C. In a large bowl, beat cream cheese and ricotta until smooth.
Add granulated sugar, vanilla extract, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt. Beat until combined.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing until just incorporated after each addition. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in the cooled caramelized radicchio.
Pour filling over the cooled crust in the springform pan. Place the pan in a larger roasting pan.
Pour hot water into the roasting pan, halfway up the side of the springform pan (creating a water bath).
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until the edges are set but the center slightly jiggles.
Turn off the oven. Leave the cheesecake in the oven with the door ajar for 1 hour.
Remove from oven. Cool completely on a wire rack. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
For the balsamic glaze, combine balsamic vinegar and honey in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer until thickened to a syrupy consistency, about 10-15 minutes. Let cool.
Carefully remove cheesecake from the pan. Slice and drizzle with balsamic glaze before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Crostini with Fresh Tomato-Basil Relish
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown toasted baguette slices serve as the base for these elegant crostini. Each slice is generously topped with a mound of finely diced, sautéed chicken and cremini mushrooms, creating a savory, earthy foundation. The chicken pieces are golden from searing, and the mushrooms are tender and lightly caramelized. Crowned atop is a vibrant, fresh tomato-basil relish, featuring small, bright red cherry tomato cubes and flecks of deep green basil, glistening slightly from olive oil. The relish provides a burst of fresh color and texture against the warm tones of the chicken and bread. A delicate drizzle of dark, glossy balsamic glaze traces across some crostini, adding visual depth. The canapés are arranged neatly, with consistent spacing, on a simple rustic wooden board or a clean white rectangular ceramic platter, showcasing 8-12 pieces. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered around for garnish. The setting is a modern bistro, with a clean white porcelain dinner plate visible in the background, a cotton napkin beside it, and natural, even lighting highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimal and unobtrusive.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an appetizer with a pre-dinner aperitivo or a light, crisp Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Arrange on a baking sheet. Brush both sides lightly with 30ml olive oil.
Toast in the oven for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Set aside.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Dice chicken into 1 cm cubes. Add diced chicken to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Dice mushrooms into 1 cm cubes. Finely dice onion. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced mushrooms and onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Minced garlic. Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return cooked chicken to the pan with the mushroom mixture. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.

Finely dice cherry tomatoes. Finely chop most of the fresh basil. In a small bowl, combine diced cherry tomatoes and chopped basil. Drizzle with a small amount of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Stir gently to create the relish.
Spoon a portion of the chicken and mushroom mixture onto each toasted crostini. Top with a spoonful of the fresh tomato-basil relish.
Arrange crostini on a serving platter. Drizzle lightly with balsamic glaze, if using. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves and shaved Parmesan, if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C for safety.
For best flavor, use fresh, ripe cherry tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single bone-in chicken thigh, braised to a deep reddish-brown, rests on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously coated in a rich, rustic chipotle-tomato sauce, showcasing small, tender chunks of tomato and flecks of dark chipotle. Beside the chicken, golden-brown roasted potato wedges are artfully arranged, their edges slightly crisp and interiors soft. A scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh cilantro brightens the dish. A bright green lime wedge is placed nearby, ready for squeezing. The overall presentation is professional yet inviting, with balanced colors and textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with natural, even lighting from above, creating a casual bistro atmosphere. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping up the sauce.
Offer a side of simple white rice.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chipotle peppers, and adobo sauce. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.

While chicken braises, preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut potatoes into 3 cm wedges. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.
Carefully remove chicken from the oven. Discard skin if desired, or leave on for texture. Taste sauce and adjust seasoning.

Serve braised chicken thigh on a clean white porcelain plate. Spoon ample chipotle tomato sauce over and around the chicken. Arrange roasted potato wedges alongside the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: Adjust chipotle peppers to your preferred spice level. For more heat, add an extra pepper; for less, use only the adobo sauce.
Braising bone-in chicken adds more flavor to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Corn Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, golden-hued Creamy Chicken and Corn Risotto is presented in a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto flows naturally across the plate, showcasing its rich, velvety texture. Visible within the creamy rice are tender, golden-brown seared chicken chunks and bright yellow corn kernels. A generous scattering of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves adorns the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese completes the dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, evoking a casual bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting colors and textures, with a soft, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Finely dice the yellow onion.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 20 g butter to the pot.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent. This is tostatura.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add a ladleful of hot chicken stock to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is almost absorbed. Maintain a gentle simmer.
Continue adding stock, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each addition is nearly absorbed before adding the next.
After about 10 minutes of cooking the rice, return the seared chicken chunks to the pot. Add corn kernels and dried oregano.
Continue adding stock and stirring until rice is al dente, about 18-20 minutes total cooking time for the rice. Risotto should be creamy and fluid.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in remaining 40 g butter and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute. This is mantecare.
Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves, roughly chopped.
Cover and let risotto rest for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Potato & Bean Fritters with Tangy Gherkin Relish
recipes.visual_description: Fritters are arranged in a natural, slightly overlapping cluster on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Each fritter is golden-brown with visible crispy edges, showcasing the texture of the mashed and lightly crushed beans within. A dollop of vibrant green gherkin relish, with finely diced red onion and fresh dill, sits atop or beside each fritter. The dominant golden brown of fritters contrasts with the bright green and pinkish-red of the relish. Textures are crispy exterior, soft interior, and chunky relish. Plating is casual, with negative space. Potatoes are mashed, beans lightly crushed, gherkins and red onion finely diced. Served on a light bamboo table, with an undyed linen napkin. Soft natural light illuminates the scene, with a clean, minimalist background. A shared portion is presented.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a shared appetizer or snack.
Pair with a light, crisp beer or sparkling water.
The concept aligns with zero-waste and plant-forward movements in modern global cuisine, drawing inspiration from various pickling and fritter traditions.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly.
Drain cannellini beans. Reserve liquid for other uses. Lightly mash some beans, leave some whole.
Combine mashed potatoes, mashed and whole beans, flour, vegan Worcestershire sauce, and beer in a large bowl. Mix until just combined. Season with salt and pepper.
Scoop approximately 30g of mixture per fritter. Gently flatten into small patties, about 5cm diameter and 1.5cm thick.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. Fry fritters for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Finely dice gherkins and red onion. Combine with apple cider vinegar, sugar, and chopped dill in a small bowl. Mix well. Let sit for 5 minutes.
Arrange fritters on a platter. Top each with a spoonful of gherkin relish. Garnish with fresh dill.
notes: The reserved bean liquid (aquafaba) can be used as a vegan egg white substitute in other recipes, such as meringues or mayonnaise, contributing to zero-waste cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Velouté of Green Lentils and Split Peas with Crispy Garlic and Chive Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated individual portion of a Velouté of Green Lentils and Split Peas is presented in a deep, pristine white bone china bowl with a subtle, modern rim design. The soup itself is a smooth, satiny, and rich verdant green-gold hue, perfectly consistent in texture, filling the bowl with generous negative space around its edges. Precisely placed on the surface are a few artfully arranged, golden-brown, translucent crispy garlic chips, providing a textural contrast. Around the chips, several deliberate, vibrant emerald green droplets of chive oil create an abstract, organic pattern on the soup's surface, reflecting the light. The overall composition is minimalist and intentional, with each element contributing to the visual and textural narrative. The bowl rests on a luxurious grey-veined Carrara marble surface, which provides a cool, sophisticated backdrop. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, lies to the left of the bowl. The lighting is dramatic and professional, creating soft shadows that enhance the depth and form of the dish. The background is ultra-minimalist, allowing the dish to be the sole, undisputed focal point of the image.
instructions: Rinse green lentils. Rinse yellow split peas. Soak split peas in cold water for 2 hours. Drain.
Peel and thinly slice 4 garlic cloves. Set aside for crispy chips. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Mince shallots.
In a large pot, melt butter with 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and shallots. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.

Add rinsed green lentils and drained split peas to the pot. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-50 minutes, or until lentils and peas are very tender.

While soup simmers, prepare garlic chips. Heat remaining olive oil in a small pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced garlic. Fry gently until golden and crispy. Do not burn. Remove garlic chips with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towel to drain. Season with a pinch of salt. Reserve the garlic-infused oil.

Prepare chive oil. Blanch fresh chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice water to cool. Drain and pat dry. Blend blanched chives with 2 tablespoons of the reserved garlic-infused oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a clear oil. Discard solids.

Once lentils and peas are tender, remove soup from heat. Use an immersion blender to purée soup until completely smooth. For an ultra-velvety texture, pass the puréed soup through a fine-mesh chinois, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Return strained soup to a clean pot. Reheat gently over low heat. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with a little hot water or stock if too thick.
To serve, ladle the hot velouté into warm bowls. Drizzle a few drops of the vibrant chive oil onto the surface. Artistically place a few crispy garlic chips in the center.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Mushroom Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Garlic Mushroom Crostini is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. Two thick slices of toasted ciabatta bread, golden-brown, serve as the base. Each is generously piled with sautéed brown mushrooms, cut into thick slices, glistening with olive oil and minced garlic. The mushrooms display an earthy brown hue and tender texture. Vibrant green, torn fresh basil leaves are scattered over, adding color and aroma. A light dusting of black pepper is visible. The homely presentation suggests a casual family meal. A simple linen napkin and water glass are softly blurred in the background. Warm, natural light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its comforting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an appetizer before a pasta dish or main course
Pair with a simple glass of dry white wine or sparkling water
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice ciabatta bread diagonally into 2cm thick pieces.
Brush bread slices with 5ml olive oil.
Toast bread in the oven for 5-7 minutes, until golden. Remove.
While bread toasts, heat 10ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season mushrooms with salt and black pepper.
Spoon sautéed mushrooms over toasted ciabatta slices.
Garnish with torn fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: This dish is a simple, comforting vegetarian starter that highlights fresh ingredients.
Adjust garlic and basil to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom and Basil Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy Mushroom and Basil Risotto is presented in a wide, shallow ceramic bowl with a rustic, slightly irregular edge. The risotto is a warm, pale ivory color, with tender Arborio rice grains suspended in a fluid, rich sauce. Sliced cremini mushrooms, sautéed until golden-brown, are generously mixed throughout, some resting on top. Finely chopped fresh basil leaves are scattered over the surface, providing vibrant green accents. The dish has a natural, slightly asymmetrical arrangement. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple white linen napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. A silver fork and spoon rest on the table. Warm, soft light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's comforting appeal. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a homely, inviting presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
instructions: Heat olive oil and 5g butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until softened and slightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent.
Warm vegetable broth in a separate pot.
Pour in 125 ml warm vegetable broth into the rice. Stir until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding warm broth, 125 ml at a time, stirring constantly. Allow each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes.
Risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 10g butter, grated Parmesan, and chopped fresh basil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use warm broth to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring continuously helps release starch for creaminess.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Pasta Croquettes with Tomato-Coffee Aioli
recipes.visual_description: The dish features small, golden-brown Savory Pasta Croquettes, each approximately 3 cm in diameter, arranged organically on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The ditalini pasta, cooked al dente, is bound within a rich, savory tomato and coffee-infused matrix. The exterior boasts a crisp, Panko-crumbed texture, contrasting with the soft, flavorful interior. A small, creamy dollop of pale brown Tomato-Coffee Aioli sits elegantly beside the croquettes, garnished with a single, vibrant green parsley leaf. Finely chopped fresh parsley is lightly sprinkled over the croquettes for a pop of color. The setting is a light wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin to the left. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the warm tones of the croquettes and the smooth texture of the aioli, against a subtle, blurred modern bistro background. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, showcasing the refined snack.
instructions: Cook ditalini pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté minced garlic and diced shallot until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Stir in espresso powder until dissolved.
Transfer cooked pasta to a large bowl. Add the tomato-espresso mixture, grated Parmesan, and half of the chopped parsley. Crack in the egg.
Mix thoroughly. Season with salt and black pepper. The mixture should be firm enough to form.
Take small portions of the pasta mixture and form into uniform 3 cm diameter croquettes. Press firmly to ensure they hold shape.
Place Panko breadcrumbs in a shallow dish. Roll each croquette in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to coat completely.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or high-sided pan to 175°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
For the aioli: In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, lemon juice, and a pinch of espresso powder. Stir well. Season with salt to taste.
Arrange hot croquettes on a serving plate. Serve immediately with the Tomato-Coffee Aioli for dipping. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure pasta mixture is well-drained and cooled slightly before forming to prevent sticking.
For best results, chill formed croquettes for 15 minutes before frying to help them hold their shape.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Tamarind White Port Parcels
recipes.visual_description: A clean, professional restaurant-style plating. Three golden-brown, crispy rice paper parcels are neatly arranged on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate, slightly off-center. Each parcel is about 6-7 cm long, cylindrically shaped, and has a delicate, translucent crispiness. A generous drizzle of glossy, dark amber Tamarind White Port Sauce cascades over and around the parcels, creating a rich, inviting sheen. The sauce pools slightly at the base of the parcels. Sprinkled over the parcels and sauce are vibrant red chili threads, providing a sharp color contrast and delicate texture. A small, fresh mint sprig is placed beside the parcels, adding a touch of verdant green and freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtle, clean background that suggests a modern bistro setting. The overall presentation is elegant, balanced, and inviting.
instructions: Thinly slice 3 shallots. In a small saucepan, combine 50ml white port and 50g sugar. Bring to a simmer. Dissolve sugar. Add sliced shallots. Poach gently until translucent and tender, about 10-15 minutes. Drain shallots, reserve liquid. Spread shallots on parchment paper to dry slightly.

In a saucepan, combine 100g tamarind paste, 100ml white port, 100ml water, and 80g sugar. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring, until sugar dissolves and sauce thickens slightly, about 8-10 minutes. Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve to remove pulp. Set aside.
Carefully remove seeds from the red chili. Slice chili into very thin strips (threads). Set aside.

Rehydrate one rice paper sheet at a time in warm water for 20-30 seconds until pliable. Lay flat on a clean surface. Place about 5g of candied shallots in the center. Fold sides over, then roll tightly into a small parcel or spring roll shape. Repeat for 12 parcels.

Heat neutral oil in a deep pan to 170°C. Fry parcels in batches for 30-45 seconds until golden and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain excess oil.
Arrange 3 crispy parcels on each plate. Drizzle generously with Tamarind White Port Sauce. Garnish with chili threads and a fresh mint sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Pineapple Coconut Chicken Soup with Crispy Rice Paper
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Savory Pineapple Coconut Chicken Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with subtle imperfections, placed on a well-used, warm-toned wooden kitchen table. The soup, a creamy, pale yellow from coconut milk, contains tender, diced chicken pieces, vibrant small diced pineapple chunks, and translucent thinly sliced onion, all gently simmered. A scattering of fresh chopped cilantro and a few julienned red chili strips float on top, adding contrasting green and red. Beside the bowl, a simple white ceramic Asian soup spoon rests casually. A few crispy, golden-brown rice paper crackers are stacked loosely on a small side plate. The scene is lit by soft, warm kitchen light, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere with natural, lived-in clutter.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes. Dice pineapple into 1.5 cm cubes. Thinly slice onion. Mince garlic. Peel and julienne ginger. Dice red bell pepper.

Prepare crispy rice paper: Heat 1 cm oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Carefully add rice paper sheets, one at a time. Fry 10-15 seconds per side until crispy and puffed. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate. Repeat for all sheets. Set aside.
Drain excess oil from skillet, leaving about 5 ml. Add sliced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and julienned ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides and cooked through to 75°C (167°F).
Stir in diced pineapple and diced red bell pepper. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in fish sauce, sugar, and juice from half a lemon. Taste and adjust seasoning with more lemon juice, fish sauce, or salt as needed.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Slice red chili into thin rounds if using. Serve with crispy rice paper crackers on the side.
notes: This recipe is naturally gluten-free. Ensure all packaged ingredients (broth, fish sauce) are certified gluten-free if strict dietary requirements apply.

recipes.recipe_name: Coca-Cola Braised Pork Ribs with Spicy Orange Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of glistening Coca-Cola braised pork ribs rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three tender, bone-in ribs are arranged neatly, showcasing their dark reddish-brown exterior and sticky, vibrant orange-red glaze. The meat appears succulent and falls easily from the bone. Beside the ribs, a generous serving of golden-brown chorizo-potato hash is presented, featuring evenly diced potatoes and crispy chorizo bits. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley or cilantro and a few thin strips of bright orange zest, adding color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a fork and knife placed beside it on a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional, yet approachable restaurant-style presentation with moderate negative space. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of creamy coleslaw or cornbread.
Offer extra BBQ glaze on the side for dipping.
Traditionally enjoyed with a cold beverage like iced tea or a craft beer.

ingredients.name: Pork Ribs (St. Louis style or baby back)

instructions: Pat pork ribs dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and half of the fennel seeds.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear ribs in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and dried red chilies. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining fennel seeds, brown sugar, and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze with Coca-Cola, orange juice, apple cider vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer.
Return ribs to the pot. Ensure ribs are mostly submerged; add a little water if needed. Cover and braise in a preheated oven at 150°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until very tender.

While ribs braise, prepare the chorizo-potato hash. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Dice chorizo into 1 cm cubes. Cook chorizo in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove chorizo, leaving rendered fat in the pan.
Add diced potatoes to the skillet with chorizo fat. Cook until golden brown and tender, about 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in crispy chorizo.
Once ribs are tender, carefully remove them from the pot. Strain the braising liquid into a saucepan. Skim off excess fat.
