Peel carrots. Slice into 1.5 cm thick coins. Toss with 200 ml olive oil, 20 g salt, and 10 g black pepper. Spread on large baking sheets.
Roast carrots for 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
Thinly slice red onions. Heat remaining 300 ml olive oil in large pots or pans over medium-low heat. Add sliced red onions.
Cook onions slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft.
Whisk together balsamic vinegar, 1.5 litres extra virgin olive oil, Dijon mustard, honey, minced garlic, 30 g salt, and 10 g black pepper in a large bowl.
Allow roasted carrots and caramelized onions to cool to room temperature.

Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly.
Roughly chop pecans. Crumble feta cheese. Fold in chopped pecans and crumbled feta cheese.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad
recipes.visual_description: A homely, warm Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The roasted carrots, cut into 1 cm thick rounds, display tender edges and slight caramelization, a warm orange hue. Red onion wedges, 1.5 cm thick, are softened and slightly browned. Cooked green lentils, plump and earthy brown, are interspersed throughout. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is generously scattered over the top. A simple, clear lemon-olive oil dressing glistens lightly on the ingredients. The components are casually tossed, allowing natural overlaps and varied textures to show. The plate is adequately filled but not overcrowded, allowing some negative space. A plain linen napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. Warm, inviting light suggests a cozy kitchen setting. The entire plate is visible.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 large, peeled and sliced into 1 cm thick rounds

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Toss carrot rounds and red onion wedges with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Flip halfway through cooking.
While vegetables roast, combine rinsed lentils and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid.
In a small bowl, whisk remaining 30ml olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
In a large serving bowl, combine warm roasted carrots and red onions with cooked lentils.
Pour dressing over the salad. Add chopped parsley. Toss gently to combine.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot and Red Onion Marinated Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Carrot and Red Onion Marinated Salad is presented casually on a well-used, rustic wooden dining table. The salad fills an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, showcasing a generous, unpretentious portion. Vibrant julienned carrots, bright orange in color, are loosely mixed with thinly sliced, pale purple and white red onion rings. Freshly chopped green dill is sprinkled throughout, adding flecks of color and a fresh aroma. The vegetables glisten with a light, clear vinaigrette, indicating they are well coated and marinated. The arrangement is organic and flowing, with components touching and overlapping naturally, as if served directly from a family bowl. A simple, sturdy fork rests beside the plate, and a casually folded cloth napkin or a paper towel is nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen window or overhead fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a home kitchen.
instructions: Wash and peel carrots. Julienne the carrots into thin, uniform strips.
Peel the red onion. Thinly slice the red onion into half-moons.
Roughly chop the fresh dill.
In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, apple cider vinegar, sugar, salt, and black pepper until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Add the julienned carrots, sliced red onion, and chopped dill to the bowl with the dressing.
Toss all ingredients together until well combined and coated with the dressing.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. For best results, marinate for 2-3 hours before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The Chicken and Broccoli Risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing its creamy, fluid consistency. The Arborio rice maintains its al dente texture, glistening with melted Parmesan and butter. Tender, golden-brown chicken cubes are nestled throughout the risotto, alongside vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets. Fresh basil leaves, torn into irregular pieces, are scattered on top, providing a fragrant, contrasting green. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese finishes the dish. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp dry white wine
Accompany with a simple mixed green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar
instructions: Dice chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through, reaching 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter to the pot. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is absorbed.

Add one ladle of hot chicken broth. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 20-25 minutes.
While risotto cooks, steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp.
After 20 minutes, stir in cooked chicken and broccoli into the risotto.
Continue adding broth and stirring until risotto is creamy and rice is al dente. It should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Stir in torn fresh basil leaves. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken broth is hot throughout the risotto cooking process for best results.
The risotto should be stirred constantly for a creamy texture.
Use freshly grated Parmesan for superior flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Russian Beef and Sausage Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Russian Beef and Sausage Skillet is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The dish features tender, braised beef cut into rustic 3cm cubes, alongside golden-brown, pan-seared pork sausage rounds, approximately 2cm thick. Interspersed are earthy, varied mushrooms (rustic slices and halves) and tender 2cm potato cubes, all coated in a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown sauce. A vibrant green scattering of freshly chopped dill garnishes the top, with a small swirl of white sour cream adding a contrasting creamy element. The composition is hearty and inviting, with a balanced distribution of ingredients showcasing their distinct shapes and textures. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A fresh white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are neatly placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with slices of dark rye bread for dipping.
Traditionally accompanied by pickled cucumbers (marinovannye ogurtsy) or sauerkraut.
A shot of vodka is a common accompaniment for a hearty Russian meal.
instructions: Season beef cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove beef from skillet and set aside.
Add sausage rounds to the skillet. Brown well on both sides. Remove sausage and set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, tomato paste, and paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return seared beef to the skillet. Pour in beef broth and add the bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Add potato cubes and sliced/halved mushrooms to the skillet. Return sausage to the skillet.
Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and sauce has slightly thickened.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in sour cream and chopped fresh dill. Heat through gently; do not boil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot with slices of rye bread.
notes: This dish develops deeper flavors if made a day ahead and reheated.
Adjust the sauce consistency by simmering longer for a thicker sauce or adding a splash more broth for a looser consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Salmon Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single confit salmon fillet, golden-pink and moist, rests on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate. The salmon is a whole, thick piece. Beside it, a vibrant, smooth swirl of bright orange fermented carrot puree. Scattered around are deep green roasted broccoli florets and tender-crisp batons of broccoli stem, showing slight charring. The plate maintains ample negative space, highlighting each ingredient's natural beauty. A light bamboo table surface, undyed linen napkin, and a simple ceramic water glass are visible. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the varied textures and organic shapes.

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves, peeled and lightly crushed

instructions: Prepare Fermented Carrots (at least 5-7 days in advance): Wash and thinly slice 200g of carrots. Pack tightly into a clean jar. Dissolve 5g salt in 250ml filtered water to make a brine. Add 1g peppercorns to jar. Pour brine over carrots, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, burping daily, until pleasantly sour. Refrigerate.

Prepare Carrot Puree: Peel remaining 300g carrots. Cut into 2cm rounds. Steam or boil until very tender. Drain well. Combine cooked carrots with 50g of the fermented carrots (drained). Blend until very smooth, adding a tablespoon of the fermented carrot brine if needed for consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Prepare Broccoli: Wash broccoli. Cut florets into bite-sized pieces. Peel the thick skin from the broccoli stems. Cut stems into 1.5 cm thick batons.
Roast Broccoli: Toss broccoli florets and batons with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast at 200°C for 12-15 minutes, until tender-crisp and lightly charred.
Confit Salmon: Preheat oven to 120°C. Place salmon fillets in a small, oven-safe dish. Add dill, thyme, garlic, and lemon slices around salmon. Pour olive oil over salmon until fully submerged.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until salmon is cooked through and flakes easily. Internal temperature should reach 60-63°C.
Carefully remove salmon from oil. Drain excess oil.

Plate: Spoon a generous swirl of carrot puree onto each plate. Place one confit salmon fillet next to the puree. Arrange roasted broccoli florets and batons around the salmon. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a sprinkle of flaky sea salt.
notes: This recipe minimizes food waste by utilizing broccoli stems and fermenting carrots.
Confit is a traditional preservation method, extending shelf life.
Fermentation enhances flavor and adds probiotic benefits.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken and Roasted Cherry Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous swirl of al dente penne pasta forms the base on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Scattered throughout the pasta are vibrant, slightly burst roasted cherry tomato halves, displaying their deep red and caramelized edges. Golden-brown, irregular chunks of pan-seared chicken are nestled atop and within the pasta, showcasing a crisp exterior. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the dish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish has a cohesive, saucy coating without being swimming in liquid. The overall presentation is inviting, professional, and approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface. A fork and knife are placed to the right, and a folded natural linen napkin to the left. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese.
Offer crusty artisan bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 50 g (freshly grated, plus extra for serving)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss halved cherry tomatoes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

While tomatoes roast, season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.

Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the pan.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Add drained pasta, roasted cherry tomatoes, seared chicken, and most of the fresh basil leaves to the pan with the sauce. Toss to combine.
Add grated Parmesan cheese and about 60-120 ml reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until a light sauce coats the pasta. Season with more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil and extra Parmesan.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.
Using reserved pasta water helps emulsify the sauce and thicken it.

recipes.recipe_name: Tofu Blanc Mousse Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably cut slice of the Tofu Blanc Mousse Entremet is centered on a pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a delicate gold rim. The slice, approximately 4 cm wide and 8 cm high, stands upright, showcasing its distinct layers. The bottom layer is a thin, golden-brown Almond Dacquoise, revealing its crisp, slightly textured surface. Above it rests a vibrant, jewel-toned Raspberry Coulis insert, a precise square of deep red, providing a striking color contrast. Encasing the coulis is the ethereal Tofu Blanc Mousse, a creamy, off-white layer with a smooth, velvety finish. The entire entremet is enveloped in a glossy, mirror-like white chocolate glaze that cascades down the sides, reflecting light with subtle sheen. Abundant white space surrounds the dessert on the plate, emphasizing its minimalist elegance. Two perfectly plump, fresh red raspberries are artfully placed beside the slice, one slightly forward, the other slightly behind, adding a burst of natural color. A tiny, delicate fragment of edible silver leaf adheres to the top edge of the mousse, catching the light with a subtle gleam. The setting features a pristine white marble surface, under dramatic, professional lighting that casts soft shadows, enhancing the dessert's architectural precision and refined aesthetic. The background is utterly minimalist, allowing the entremet to be the sole, exquisite focal point.

ingredients.name: Full-Fat Coconut Cream (chilled, solid part only)

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Draw a 15x15 cm square on it.
For the Almond Dacquoise: Sift almond flour and icing sugar together. Set aside.
Whip aquafaba in a stand mixer until foamy. Gradually add 40 g granulated sugar. Whip until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Gently fold in the almond flour mixture into the aquafaba meringue.

Spread the dacquoise batter evenly within the drawn square on the parchment paper. Bake for 20-25 minutes, until lightly golden and crisp. Let cool completely. Trim edges for a precise 15x15 cm square.
For the Raspberry Coulis Insert: Combine raspberries, 30 g granulated sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until berries soften.
Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Return purée to saucepan.
Whisk agar-agar powder into the purée. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly, for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Pour coulis into a 12x12 cm square mold (or a larger mold lined to this size). Freeze for at least 2 hours until solid.
For the Tofu Blanc Mousse: Melt 150 g vegan white chocolate over a double boiler or in a microwave. Let cool slightly.
Drain silken tofu well. Blend tofu in a high-speed blender until perfectly smooth and creamy. Ensure no lumps remain.
Add melted white chocolate, maple syrup, and vanilla extract to the blender. Blend until thoroughly combined and smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the solid part of chilled coconut cream until light and fluffy. Do not over-whip.
Gently fold the tofu-chocolate mixture into the whipped coconut cream until just combined. Do not deflate the mixture.
To Assemble the Entremet: Line a 16x16 cm square mold with acetate strips or plastic wrap.
Place the cooled almond dacquoise square at the bottom of the mold.
Pour half of the tofu blanc mousse over the dacquoise, spreading evenly.
Carefully place the frozen raspberry coulis insert onto the mousse layer, centered.
Pour the remaining tofu blanc mousse over the coulis, spreading to cover completely. Smooth the top.
Freeze the entremet for a minimum of 6 hours, preferably overnight, until completely solid.
For the White Chocolate Glaze: Gently melt 100 g vegan white chocolate and coconut oil together over a double boiler or in a microwave. Stir until smooth and fluid.
Remove entremet from freezer. Gently unmold and place on a wire rack set over a tray to catch excess glaze.
Pour the warm (not hot) glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Allow glaze to set for 10-15 minutes.
Transfer the entremet to a serving plate. Allow to temper in the refrigerator for 30-45 minutes before slicing.
To Serve: Using a hot, sharp knife, cut the entremet into 4 precise slices. Clean knife between each cut.
Plate each slice centrally on individual dessert plates. Garnish each with two fresh raspberries and a small piece of edible silver leaf.
notes: Ensure all components are chilled or frozen to the specified temperatures for clean layering and glazing.
Use a hot, sharp knife for clean cuts to reveal the layers perfectly.
Adjust sweetness of mousse and coulis to your preference, tasting as you go.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tofu Berry Bites
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine uniform miniature square tofu bites are arranged with consistent spacing on a light, handcrafted ceramic serving platter in an earthy cream tone. Each bite features a compact, light golden-brown oat-almond crust base, topped by a smooth, creamy, off-white fermented tofu layer. A small dollop of vibrant, glossy mixed berry topping, showcasing natural fruit shapes, is spooned onto the center of each bite. A single, small, fresh green mint leaf garnishes each piece. The presentation is minimalistic and clean, with ample white space. The platter rests on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed natural beige linen napkin. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, with subtle green foliage in the clean, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Rinse tofu. Press excess water from tofu for 30 minutes. Wrap in clean cloth. Place heavy object on top.
Combine pressed tofu, maple syrup, vegan yogurt, vanilla extract, and lemon zest in a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Scrape down sides as needed.

Transfer tofu mixture to a clean glass jar. Cover loosely with a cloth. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 12-24 hours. Taste periodically. It should develop a slight tang. Refrigerate once desired tang is reached.
For the crust, combine rolled oats and almonds in a food processor. Process until a coarse flour forms.
Add melted coconut oil to oat-almond mixture. Pulse until crumbs stick together when pressed.
Line a small square baking pan (approx. 20x20 cm) with parchment paper, leaving overhangs. Press crust mixture evenly into the bottom of the pan. Chill in refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Pour fermented tofu mixture over chilled crust. Spread evenly. Return to refrigerator. Chill for at least 4 hours, or until firm.

For the berry topping, combine mixed berries and 2 tablespoons of maple syrup in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally. Berries should soften and release juices. Mash lightly if desired. Cool completely.
Once tofu layer is firm, lift from pan using parchment overhangs. Cut into 6 or 9 uniform square or rectangular pieces. Use a hot, clean knife for clean cuts.
Spoon a small amount of cooled berry topping onto the center of each tofu bite. Garnish each piece with a single fresh mint leaf.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Cottage Cheese & Herb Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: A rustic wooden board holds a generous portion of golden-brown crispy cottage cheese and herb croquettes. Each oblong croquette boasts a crunchy, textured crust from the corn flakes. A few croquettes are artfully stacked or clustered, revealing hints of the creamy, herb-flecked cottage cheese interior where one might be slightly broken. The dominant colors are rich golden brown with flecks of vibrant green herbs. A small white ceramic ramekin of pale yellow lemon mayonnaise sits beside the croquettes. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a casual cotton napkin placed nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the snack, creating an inviting, professional presentation.
instructions: Drain cottage cheese thoroughly. Press out excess liquid.
In a large bowl, combine drained cottage cheese, egg, flour, chives, parsley, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Mix until well combined.
Place crushed corn flakes in a shallow dish.
Form the cottage cheese mixture into oblong or cylindrical croquettes, approximately 5 cm long and 2.5 cm wide. You should get about 16-20 croquettes.
Roll each croquette firmly in the crushed corn flakes, ensuring a complete and even coating.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Oil should be about 2 cm deep.
Carefully place croquettes into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan. Fry in batches.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides.
Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
For the dipping sauce, combine mayonnaise and lemon juice in a small bowl. Stir well.
Serve croquettes warm with the lemon mayonnaise.

recipes.recipe_name: Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers with Corn and Cheese Filling
recipes.visual_description: A rustic wooden board or clean rectangular white platter holds 8-10 golden-brown bacon-wrapped jalapeño poppers. They are arranged in a slightly offset cluster, showcasing vibrant colors and textures. Each popper is a halved jalapeño, roasted to a tender, slightly blistered green, generously filled with creamy, melted white Monterey Jack and yellow corn. The filling is slightly browned and bubbly. Each popper is tightly wrapped with crispy, rendered streaky bacon, showing its rich, reddish-brown hue. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped coriander provides contrast. The board rests on a light wooden table. A white cotton napkin is folded beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the bacon's crispy texture and gooey cheese. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual American bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with ranch dressing or a cool sour cream dip.
Often enjoyed at casual gatherings or game nights.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Halve jalapeño chiles lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes carefully.
In a bowl, combine softened cream cheese, shredded Monterey Jack, corn, finely diced red onion, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spoon cheese mixture into each jalapeño half.
Wrap each filled jalapeño half with a slice of bacon. Secure with a toothpick if needed.
Arrange poppers on the prepared baking tray.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bacon is crisp and cheese is bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly.
Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.
notes: Wear gloves when handling jalapeños to prevent skin irritation.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Chicken Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Potato and Chicken Salad is presented in a wide, shallow ceramic bowl, typical of a homely kitchen. It showcases a harmonious mix of creamy white diced potatoes (1.5 cm cubes), pale shredded chicken, bright orange carrot cubes (0.5 cm), vibrant green peas, golden corn kernels, and dark green chopped green beans (1 cm pieces). Finely diced red onion adds subtle flecks. All ingredients are coated in a rich, creamy mayonnaise dressing, with components naturally overlapping. Textures range from soft potatoes to tender-crisp vegetables. A generous sprinkle of grated Parmesan and fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple fork and a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm kitchen light illuminates the scene, evoking a relaxed family meal. The plate is adequately filled, reflecting the dish's generous, unpretentious character.
instructions: Cook chicken: Place chicken breast in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). This takes about 15-20 minutes. Remove chicken. Let cool. Shred or dice into small pieces.

Prepare potatoes: Dice peeled potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 8-10 minutes. Drain well. Let cool completely.

Prepare carrots and green beans: Dice carrots into small cubes (0.5 cm). Blanch diced carrots and green peas in boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Add green beans (trimmed, cut into 1 cm pieces) to the boiling water for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
Prepare corn: If using frozen corn, blanch briefly or thaw. If canned, drain well.
Combine ingredients: In a large bowl, gently combine cooled potatoes, shredded chicken, blanched carrots, green peas, corn kernels, green beans, and finely diced red onion.
Dress the salad: Add mayonnaise, grated Parmesan cheese, salt, and black pepper to the bowl. Gently fold until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Chill: Cover the bowl. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow flavors to meld.
Serve: Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Goat Cheese and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Goat Cheese and Mushroom Risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto maintains a creamy, fluid consistency, naturally spread on the plate, not in a rigid ring. Its color is a soft, creamy off-white from the goat cheese and rice, with earthy brown tones from the sautéed mushroom slices. Flecks of vibrant green chopped parsley are visible throughout. A small, artful pile of reserved sautéed mushroom slices is placed on top of the risotto. A final sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese complete the garnish. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, featuring standard silver flatware and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a minimal, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Serve with crusty Italian bread on the side.
instructions: Heat olive oil and 200g butter in a very large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until tender and browned, about 10-12 minutes. Remove about 1/4 of the mushrooms for garnish.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Toast rice for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Begin adding hot broth, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each ladleful to be mostly absorbed before adding the next.
Continue stirring and adding broth for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is al dente (creamy on outside, slightly firm in center).
Remove pot from heat. Stir in remaining 200g butter, crumbled goat cheese, and grated Parmesan cheese.
Stir vigorously for 2-3 minutes (mantecatura) until risotto is creamy and flowing.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.
notes: For best results when serving 42 people, consider preparing the risotto in large batches or multiple pots simultaneously.
Risotto is best consumed immediately after preparation to maintain its optimal creamy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl contains a vibrant mound of golden-hued short-grain rice. Two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs rest atop the rice, featuring a deeply seared, crispy bronze skin. Evenly distributed through the rice are 1cm cubes of charred red bell pepper and finely diced translucent onions. The rice is moist and slightly glossy from the olive oil and tomato reduction. Sprigs of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the dish. The plate sits on a rustic light oak table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy skin and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional shallow terracotta dish or paella pan
Accompany with a side of garlic aioli
Pair with a chilled glass of Spanish Albariño
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion and red pepper in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in grated tomato. Cook for 4 minutes until liquid evaporates.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Grate the tomatoes to remove skins easily while keeping the pulp

recipes.recipe_name: Cottage Cheese Gnudi, Brown Butter, Crispy Sage
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely composed portion of Cottage Cheese Gnudi rests on a pristine, oversized round bone china plate with a subtle, elegant pattern. Three to four plump, irregularly shaped golden-brown gnudi are nestled together, glistening with a rich amber brown butter sauce that pools subtly around them. Each gnudi shows a delicate, slightly textured exterior, hinting at its tender, melting interior. Strategically placed alongside are two or three vibrant green, crisp sage leaves, their edges slightly curled from frying. A scattering of toasted pine nuts adds a contrasting, warm brown hue and a touch of delicate crunch. A few sprigs of bright green microgreens provide a final flourish of fresh color and refined presentation. The plate is set on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, reflecting the dramatic, professional lighting that creates soft shadows and highlights the dish's contours. A polished silver fork and knife rest to the side, accompanied by a crisply folded white linen napkin, all contributing to an ultra-minimalist, high-end dining ambiance with abundant negative space.
instructions: Place cottage cheese in a fine-mesh sieve. Let drain for 1 hour or gently press out excess liquid. The drier the cheese, the better the gnudi texture.
In a bowl, combine drained cottage cheese, egg yolk, grated Parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Gradually fold in the plain flour until a soft, pliable dough forms. Do not overmix. The dough should be sticky but manageable.
Cover the bowl and chill the dough for at least 30 minutes. This helps firm the dough for shaping.
Lightly flour a clean surface. Scoop small portions of dough (about 15g each). Gently roll each portion into an oval or irregular dumpling shape. Aim for light, airy gnudi.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.
Carefully drop the gnudi into the simmering water in batches. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Cook gnudi for 3-5 minutes. They are done when they float to the surface and are tender through.

While gnudi cook, prepare the brown butter. In a small pan, melt unsalted butter over medium heat. Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until butter solids turn golden brown and smell nutty. Remove from heat immediately.
In a separate small pan, heat a teaspoon of the brown butter. Fry sage leaves for 30 seconds until crisp. Remove and drain on paper towel.
Toast pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer cooked gnudi directly from the water to the pan with brown butter. Gently toss to coat.

To plate, arrange 3-4 gnudi artfully on each warm plate. Drizzle generously with the brown butter. Place 2-3 crispy sage leaves beside the gnudi. Sprinkle toasted pine nuts. Garnish with a few delicate microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti Carbonara
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Spaghetti Carbonara is artfully twirled into a neat mound on a clean white porcelain plate. The pasta, glistening with a rich, creamy, golden-yellow emulsion, forms the central focus. Scattered generously over the spaghetti are crispy, golden-brown cubes of rendered guanciale, adding textural contrast and deep savory notes. A generous dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese blankets parts of the dish, creating a delicate white layer. Freshly cracked black pepper provides dark speckles across the creamy surface. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a classic silver fork and spoon placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the pasta's sheen and the guanciale's crisp edges. The overall presentation is refined yet inviting, embodying a modern bistro style with authentic Italian simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine or sparkling water.
Traditionally eaten with a fork, using a spoon to assist in twirling the pasta.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Dice guanciale into 1 cm cubes.
Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add diced guanciale. Cook slowly until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove crispy guanciale. Leave rendered fat in pan.
Cook spaghetti in boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
While pasta cooks, whisk egg yolks, whole egg, and 80 g grated Pecorino Romano in a bowl. Add half of the freshly ground black pepper.
Drain spaghetti. Add hot spaghetti directly to the pan with rendered guanciale fat. Toss to coat.
Immediately add egg mixture to spaghetti. Stir quickly and vigorously.
Gradually add reserved hot pasta water, 30 ml at a time, while stirring constantly. Continue until a creamy, emulsified sauce forms.
Add crispy guanciale back to the pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining grated Pecorino Romano and fresh black pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Red Snapper with Fennel-Pea Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared red snapper fillet, skin-side up, rests atop a vibrant, smooth green fennel-pea puree. The snapper's skin is deeply golden and crisp, contrasting with the moist, flaky white flesh. The puree forms a natural, flowing base, its bright green hue enhanced by fresh green peas scattered artfully around the plate. Thin, translucent slices of raw fennel are casually arranged near the fish, adding texture and a subtle white accent. Freshly chopped bright green parsley and a sprinkle of yellow lemon zest provide a final burst of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: A light white wine (e.g., Vermentino or Sauvignon Blanc)
Crusty bread for dipping in puree
instructions: Prepare fennel. Halve fennel bulbs. Slice one bulb thinly for garnish. Dice remaining fennel into small cubes.
Blanch green peas. Bring a pot of salted water to boil. Add peas. Cook 2 minutes. Drain. Plunge into ice bath. Drain again.
Make fennel-pea puree. In a saucepan, heat 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced fennel. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Add half blanched peas and 120 ml vegetable broth to saucepan. Simmer 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in 15g butter.
Transfer fennel-pea mixture to a blender. Add half chopped parsley. Add juice of half lemon. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare snapper. Pat snapper fillets dry. Score skin several times with a sharp knife. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Sear snapper. Heat remaining 45 ml olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Place snapper fillets skin-side down. Press gently with a spatula for 30 seconds to ensure even searing.
Cook skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown. Flesh should be cooked halfway up.
Flip fillets. Cook 2-3 minutes more until fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Plate the dish. Spoon a generous amount of fennel-pea puree onto the center of each plate. Place one seared red snapper fillet, skin-side up, on top of the puree.

Garnish. Sprinkle remaining blanched peas around the plate. Arrange a few thin slices of raw fennel beside the fish. Garnish with remaining chopped parsley and lemon zest. Drizzle lightly with extra virgin olive oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Chicken and Carrot Consommé with Egg Cloud
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, clear golden consommé fills a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Tender, unsliced chicken chunks rest at the bottom, complemented by vibrant orange julienned carrots. Delicate, ethereal strands of whisked egg float gracefully within the broth, creating a soft, cloud-like texture. The soup's surface is lightly scattered with bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh aromatic contrast. The bowl is positioned centrally on a simple light wooden table surface. A polished silver soup spoon rests to the right of the bowl. A neatly folded crisp white cotton napkin is placed to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the clarity of the broth and the distinct colors of the ingredients. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel carrots. Julienne carrots into thin matchsticks (about 4 cm long). Set aside.
Finely dice onion and celery (mirepoix).
In a large pot, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion and celery. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Do not brown.
Add chicken stock, parsley sprigs, and thyme sprigs to the pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat. Simmer 15 minutes to infuse flavors.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Discard solids. This creates a clear consommé base.
Bring the strained consommé to a gentle simmer. Add diced chicken cubes. Poach chicken 5-7 minutes, or until cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from broth. Set aside.
Add julienned carrots to the simmering consommé. Cook 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Crack eggs into a small bowl. Lightly whisk with a fork until just combined. Do not over-whisk.

Slowly pour the whisked eggs into the gently simmering consommé in a thin stream, stirring continuously with a fork or chopsticks in a circular motion. This creates fine egg ribbons or a delicate egg cloud.
Return poached chicken cubes to the consommé. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot consommé into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Carrot and Chicken Velouté with Soft-Boiled Egg
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, smooth orange velouté fills a deep, pristine white porcelain soup bowl. Tender, shredded chicken pieces are nestled centrally within the soup, providing a contrasting lighter hue. A perfectly halved soft-boiled egg, revealing a creamy, golden-orange yolk, is carefully placed atop the chicken. A delicate swirl of golden-brown butter glistens on the soup's surface, adding a rich sheen. Finely chopped fresh green chives are scattered over the egg and soup, offering a pop of fresh color. The bowl rests on a rustic wooden table, accompanied by a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin and a classic polished silver soup spoon. Natural, soft ambient lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel and roughly chop carrots. Toss with olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.

Meanwhile, poach chicken. Place chicken breast in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from liquid. Shred into small pieces.
In a large pot, melt 30g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add roasted carrots, chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf from the pot. Carefully transfer soup mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. Return soup to the pot.
Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm over low heat.

Prepare soft-boiled eggs. Bring a small pot of water to a rolling boil. Carefully lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for 6-7 minutes for a soft, jammy yolk. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Peel eggs. Halve each egg lengthwise.
Make brown butter. In a small saucepan, melt remaining 30g butter over medium heat. Cook, swirling occasionally, until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Be careful not to burn.

To serve, ladle soup into four bowls. Arrange shredded chicken in the center of each bowl. Place two egg halves on top of the chicken. Drizzle brown butter over the soup and egg. Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives.
notes: For best flavor, ensure carrots are well-caramelized during roasting.
Submerge soft-boiled eggs immediately in ice water for easier peeling.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Fricassée aux Carottes Glacées
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown chicken thigh, perfectly seared and braised, rests on a generous pool of glossy, creamy white sauce. Bright orange carrots, cut into 2cm thick oblique slices, are neatly arranged alongside the chicken. A vibrant scattering of chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of green over the dish. The sauce pools elegantly around the chicken, highlighting its tender texture. The dish is presented on a clean, classic white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple rustic wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and polished traditional flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, suggesting a relaxed bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the rich sauce
Pair with a glass of dry white wine
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil and 20g butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown, 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Stir in flour. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in white wine, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Gradually whisk in chicken stock. Add thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to pot. Cover. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
While chicken simmers, prepare carrots. Peel carrots. Cut into 2cm thick oblique slices.
In a separate saucepan, melt 30g butter. Add carrots and 60ml water. Season with salt.
Cover. Cook over medium heat until water evaporates and carrots are tender-crisp and glazed, 10-12 minutes. Shake pan occasionally.
Remove chicken from pot. Keep warm. Discard thyme and bay leaf.
In a small bowl, whisk egg yolks and heavy cream.
Slowly whisk a ladleful of hot sauce into egg yolk mixture to temper.
Pour tempered mixture back into pot, whisking constantly.
Cook sauce over low heat, stirring, until slightly thickened. Do not boil. Stir in remaining 30g butter until melted. Season with salt and pepper.
Return chicken to sauce. Serve immediately with glazed carrots. Garnish with fresh parsley.
traditional_techniques: Liaison (thickening and enriching sauce with egg yolks and cream)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Carrot Puree and Glazed Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken Breast is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A vibrant orange, smooth carrot puree is smeared across one side. Two to three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast pieces are neatly arranged on the puree. A small cluster of glossy, tender-crisp glazed carrot batons are carefully placed alongside the chicken. A perfectly halved jammy egg, revealing its soft, pale yellow yolk, sits next to the chicken. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh green parsley or chives. The overall presentation is professional, approachable, and balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a clean cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the food, creating an inviting bistro ambiance.
instructions: Prepare carrot puree: Peel 350g carrots. Cut into 2 cm chunks. Place in a saucepan. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Transfer to a food processor. Add 30g butter and 50ml chicken stock. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare glazed carrots: Peel remaining 150g carrots. Cut into 1 cm thick batons. Heat 20g butter in a small pan over medium heat. Add carrot batons. Sauté for 2 minutes. Add 100ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid reduces and carrots are tender-crisp and glossy, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Cook eggs: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil. Carefully lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for exactly 6.5 minutes for jammy yolks. Immediately transfer eggs to an ice bath. Let cool for 2 minutes. Peel carefully.

Cook chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Heat 30g butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once butter is melted and sizzling, add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes. Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick pieces.

Plate the dish: Spoon a generous smear of warm carrot puree onto one side of each white dinner plate. Arrange sliced chicken pieces neatly over the puree. Place glazed carrot batons alongside the chicken. Halve each peeled egg lengthwise. Place one egg half, cut-side up, on each plate. Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley or chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Roasted Carrots, Herbed Butter Sauce, and Soft-Boiled Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden brown with a slight crust, sits centrally on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a neat pile of roasted carrot batons, vibrant orange with lightly caramelized edges. A soft-boiled egg, halved lengthwise, reveals a rich, jammy yellow yolk, positioned next to the carrots. A glistening, pale yellow herbed butter sauce is spooned over the chicken and carrots, creating a subtle sheen. Fresh green specks of parsley and chives are visible within the sauce and as a light garnish. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded light grey cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. Traditional European-style flatware (fork and knife) are neatly placed beside the plate. Lighting is natural, even, and bright.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel carrots. Cut carrots into 5cm long batons. Toss carrots with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.

Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for exactly 6.5 minutes for a soft-boiled yolk. Immediately transfer eggs to an ice bath for 5 minutes. Peel carefully.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from oven. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

While chicken rests, return skillet to medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Deglaze with chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits. Add butter, lemon juice, chopped parsley, and chives. Whisk until butter is melted and sauce is emulsified. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Place one roasted chicken breast on each plate. Arrange a portion of roasted carrots next to the chicken. Halve one soft-boiled egg lengthwise and place beside the carrots. Spoon herbed butter sauce generously over chicken and carrots.
notes: The sauce can be adjusted with more lemon juice for brightness or more herbs for stronger flavor.
Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C.
The soft-boiled egg provides a rich, creamy element that complements the savory chicken and carrots.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Fricassee with Glazed Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic French Chicken Fricassee is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, succulent chunks of chicken, seared to a light golden hue, are nestled within a rich, velvety white sauce. The sauce, thickened with a delicate egg yolk liaison, gleams with a creamy sheen. Alongside the chicken, vibrant orange carrot batons, gently glazed in butter, provide a contrasting pop of color and subtle sweetness. Quartered cremini mushrooms are interspersed throughout the fricassee, adding earthy notes. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley, providing a final touch of green and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, not overly geometric. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and warm colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce
Serve alongside simple egg noodles or steamed rice
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Melt 30 g butter in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add another 20 g butter to the pot. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Stir well and cook for 2 minutes, forming a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken stock, ensuring no lumps. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

While chicken simmers, prepare carrots. Cut carrots into 1 cm x 4 cm batons. Melt 15 g butter in a separate pan over medium heat. Add carrot batons and a splash of water (about 30 ml). Season with salt. Cover and cook until tender-crisp and lightly glazed, about 8-10 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together heavy cream and egg yolks to create a liaison.

Remove pot from heat. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Gradually whisk a ladleful of the hot sauce into the liaison. Then, slowly pour the tempered liaison back into the pot, whisking constantly until sauce slightly thickens. Do not boil after adding liaison.
Stir in chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken fricassee immediately with glazed carrots alongside.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not boil the fricassee after adding the egg yolk liaison, as this can cause the sauce to curdle.

recipes.recipe_name: Jajangbap (Black Bean Sauce Rice)
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rich black bean sauce generously coats a bed of fluffy white short-grain rice, centrally plated in a clean, white ceramic bowl. The sauce, a glossy dark brown, holds substantial diced pork belly, tender diced potatoes, diced zucchini, and diced onions, all cooked until softened but holding their shape. The dish presents a striking contrast of the dark, savory sauce against the pristine white rice. Garnished with bright green julienned cucumber and thinly sliced scallions, providing a fresh, crisp counterpoint. The presentation is clean, with moderate negative space. Served on a simple light wooden table with a side of traditional Korean danmuji (pickled yellow radish) and a metal spoon, under natural, even lighting. The scene captures an authentic Korean casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with danmuji (pickled yellow radish) on the side.
Accompany with kimchi.
Optionally, top with a fried egg.
instructions: Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large pot or wok over medium heat. Add diced pork belly. Stir-fry until browned and cooked through. Remove pork, set aside.
In the same pot, add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil. Add chunjang. Stir-fry the chunjang for 2-3 minutes, pressing it against the bottom of the pot to break it up. This removes bitterness.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add diced potato and zucchini. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return cooked pork to the pot. Add sugar and soy sauce. Stir well to combine.
Pour in water or chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 30 ml water to create a slurry. Gradually stir slurry into the simmering sauce until thickened to desired consistency. Continue simmering for 1 minute.
Serve hot over individual portions of cooked short-grain white rice. Garnish each serving with julienned cucumber and sliced scallions.

recipes.recipe_name: Entremet de Cigalas con Tomate Dulce y Espuma de Idiazábal
recipes.visual_description: This elegant entremet presents a pristine rectangular block of delicate, pale pink cigala mousse, precisely molded with a smooth, velvety texture. It is topped with a translucent, ruby-red layer of sweet tomato gelée, offering a vibrant color contrast and subtle shimmer. A delicate, golden-brown caramelized onion crisp, intricately shaped, crowns the entremet, providing an ethereal, savory-sweet crunch. Beside it, a cloud-like quenelle of pure white, subtly sweet Idiazábal espuma rests, its airy texture a counterpoint to the structured layers. A single, vibrant green micro basil leaf is precisely placed atop the espuma. The dish is presented on a minimalist, pristine white porcelain plate with a wide rim, leaving generous negative space around the central composition. Elements are arranged with geometric precision, emphasizing clean lines and sophisticated simplicity, under dramatic professional lighting with soft shadows.
instructions: Prepare Cigalas Mousse: Boil cigalas for 2 minutes. Cool. Extract tail meat. Reserve shells for stock. Finely mince cigala meat.
Make Cigala Stock: Sauté reserved cigala shells with a quarter of the red onion. Add 500ml water. Simmer 20 minutes. Strain. Reduce to 100ml. Season lightly.

Bloom 2 gelatin sheets in cold water. Dissolve in warm cigala stock. Combine with minced cigala meat. Fold in 50ml lightly whipped cream. Press into a 15x15 cm square mold, 1 cm thick. Chill 2 hours until firm.

Prepare Sweet Tomato Gelée: Dice tomatoes. Simmer with 25g sugar and 15ml olive oil until soft. Pass through a fine sieve to get clear juice. Add 1g agar-agar. Bring to boil, simmer 1 minute. Pour a 0.5 cm layer over chilled cigala mousse. Chill 1 hour until firm.

Prepare Caramelized Onion Crisp: Thinly slice remaining red onion. Slowly caramelize in 15ml olive oil until very dark and sweet (about 45 minutes). Puree. Spread very thinly on a silpat-lined baking sheet. Bake at 120°C (250°F) for 30-40 minutes until crisp. Cool. Break into elegant shards.

Prepare Sweet Idiazábal Espuma: Dice Idiazábal cheese. Gently heat 150ml cream with 25g sugar until cheese melts. Strain through a fine sieve. Bloom remaining 2 gelatin sheets. Dissolve in warm cheese mixture. Pour into a siphon. Charge with N2O. Chill 1 hour.

Assemble: Cut the chilled entremet block into 4 precise 7.5x5 cm rectangles. Place one rectangle on each plate. Dispense a quenelle of Idiazábal espuma beside the entremet. Garnish with a caramelized onion crisp shard and a single micro basil leaf or chive baton. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Seared Artichokes and Lemon-Oregano
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Orecchiette with Seared Artichokes and Lemon-Oregano is presented in a shallow, matte white porcelain bowl. The orecchiette pasta, a pale yellow, is loosely mounded in the center, allowing the sauce to cling to its cup-like shape. Golden-brown, seared artichoke halves and quarters are interspersed throughout the pasta, with some resting prominently on top, showcasing their slightly caramelized edges. Thinly sliced garlic and flecks of vibrant red pepper flakes are visible, adding visual interest. Fresh, bright green chopped oregano leaves are generously scattered over the dish, with some lemon zest grated over top, providing pops of color and texture. A subtle sheen of olive oil coats the pasta, indicating a well-emulsified sauce. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space around the pasta. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded natural cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the flavorful sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Dry white wine or vegetable broth

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add orecchiette pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add drained and halved artichoke hearts. Sear for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and slightly crispy on the edges.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes to the skillet. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Do not burn garlic.
Pour in white wine or vegetable broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 1 minute.
Drain pasta, reserving 250 ml of pasta cooking water.

Add cooked orecchiette, lemon juice, half of the fresh oregano, and 125 ml of reserved pasta water to the skillet. Toss vigorously to combine, creating a light sauce. Add more pasta water as needed to achieve desired consistency.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh oregano, lemon zest, and optional plant-based parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Bistro Surf & Turf with Coffee-Chocolate Jus, Lemon-Clam Pasta, and Cheesy Potato Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is plated on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a refined yet approachable bistro style. A bed of lemon-clam linguine, with its vibrant red cherry tomato halves and dark Kalamata olives, forms the base on one side. Nestled beside the pasta are a golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast and a perfectly seared beef medallion, both glistening with a rich, dark coffee-chocolate jus. The jus, a deep reddish-brown, pools subtly around the meats. Three crisp, golden-brown potato croquettes, cylindrical and lightly textured from frying, are arranged artfully on the plate. A small, fresh pile of mixed salad greens, dressed simply, adds a touch of vibrant green and freshness. A thin lemon slice provides a bright yellow accent. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of each component.
instructions: Prepare Potato Croquettes: Boil peeled potatoes until tender. Drain well. Mash potatoes thoroughly. Heat milk and margarine in a small saucepan until melted. Add to mashed potatoes with grated cheese, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Let cool slightly. Form into 12 small cylindrical croquettes.

Cook Pasta and Clams: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add linguine; cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100ml pasta water. In a large pan, heat 15ml olive oil. Add 2 minced garlic cloves and half the diced shallot; sauté 1 minute. Add clams and 60ml reserved pasta water. Cover and steam until clams open (discard any unopened). Remove clams, keep warm.

Prepare Coffee-Chocolate Jus: In the same clam pan (or a clean saucepan), add 15ml olive oil, remaining shallot, and 1 minced garlic clove. Sauté 2 minutes. Deglaze with apple cider vinegar. Add chicken stock, espresso, and chopped dark chocolate. Simmer, stirring, until chocolate melts and sauce reduces slightly to a glaze consistency. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook Chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from pan, rest 5 minutes.
Cook Beef: In the same skillet, add 15ml olive oil. Season beef medallions with salt and pepper. Sear beef 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Remove from pan, rest 5 minutes.

Finish Pasta: To the clam pan (or a clean pan), add drained pasta, halved cherry tomatoes, pitted Kalamata olives, juice of half a lemon, and chopped parsley. Toss to combine. If too dry, add a splash of reserved pasta water. Stir in clams.
Cook Croquettes: Heat 30ml olive oil in a separate skillet over medium heat. Fry potato croquettes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels.

Assemble Plate: Place a portion of lemon-clam pasta on one side of each plate. Arrange 1 chicken breast piece and 1 beef medallion next to the pasta. Drizzle meats generously with the coffee-chocolate jus. Place 3 potato croquettes strategically on the plate. Garnish with a small mound of mixed salad greens and a lemon slice.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Indian Chicken and Potato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spicy Indian Chicken and Potato Curry rests in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The rich, reddish-brown curry sauce envelops tender, 3-4 cm cubed chicken pieces, along with softened 2 cm potato chunks and 1.5 cm carrot chunks. The ingredients are naturally arranged, with some pieces partially submerged and others peeking through the vibrant sauce. A light sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped green coriander leaves adds a pop of contrasting color. The bowl is accompanied by a simple metal spoon. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen light, creating a lived-in, comforting atmosphere, with a glimpse of a plain white cloth napkin or paper towel casually placed nearby. A side of fluffy basmati rice in a smaller, matching bowl is partially visible, completing the authentic, homely presentation.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 400 g, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 200 g, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add chopped onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in red chili powder, turmeric, ground cumin, and ground coriander. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add chicken cubes to the pot. Brown chicken on all sides for 3-5 minutes.
Pour in chopped tomatoes and water or stock. Add potatoes and carrots. Stir well.
Bring the curry to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes.
Check chicken for doneness (internal temperature 75°C) and vegetables for tenderness. Cook longer if needed.
Stir in garam masala and salt. Cook for 2 more minutes.
Remove from heat. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Kissed Beef Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coffee-Kissed Beef Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The risotto is free-flowing and creamy, a rich, warm beige color, with visible specks of finely diced onion and sliced cremini mushrooms. Nestled atop the risotto are several golden-brown, seared beef tenderloin chunks, approximately 3cm cubes, showcasing a beautiful crust from precise searing. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the beef and risotto. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits beside a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its comforting textures and inviting warmth. The background is a soft blur of a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Cut beef tenderloin into 3cm cubes. Season beef generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear beef cubes on all sides until well browned. Remove beef from pan. Set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic. Slice the cremini mushrooms.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Combine hot coffee, hot milk, and hot beef broth in a separate saucepan. Keep warm over low heat.
Add 120 ml of the hot liquid mixture to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding hot liquid, 120 ml at a time, stirring constantly until each addition is absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
The risotto is ready when the rice is creamy but still firm to the bite (al dente).
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy.
Season risotto with salt and black pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Gently fold seared beef cubes into the risotto or place them on top when serving.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle Coffee Pork Loin with Creamy Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features thick medallions of coffee-rubbed pork loin, boasting a rich, dark sear and tender interior. The pork is artfully arranged on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A luscious, creamy chipotle-coffee sauce, a deep reddish-brown hue, is generously spooned over the pork and around the plate, creating a pool of flavor. The sauce's smooth texture contrasts with the pork's slight crust. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped cilantro leaves garnishes the pork, adding a pop of green. Beside the plate, a small, neatly stacked trio of warm corn tortillas suggests traditional accompaniment. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table and natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's warmth and inviting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Side of Mexican rice
Refried beans
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Pat pork loin dry. Combine ground coffee, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, 1.5 teaspoons salt, and 0.5 teaspoon black pepper for the rub. Rub mixture evenly over pork loin.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until browned, about 6-8 minutes total.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Remove pork from pan. Rest pork 10 minutes before slicing.
For the sauce, drain excess fat from the pan if needed. Add finely diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and minced chipotle. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in brewed coffee and chicken broth. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of pan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Simmer 5 minutes.

Stir in milk and hot sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer. In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with cold water to create a slurry. Whisk slurry into the simmering sauce. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested pork loin into thick medallions. Arrange pork on serving plates. Spoon generous amount of creamy chipotle-coffee sauce over pork. Garnish with fresh, chopped cilantro.
notes: Adjust chipotle and hot sauce quantity to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork and Kidney Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of the hearty Spicy Pork and Kidney Bean Stew is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl with a moderate rim. The deep reddish-brown stew, rich and glossy, fills the bowl, showcasing tender, braised pork chunks (2.5 cm cubes) alongside plump, whole kidney beans. Vibrant green tatsoi leaves, lightly wilted, are gently folded throughout, providing a fresh textural and color contrast. A dollop of bright white sour cream rests on top, its cool creaminess beginning to melt into the warm stew. The bowl sits on a light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded plain white cotton napkin and a simple fork and spoon are placed beside it. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors against a subtly blurred casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside steamed white rice to absorb the rich sauce.
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork cubes in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chili bean paste and Sriracha sauce. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return seared pork to the pot. Pour in coconut vinegar, milk, and water or chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until pork is very tender.
Stir in rinsed kidney beans. Continue to simmer for 5 minutes.
Add chopped tatsoi. Cook for 2-3 minutes until tatsoi is just wilted.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with a dollop of sour cream.
notes: Ensure pork is cooked until very tender for best results.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Vegetable Makloubeh
recipes.visual_description: Chicken and Vegetable Makloubeh is presented on a large, round white ceramic platter, forming an impressive dome. The golden-brown chicken pieces, cooked to perfection, are prominently displayed on top, nestled among tender, vibrant vegetables. Slices of roasted bell pepper, tomato, and onion in various shades of red, green, and translucent white create a mosaic of color and texture. The golden turmeric-infused basmati rice, fluffy and aromatic, forms the base, with some grains peeking out from beneath the vegetables. Potato rounds, caramelized on the edges, are visible throughout. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley and toasted pine nuts adds a final touch of color and crunch. The dish is centrally placed, allowing for negative space. A simple patterned napkin is folded beside the platter. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's warmth and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with plain yogurt or a simple cucumber-tomato salad on the side.
Traditionally eaten communally from a large platter, allowing diners to serve themselves.
A common main dish for family gatherings and celebrations.
instructions: Rinse basmati rice thoroughly until water runs clear. Soak rice in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain well.
Slice potatoes, tomatoes, and bell pepper into 5mm thick rounds. Slice onion into rings. Dice celery into 1cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt, pepper, and 5g ground allspice.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot (approx 24-26cm diameter). Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pot. Fry potato rounds until golden on both sides. Remove.
Lightly fry bell pepper, onion rings, celery, and minced garlic in the same pot until softened. Remove.
Arrange tomato slices in a single layer on the bottom of the pot. Place fried potato rounds over tomatoes.
Distribute fried bell pepper, onion, and celery over the potatoes.
Place seared chicken pieces evenly over the vegetables.
Evenly spread the drained rice over the chicken and vegetables.
In a separate bowl, whisk chicken stock with remaining 10g ground allspice, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and turmeric. Season with salt and pepper.
Carefully pour the seasoned chicken stock over the rice. Ensure rice is just covered by liquid. If needed, add a little more hot water.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove pot from heat. Let rest, covered, for 10-15 minutes.

Place a large, round serving platter upside down over the pot. Firmly hold pot and platter together. Carefully and confidently flip the pot over onto the platter. Lift the pot slowly, allowing Makloubeh to release onto the platter.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and toasted pine nuts.
notes: The success of Makloubeh lies in the proper layering and the dramatic 'flip'.
Ensure the rice is cooked perfectly to avoid sticking. Do not stir the rice once the liquid is added.
traditional_techniques: Layering ingredients for distinct flavors and textures.
The 'flip' (Makloubeh) as a unique presentation method.
Seasoning with traditional Middle Eastern spices like allspice and cinnamon.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Corn and Black Tea Baked Custard with Clementine Zest
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sweet Corn and Black Tea Baked Custard is presented in a white, slightly imperfect ceramic ramekin on a rustic wooden dining table.
