Carefully unmold the frozen cherry-verjus confit insert. Place it centrally on top of the mousse layer.
Pour remaining robiola-kewra mousse over the confit, spreading to cover completely. Tap gently.
Freeze entremet for at least 6-8 hours, or preferably overnight, until completely solid.
Once entremet is completely frozen, prepare a wire rack over a large tray.
Unmold the frozen entremet. Place it on the wire rack.
Pour the cooled glaze (30-35°C) evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess glaze drip off.
Carefully transfer the glazed entremet to a serving platter. Refrigerate for 3-4 hours to thaw completely.
To serve, use a hot, sharp knife to cut precise slices. Garnish each slice with a halved candied cherry.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are high quality for best results.
Freezing the entremet thoroughly before glazing is crucial for a smooth mirror glaze finish.
Use an immersion blender for the glaze to achieve a perfectly smooth, bubble-free consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pork & Pickled Onion Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve elegant, bite-sized canapés are artfully arranged on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood serving board. Each piece features a thin, golden-brown sourdough crisp as its base. Crowned upon the crisp is a rustic, tender chunk of confit pork belly, its surface glistening slightly. Vibrant, thinly sliced quick-pickled red onions are delicately draped over the pork, providing a striking purple contrast. A glossy, amber drizzle of verjus gastrique subtly adorns each canapé. The ensemble is sparingly garnished with tiny, bright green microgreens or finely chopped chives, adding a fresh pop of color and texture. The presentation is clean and minimalist, allowing ample negative space. The board sits on a light bamboo table, accompanied by a natural undyed linen napkin, under soft, diffused natural lighting. The background is clean and unobtrusive, hinting at natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sophisticated appetizer for a gathering
Present on a large, communal platter for sharing

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, skin on or off, cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Season pork belly cubes generously with sea salt and fresh black pepper. Place in a small oven-safe pot with bay leaf and 2 thyme sprigs. Cover completely with duck fat or olive oil. Cook in an oven preheated to 140°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let cool slightly in fat, then remove pork pieces and set aside. Reserve fat for future use.

Combine apple cider vinegar, water, granulated sugar, and 5g sea salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Add thinly sliced red onion to the hot liquid. Let steep for at least 30 minutes, or until onions are vibrant pink and slightly softened. Drain onions before use.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Arrange sourdough baguette slices on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Let cool completely.

In a small saucepan, combine verjus with 1-2 teaspoons of granulated sugar (adjust to taste for balance). Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Reduce by half, until slightly syrupy. This is the verjus gastrique. Keep warm.

To assemble, place a crisp sourdough slice on a serving platter. Top each crisp with a rustic chunk of confit pork belly. Drape a small cluster of pickled red onion over the pork. Drizzle a small amount of the verjus gastrique over each canapé. Garnish with fresh microgreens or finely chopped chives. Arrange 8-12 pieces on a platter.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using preservation techniques (confit, pickling) and minimizing food waste. Consider sourcing ingredients locally and seasonally.
The reserved duck fat from the confit can be strained and reused for other cooking.
Adjust sugar in the verjus gastrique to balance the acidity of the verjus to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Hand-Rolled Tagliolini with Poached Lobster, Saffron, and Bottarga
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant portion of hand-rolled golden tagliolini forms a delicate, free-flowing nest, centrally placed on a pristine white bone china plate. Three to four succulent, bright orange chunks of perfectly poached lobster, each approximately 3-4 cm, are artfully arranged around the pasta, slightly nestled within its curves. A delicate, glossy saffron-infused butter sauce pools subtly at the base of the pasta, reflecting light. A whisper of finely grated golden bottarga dusts over the lobster and tagliolini, adding a subtle texture. A few bright green, precisely cut 1 cm chive batons are scattered sparingly and intentionally for color and freshness, enhancing the minimalist composition. The arrangement is organic and flowing, emphasizing abundant negative space on the large white plate. The plate rests on a cool, polished white Carrara marble surface. A single, heavy silver fork and knife with a minimalist design are positioned to the right. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits to the left. Dramatic, focused overhead lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's refined textures and vibrant colors. The background is an ultra-minimalist, softly blurred charcoal grey, ensuring the dish remains the sole focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp, dry Italian white wine, such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
Present on traditional Italian fine porcelain plates.
instructions: Prepare lobster stock: Submerge live lobsters in rapidly boiling salted water. Cook for 5 minutes. Remove lobsters. Immediately plunge into ice bath. Once chilled, carefully remove tail and claw meat. Reserve shells.

Chop lobster shells into small pieces. Sauté shells in a pot with a drizzle of olive oil until fragrant. Add minced shallots and crushed garlic. Cook until softened. Deglaze with white wine. Reduce by half. Add vegetable broth. Simmer for 20 minutes. Strain stock, pressing solids. Reduce stock until intensely flavorful, approximately 150ml. Keep warm.

Make tagliolini dough: On a clean surface, create a well with 00 flour. Place egg yolks and whole egg in the center. Gradually incorporate flour into eggs using a fork. Knead dough for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in cling film. Rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.

Roll and cut tagliolini: Divide dough into four portions. Roll each portion very thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin, achieving a thickness of 1mm. Dust lightly with flour. Fold dough sheets. Cut into fine tagliolini strands, approximately 2mm wide. Unfurl strands. Dust with semolina to prevent sticking.

Prepare saffron butter sauce: Bloom saffron threads in a tablespoon of warm lobster stock for 5 minutes. In a wide pan, combine remaining warm lobster stock with bloomed saffron. Bring to a gentle simmer. Gradually whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, to create a smooth, emulsified sauce. Do not boil. Season with salt and pepper.

Poach lobster meat: Gently poach reserved lobster tail and claw meat in the saffron butter sauce for 2-3 minutes until just cooked through and tender. Do not overcook. Remove lobster meat. Cut into 3-4 cm chunks.
Cook tagliolini: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Add fresh tagliolini. Cook for 2-3 minutes until al dente. Reserve 50ml pasta water.

Finish dish: Transfer cooked tagliolini directly into the saffron butter sauce. Add a splash of reserved pasta water. Toss gently to coat, emulsifying the sauce (manteca). The sauce should cling to the pasta. Add lobster chunks. Toss briefly to warm through.

Plate: Divide tagliolini into four individual portions, creating a neat nest on the center of each plate. Arrange lobster chunks artfully around and slightly tucked into the pasta. Finely grate bottarga generously over the dish. Garnish with finely cut chive batons. Serve immediately.
notes: Use only the freshest live lobsters for optimal flavor and texture.
The key to the sauce is a precise emulsion; ensure butter is cold and added gradually.
Do not overcook the lobster; it should remain tender and succulent.
Fresh pasta cooks very quickly; monitor closely to achieve perfect al dente texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Uni Cacio e Pepe with Shaved Bottarga
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly formed, compact nest of glistening, golden tonnarelli pasta, precisely twirled and centered on a pristine white bone china plate. The pasta exhibits a rich, creamy sheen from the emulsified Pecorino and black pepper sauce, revealing subtle dark pepper flecks. Two plump, vibrant orange-yellow lobes of fresh uni are strategically placed, their delicate texture contrasting with the smooth pasta. Thin, translucent, amber-hued shavings of bottarga delicately rest over the uni and pasta. A minimal drizzle of bright green extra virgin olive oil creates a subtle sheen. The composition is organic and flowing. The dish is presented on a cool grey-veined Carrara marble surface. The large bone china plate allows maximum negative space. A single, perfectly folded white linen napkin lies to the left. Dramatic lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting textures. The background is minimalist, showcasing a single, refined individual portion.
instructions: Cook tonnarelli pasta in generously salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 250ml of the pasta cooking water.
In a large pan, toast freshly cracked black peppercorns over medium heat until fragrant. Remove from heat.
Add 100ml of reserved pasta water to the pan with the toasted peppercorns. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Gradually add finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese, stirring vigorously to create a smooth, creamy emulsion. Add more pasta water, a tablespoon at a time, if needed to achieve a silky sauce consistency. This is the 'mantecare' technique.
Drain the cooked tonnarelli. Add it directly to the sauce pan. Toss vigorously to coat the pasta evenly with the creamy sauce.
Divide the pasta into four individual portions, twirling each neatly onto the center of a plate.
Arrange 2-3 fresh uni lobes elegantly on top of each pasta portion.
Grate or shave thin slices of bottarga generously over the uni and pasta.
Drizzle each dish with a few drops of high-quality extra virgin olive oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Mushroom and Gruyère Bread Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A generous square portion of golden-brown Savory Mushroom and Gruyère Bread Pudding is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The surface is rustic, showing crisp edges of bread cubes and melted Gruyère. The interior reveals soft, custardy bread cubes interspersed with dark, earthy caramelized onions and browned mushrooms. The color palette is warm, with golden crusts, deep browns, and creamy off-white. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a pop of color. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting textures. The background suggests a cozy, modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add thinly sliced onion. Cook slowly until deeply caramelized, about 15-20 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Increase heat slightly. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and thyme leaves. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, and cream. Season with salt and pepper.
Add 2-3 cm bread cubes, sautéed mushroom-onion mixture, and grated Gruyère to the egg mixture. Toss gently to combine. Ensure all bread is coated.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish. Press down gently to ensure even distribution.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until golden brown and set. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Eggplant Velouté, Wild Mushrooms, Parmesan Air, and Pasta Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated starter on a large, matte white ceramic plate. A lustrous, deep aubergine-colored smoked eggplant velouté forms a natural, organic swirl slightly off-center. Nestled within and around the velouté are earthy brown and golden roasted wild mushrooms, showcasing varied shapes and seared edges. A scattering of dark red and black sun-dried tomato and Kalamata olive crumble adds textural contrast and concentrated flavor. An ethereal, light ivory cloud of Parmesan air floats delicately atop the velouté. Two golden-brown, irregularly shaped, thin, crispy pasta shards stand upright, adding height and crisp texture. A single, vibrant green microgreen sprig provides a precise, fresh garnish. The plate is surrounded by abundant negative space, highlighting the architectural precision of the composition. The setting features a pristine white Carrara marble surface, a precisely folded white linen napkin, and modern, high-end silver flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the textures and sophisticated colors of the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve eggplants lengthwise. Score flesh. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper.

Roast eggplants cut-side down for 30-40 minutes until very tender and slightly charred. Scoop flesh into a bowl. Add a few drops liquid smoke if desired. Blend with 20ml olive oil until silky smooth. Pass through a fine sieve. Season. Keep warm.

Clean mushrooms. Cut larger ones into thick slices or bite-sized pieces. Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms. Sear until golden and tender. Add minced garlic and 2 thyme sprigs. Cook 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper.

Finely dice sun-dried tomatoes and Kalamata olives. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake at 100°C for 30-45 minutes until dried and crumbly. Pulse briefly in a food processor for finer crumble. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Combine 30g finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano with 100ml vegetable broth. Heat gently until Parmigiano melts. Do not boil. Strain through a fine sieve. Cool slightly. Whisk in 1g soy lecithin. Use an immersion blender at an angle to create a stable foam on the surface.
Cut fresh lasagna sheet into small, irregular shards. Fry in neutral oil at 170°C until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels. Lightly salt.

Spoon a dollop of smoked eggplant velouté slightly off-center on each plate. Swirl gently. Arrange a few roasted mushroom pieces artfully on the velouté. Sprinkle sun-dried tomato and olive crumble beside the mushrooms. Gently spoon a cloud of Parmigiano air on top of the velouté. Place one or two crispy pasta shards upright. Garnish with a tiny microgreen sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Mexican Beef Picadillo
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Mexican Beef Picadillo is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim, reflecting everyday use. The rich, reddish-brown beef mince, cooked to a tender consistency, is mixed with distinct 1 cm cubes of tender potatoes and carrots, and bright green peas. The picadillo fills the bowl adequately, allowing its natural textures and colors to show. A small, casual pile of fluffy white rice sits beside the bowl on a well-worn wooden dining table. A few warm, soft corn tortillas, lightly browned, are folded and placed nearby. A small, simple bowl of vibrant red salsa is visible in the background, along with a lime wedge. The scene is lit by warm, inviting kitchen light, creating a cozy, lived-in family dining atmosphere. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, showcasing comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Accompany with white rice.
Offer a side of simple salsa or pickled jalapeños.
instructions: Dice potatoes and carrots into 1 cm cubes. Dice onion, garlic, and red bell pepper finely.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add beef mince. Cook, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, garlic, and bell pepper to the pot with the beef. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in ground cumin, dried oregano, and chili powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes, carrots, canned diced tomatoes, and beef broth to the pot. Stir well.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Stir in frozen peas. Cook for 3-5 minutes until heated through.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove from heat.
Stir in fresh chopped coriander just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Cheek with Fermented Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial portion of slow-cooked beef cheek, glistening with a rich, dark beer reduction, rests as the centerpiece on a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic plate. The beef, a deep reddish-brown, is fork-tender, showing its soft texture. Adjacent to the beef, a small, artful mound of thinly sliced, pale fermented mushrooms adds a textural and color contrast, their unique, slightly translucent quality visible. A delicate, irregularly shaped parmesan crisp, golden and airy, leans gracefully against the beef, offering a textural counterpoint. The plate, with its natural, unglazed finish, is presented on a light, reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly visible. The composition is clean and minimalist, with generous negative space highlighting the dish's refined restaurant portion. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and emphasizing the organic textures. The background is simple, with a hint of natural elements or plants, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare fermented mushrooms: This step requires preparation 3-5 days in advance. Thinly slice 200g mushrooms. Dissolve 5g sea salt in 250ml non-chlorinated water to make a 2% brine. Place sliced mushrooms in a clean jar. Pour brine over mushrooms to cover completely. Use a fermentation weight or small bag of water to keep mushrooms submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate when desired tang is reached.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat beef cheeks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef cheeks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery into small cubes. Add to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add to the pot with tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, bay leaf, and parmesan rind (if using). Return seared beef cheeks to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged. If not, add more broth or water.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from the pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids and parmesan rind.
Simmer strained liquid over medium-high heat. Reduce until it thickens into a rich sauce consistency.

Make parmesan crisps: Grate 50g parmesan cheese. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Place small piles of grated cheese in the pan. Cook until melted and golden brown, about 2-3 minutes. Carefully remove with a spatula. Place on parchment paper to cool and crisp.

To serve: Place a single beef cheek on a ceramic plate. Spoon reduced sauce over the beef. Arrange a small portion of fermented mushrooms next to the beef. Lean a parmesan crisp against the beef. Optionally, add a few blanched seasonal greens for color.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Corn and Mushroom Risotto with Fried Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy risotto is presented in a shallow, matte white porcelain bowl, centered on a rustic wooden table. The risotto has a fluid, natural spread, exhibiting a pale golden hue from the corn and the creamy texture. Roasted cremini mushrooms, quartered, are artfully scattered atop the risotto, displaying their earthy brown color and tender, slightly caramelized surfaces. A perfectly fried egg, with a soft, glistening yolk and slightly crispy edges, rests gently on the risotto. Delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese are gracefully draped over the egg and risotto. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh rosemary is placed beside the egg, adding a pop of color and aromatic detail. The background features a subtle, out-of-focus hint of a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s textures and colors. A simple, elegant fork and spoon are placed neatly beside the bowl, with a folded cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer extra shaved Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a light, crisp Italian white wine.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, freshly grated, plus extra for shaving

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped rosemary leaves from one sprig. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Begin adding hot vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently. Wait for broth to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next ladleful.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, until rice is creamy and al dente. It should be fluid, not dry.
While risotto cooks, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat.
Add quartered cremini mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 7-8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
In the last 5 minutes of risotto cooking, stir in corn kernels.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in remaining 45 g butter and 100 g grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute to create a creamy 'mantecato' consistency. Cover and let rest 2 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil over medium heat. Fry eggs one at a time to your preferred doneness, ensuring yolks are still runny. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon risotto into individual shallow bowls. Top each serving with sautéed mushrooms.
Place one fried egg carefully on top of each risotto portion.
Garnish with shaved Parmesan cheese and a small sprig of fresh rosemary.

recipes.recipe_name: Mini Beef & Cheddar Savory Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve round, golden-brown mini beef patties, approximately 3-4 cm in diameter, are casually arranged on a rustic, well-used wooden serving board. Each patty is topped with a dollop of glistening, amber-toned mustard-caramelized onions and a small piece of melted, slightly bubbly sharp cheddar. The rich browns of the seared beef contrast with the golden-yellow cheese, deep amber onions, and vibrant green chopped parsley garnish. Textures include the crisp exterior of the patty, its soft interior, gooey melted cheese, and tender, sweet-savory onions. The board rests on a simple kitchen table with a casually draped linen napkin. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the homely scene, highlighting the comforting, bite-sized portions.
instructions: In a bowl, combine 400g beef mince, half of the finely diced onion, minced garlic, 5g Dijon mustard, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Form into 10-12 small, flat patties, about 3-4 cm in diameter and 1 cm thick.

Thinly slice the remaining half onion. Heat 5ml olive oil in a small pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onion. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and softened. Stir in the remaining 25g Dijon mustard and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Heat 10ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook patties for 2-3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 71°C.
Place a small square or pinch of cheddar cheese on top of each hot patty immediately after cooking. Cover the pan briefly with a lid for 1 minute, or until cheese is melted and slightly gooey.
Arrange cooked patties on a serving platter. Top each patty with a small spoonful of the mustard-caramelized onions. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Tropical Citrus Ginger Bundt Cake
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown bundt cake slice is plated on a simple white ceramic plate, showcasing its moist, tender crumb flecked with small pieces of lychee and passion fruit seeds. The slice reveals a light, airy texture. The cake is generously drizzled with a thick, opaque white citrus-ginger glaze that cascades down its sides. Alongside the slice are a few fresh orange segments and halved lychees, adding vibrant color. The full, remaining bundt cake sits in the background on a wooden cake stand, also glazed. The scene is set on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A casually placed, light-colored linen napkin rests beside the plate. Warm, natural kitchen light illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The focus remains on the cake's appealing, homemade appearance and natural textures.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 6-cup bundt pan.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Stir in vanilla extract.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with ginger ale and apple juice. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Gently fold in chopped lychees, orange zest, and passion fruit pulp.
Pour batter evenly into the prepared bundt pan.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in the pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze: In a small bowl, whisk powdered sugar with 30ml orange juice and 15ml ginger ale until smooth. Add more juice or ginger ale for desired consistency.
Once cake is completely cool, drizzle glaze over the top.

recipes.recipe_name: Salade de Fruits Exotiques au Gingembre
recipes.visual_description: The Salade de Fruits Exotiques au Gingembre is presented in clear, simple glass bowls, showcasing its vibrant, natural colors. Generous portions of whole or halved lychees, bright orange segments, and golden passion fruit seeds are naturally arranged, touching and overlapping. The fruits are glistening, coated in a pale, translucent ginger ale syrup that pools slightly at the bottom. The overall texture is juicy and fresh. Each bowl is garnished with a few fresh, verdant mint leaves, providing a subtle color contrast. The bowls rest on a well-used wooden dining table, reflecting a lived-in, homestyle kitchen atmosphere. A casual, subtly patterned cloth napkin is loosely placed nearby. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural appeal of the fruit. The setting is simple and unpretentious, inviting comfort and casual enjoyment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a light dessert or afternoon 'goûter'.
Can be accompanied by small, plain butter cookies or madeleines.
instructions: Peel and deseed lychees. If using canned, drain well.
Carefully peel oranges. Remove all white pith. Segment oranges by cutting between membranes.
Halve passion fruits. Scoop out pulp into a small bowl.
In a small saucepan, combine ginger ale, sugar, and the zest of one orange. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Let the syrup cool completely.
In a large bowl, gently combine lychees, orange segments, and passion fruit pulp.
Pour the cooled ginger ale syrup over the fruit mixture. Stir gently to coat all fruit.
Cover the bowl. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour to chill and allow flavors to meld.
Ladle the fruit salad into individual clear glass bowls.
Garnish each serving with a few fresh mint leaves before serving.
notes: For the best flavor and texture, use fresh lychees and oranges when in season.

recipes.recipe_name: Exotic Fruit & Ginger Ale Jelly
recipes.visual_description: A translucent golden jelly, firm yet quivering slightly, showcasing suspended vibrant orange segments, pearly white lychee halves, and speckled passion fruit pulp. The jelly's natural amber hue is clear, allowing the fruit's colors to shine. It is served in individual, simple clear glass ramekins or small, rustic ceramic bowls. Each bowl sits casually on a well-used wooden kitchen table, suggesting a lived-in family setting. A plain metal spoon rests beside each bowl. The scene is bathed in warm, soft natural light, highlighting the dish's homely comfort and inviting texture. There are no decorative garnishes; the natural arrangement of fruit within the jelly serves as the primary visual appeal. The overall presentation is unpretentious and typical of a homemade French dessert.

ingredients.name: Fresh lychees, peeled and deseeded (or canned, drained)

instructions: Place gelatin sheets in a bowl with 50 ml cold water. Let bloom for 5-10 minutes until softened.
Gently peel lychees and remove seeds. Cut orange into segments, reserving any juice.
Scoop pulp from passion fruits.
In a small saucepan, heat 100 ml of ginger ale with sugar over low heat. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin. Add gelatin to the warm ginger ale mixture. Stir until fully dissolved.
Remove from heat. Add remaining cold ginger ale and reserved orange juice. Stir well.
Distribute lychee halves, orange segments, and passion fruit pulp evenly among four individual clear glass ramekins or small dessert bowls.
Carefully pour the ginger ale mixture over the fruit in each ramekin.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until the jelly is completely set.

recipes.recipe_name: Manzanas Fermentadas con Crema de Coco
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Manzanas Fermentadas con Crema de Coco is presented on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate, possibly in a cream or beige hue, placed on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural lighting, creating a clean, minimalist background with subtle hints of natural elements or plants. The centerpiece features a cluster of golden-hued fermented apple cubes, each about 2 cm, retaining their natural skin and a slight translucence from the fermentation process. Their arrangement is organic and unforced. Adjacent to the apples is a generous, fluffy dollop of creamy white coconut cream, its texture visibly light and airy. A glistening amber drizzle of honey-rum sauce cascades over the apples and spills onto the plate, adding a rich, warm tone. The composition emphasizes natural colors and textures, with ample negative space around the dish. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed nearby, and a small, simple ceramic spoon rests beside the plate, reinforcing the eco-conscious and authentic Mexican aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled.
Optionally pair with a small shot of mezcal for adult guests.
Accompany with a traditional Café de Olla (spiced coffee) for a complete dessert experience.
instructions: Wash apples. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Do not peel or core.
Dissolve 30 g honey and sea salt in 500 ml water. This is your brine.
Place apple cubes in a clean 1-liter glass jar. Pour brine over apples, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermenting weight if needed.
Seal jar loosely with a lid or airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 2-3 days. Bubbles indicate fermentation. Taste daily; stop when desired tanginess is reached.
Drain fermented apples. Reserve fermentation liquid for other uses, like a vinegar starter.
Chill the full-fat coconut milk can overnight. Carefully scoop the thick cream from the top into a cold bowl.
Whip coconut cream until light and fluffy. Stir in lime zest and 5 ml lime juice.
Combine remaining 30 g honey and rum in a small saucepan. Simmer gently over low heat for 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Cool slightly.

Arrange fermented apple cubes on individual handcrafted ceramic plates. Dollop coconut cream alongside or on top of apples. Drizzle with honey-rum sauce. Garnish minimally with a small lime zest curl if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Linguine with Seared Tuna and Pan-Fried Oysters
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Linguine with Seared Tuna and Pan-Fried Oysters is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente linguine forms a neat, natural mound in the center, glistening with a light lemon-garlic butter sauce. Two thick, seared tuna medallions, displaying a beautiful reddish-pink interior and a golden-brown crust, are placed artfully on top of the pasta. Around the base of the tuna and nestled within the pasta strands are three to four golden-brown, pan-fried oysters, their edges slightly crisp. The dish is vibrantly garnished with a generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits on the rim of the plate. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A silver fork rests beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp, dry Italian white wine like Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add linguine and cook according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, pat tuna steaks dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear tuna steaks for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Remove tuna from skillet and set aside to rest. Do not slice.
Gently pat oysters dry. Lightly dredge oysters in flour, shaking off excess.

In the same skillet, add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter. Heat over medium-high heat. Pan-fry floured oysters for 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown and edges are slightly crispy. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 45 g butter to the skillet. Add minced garlic and diced shallot. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and softened, do not brown.
Pour in white wine. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the pan, until slightly reduced.
Stir in lemon juice and red pepper flakes (if using). Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.

Drain cooked linguine, reserving 120 ml pasta water. Add drained linguine directly to the skillet with the sauce. Toss well to coat. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to create a light sauce.
Divide pasta among four plates. Place a whole seared tuna steak on top of each pasta portion. Arrange pan-fried oysters around the tuna and pasta.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Use high-quality fresh tuna and oysters for the best flavor.
Do not overcook the tuna; it should remain medium-rare for optimal texture.
Adjust red pepper flakes to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Cokelat Mochi Lava Bites
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly spherical, glistening Cokelat Mochi Lava Bites are artfully arranged on a minimalist white porcelain serving platter with a subtle gold rim. Each delicate bite, about 3-4 cm in diameter, is coated in finely toasted desiccated coconut, offering a warm, golden hue and subtle texture. The mochi's translucent off-white exterior hints at its chewy softness. One or two bites are precisely cut, revealing a rich, glossy, molten milk chocolate center softly oozing, showcasing contrasting textures and temperatures. Abundant negative space emphasizes their delicate form and precision. The platter rests on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, dramatically lit to enhance depth and elegance. A precisely folded white linen napkin completes the ultra-minimalist, luxurious aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a delicate dessert course following a traditional Indonesian meal.
Accompany with strong black tea or Indonesian kopi tubruk.
Present on a tiered serving stand for a formal gathering.
instructions: Prepare chocolate filling: Finely chop milk chocolate. Heat heavy cream until just simmering. Pour hot cream over chopped chocolate. Let stand 1 minute. Stir until smooth ganache forms. Stir in 20g icing sugar. Chill ganache until firm enough to scoop (about 1-2 hours).
Make mochi dough: In a bowl, whisk glutinous rice flour, 30g icing sugar, and egg yolk. Gradually add 150ml water, whisking until smooth. Stir in melted butter.

Cook mochi dough: Pour mochi batter into a heatproof bowl. Cover with plastic wrap, leaving a small vent. Steam over medium heat for 15-20 minutes, or until dough is translucent and firm. Stir well with a spatula.

Form mochi: Dust a clean surface with glutinous rice flour (not listed in ingredients, for dusting). Transfer hot mochi dough onto the surface. Knead gently until smooth. Divide dough into 6-9 equal portions.

Fill mochi: Flatten each mochi portion into a disc. Place a small scoop of chilled chocolate ganache in the center. Carefully fold the mochi dough around the ganache, sealing completely to form a ball.
Finish: Steam filled mochi balls for another 3-5 minutes to ensure chocolate center is warm and molten.
Coat: Gently roll each warm mochi ball in toasted desiccated coconut. Serve immediately.
notes: The chocolate ganache must be firm enough to handle but will soften upon steaming inside the mochi.
Adjust sweetness of ganache to personal preference.
Best served warm to enjoy the molten chocolate center.

recipes.recipe_name: Sopa de Elote Estilo Esquites
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, creamy Mexican corn soup is presented in a deep white ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, sunny yellow hue. The soup's surface is smooth, adorned with a generous, artful scattering of crumbled white Cotija cheese. Bright green chopped cilantro leaves are sprinkled over the cheese, along with a light dusting of red chili powder, adding vivid color contrasts and texture. A fresh lime wedge rests elegantly on the bowl's rim. The soup maintains a fluid, inviting consistency. The bowl is positioned on a rustic dark wood table, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its warmth and authentic presentation in a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping.
Offer extra lime wedges on the side for individual preference.

ingredients.name: Corn cobs or frozen corn kernels

instructions: Char corn kernels. If using fresh cobs, grill or broil cobs until lightly blackened. Cut kernels from cobs. If using frozen, pan-roast kernels in a dry skillet until lightly browned.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add charred corn kernels to the pot. Stir well.
Pour in broth. Add epazote, chili powder, and cumin. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cook 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Remove epazote sprig. Carefully blend soup until smooth using an immersion blender or standard blender. If using a standard blender, work in batches and do not overfill.
Return blended soup to the pot. Stir in fresh lime juice and heavy cream. Heat through gently. Do not boil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with crumbled Cotija cheese, chopped fresh cilantro, and a light dusting of chili powder. Place a lime wedge on the rim of each bowl.
notes: For a deeper smoky flavor, roast fresh corn cobs directly on a grill or open flame until lightly charred before cutting off the kernels.
Adjust the amount of chili powder to suit your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Esquites-Style Corn Soup
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, creamy Esquites-Style Corn Soup is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The soup boasts a sunny yellow hue, its smooth surface adorned with textural elements. Whole, reserved corn kernels, some lightly charred for depth, are scattered across the top. Bright green, coarsely chopped cilantro leaves are sprinkled generously, providing a fresh contrast. Crumbled white Cotija cheese adds pockets of savory richness. A light dusting of reddish-brown chili powder enhances visual warmth. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a lime wedge. The setting is a modern bistro, inviting and approachable.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas or totopos (tortilla chips) on the side.
Offer extra lime wedges for guests to squeeze over the soup.
instructions: Heat butter and olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and deseeded minced jalapeño. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add corn kernels to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in chicken or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes.
Remove 1 cup of corn kernels with a slotted spoon. Set aside for garnish.
Carefully blend remaining soup until smooth. Use an immersion blender or transfer to a blender in batches.
Return soup to the pot. Stir in crema mexicana and the juice of one lime. Heat gently. Do not boil.
Season with salt, black pepper, and ancho chili powder. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with reserved whole corn kernels, crumbled Cotija cheese, and fresh coarsely chopped cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: For an extra smoky flavor, char some of the corn kernels in a dry pan before adding to the soup, or use a grill.

recipes.recipe_name: Corn Consommé with Charred Kernels and Basil Oil
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china bowl cradles a single portion of golden, crystal-clear corn consommé. The consommé, a translucent amber, fills the bowl, leaving ample negative space around the rim. In the center, a precise, organic cluster of charred corn kernels rests, their deep golden-brown hues providing a striking textural and color contrast against the consommé's clarity. Each kernel is plump and slightly blistered, showcasing the charring technique. A few vibrant emerald droplets of basil oil are artfully dispersed on the surface, creating delicate green pools that shimmer. The bowl is positioned on a polished white Carrara marble surface, accented by a precisely folded white linen napkin to the side. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's exquisite simplicity and elegant composition.
instructions: Remove kernels from 8 corn cobs. Reserve kernels from 2 cobs for charring. Place remaining 6 cobs in a large pot. Add 1.5 litres cold water, chopped onion, carrot, and celery. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 30 minutes. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.

Chill the corn stock completely. In a separate bowl, whisk egg whites until foamy. Gently fold in the ground chicken (if using) and a small amount of the cold corn stock to create a "raft" mixture. Pour the cold stock into a clean pot. Gently add the egg white raft mixture. Place over low heat. Do not stir. Allow the raft to form and rise to the surface as the stock slowly heats and simmers. Simmer very gently for 20-30 minutes, allowing impurities to be absorbed by the raft. Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve without disturbing the raft. Season consommé with salt and white pepper to taste. Keep warm.

Heat a dry cast-iron pan or heavy skillet over high heat until smoking. Add the reserved corn kernels and olive oil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until kernels are deeply charred in spots but still tender-crisp. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with neutral oil and a pinch of salt in a high-speed blender until perfectly smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for a perfectly clear oil.

Ladle the hot, clear corn consommé into warm, shallow soup bowls. Carefully place a small, artful cluster of charred corn kernels in the center of each bowl. Drizzle a few drops of basil oil around the corn kernels or in a small swirl on the consommé surface. Serve immediately.
notes: The clarity of the consommé is crucial for this dish; ensure a slow, gentle simmer during clarification.
For best results, use the freshest, sweetest corn available.

recipes.recipe_name: Clarified Corn Consommé with Sweet Corn Ravioli
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, shallow white bone china soup bowl holds a single, elegant portion. At its core, three perfectly formed, pale yellow sweet corn ravioli are nestled, their delicate edges slightly visible beneath the liquid. The consommé, a crystal-clear, golden liquid, surrounds the ravioli, reflecting light with exquisite clarity. A few vibrant green micro chervil leaves are meticulously placed atop the ravioli, offering a precise pop of color and freshness. A minimal, artistic drizzle of bright yellow corn oil creates a subtle, shimmering pattern on the consommé surface. The overall composition features abundant negative space, highlighting the dish's minimalist elegance and refined nature. The bowl rests on a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, flanked by a precisely folded white linen napkin and a single, polished silver spoon. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing texture and depth, with an ultra-minimalist background ensuring the dish is the sole focal point.

ingredients.name: Fresh corn kernels, from 2 ears (for ravioli)

instructions: Remove kernels from 8 ears of corn; reserve for later steps. Break cobs into 5 cm pieces.
In a large pot, combine corn cobs, 1.5 litres vegetable stock, chopped onion, and celery. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer gently for 45 minutes. Skim any foam.
Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. You should have approximately 1 litre of corn stock. Cool completely.
In a large bowl, whisk egg whites until foamy.
Gently whisk cooled corn stock into egg whites. Add ice cubes.
Pour mixture into a clean, heavy-bottomed pot. Place over medium-low heat. Do not stir once it starts heating.
A "raft" of egg whites will form on top. Let it simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, allowing clear liquid to bubble through the raft.
Carefully create a small opening in the raft. Ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve into a clean bowl. Do not press the raft.
Season consommé with salt and white pepper. Keep warm or chill for later use.
Blanch 150 grams fresh corn kernels in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and cool.
In a bowl, combine blanched corn kernels, ricotta, Parmesan, and minced chives. Season with salt and pepper.
On a clean surface, make a well with "00" flour. Add egg yolks and olive oil to the center.
Gradually incorporate flour into liquids, forming a dough. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in cling film. Rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Divide pasta dough into four pieces. Roll one piece very thinly using a pasta machine (setting 6 or 7).
Place small spoonfuls of corn filling, spaced 4 cm apart, on one half of the pasta sheet.
Lightly brush water around filling. Fold other half of pasta sheet over filling.
Press gently around filling to remove air. Cut ravioli into desired shape (e.g., 3 cm squares or rounds) using a cutter.
Repeat with remaining dough and filling. Place ravioli on a floured tray.
Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle boil.
Carefully add ravioli. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until al dente and floating. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Gently warm the clarified corn consommé.
Place 3-4 cooked ravioli in the center of each shallow soup bowl.
Ladle hot consommé around the ravioli.
Garnish precisely with a few micro chervil leaves and a delicate drizzle of corn oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Butternut Squash with Fermented Huckleberry-Peach Relish and Creamy Macadamia Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted butternut squash steak, approximately 2.5 cm thick, forms the centerpiece of a round, matte cream ceramic plate. The squash steak, deeply browned from searing and roasting, is dusted with a subtle, earthy cocoa-paprika rub. Nestled around the steak are soft, roasted butternut squash cubes. A vibrant mound of fermented huckleberry-peach relish, featuring diced peaches and whole, plump huckleberries, is spooned artfully over one side of the squash steak. A smooth, creamy macadamia sauce, off-white in color, is drizzled elegantly around the plate, creating gentle curves. A few crisp, golden-green sage leaves and scattered toasted butternut squash seeds add texture and visual interest. The presentation is minimalistic, with ample negative space. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, illuminated by soft, natural light, emphasizing the dish's organic and sustainable nature.

ingredients.name: Starter culture or brine from previous fermentation

instructions: Prepare Fermented Huckleberry-Peach Relish: Dice peaches into 1 cm cubes. Combine diced peaches, whole huckleberries, 5 g sea salt, and 20 ml apple cider vinegar in a clean jar. Add 50 ml water or starter culture/brine. Ensure fruit is submerged. Seal loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate once desired tang is reached.
Prepare Macadamia Sauce: Soak macadamia nuts in hot water for 30 minutes. Drain. Blend soaked macadamia nuts with plant-based milk until smooth and creamy. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Prepare Butternut Squash: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut butternut squash into four 2.5 cm thick 'steaks.' Reserve squash seeds. Peel remaining squash and cut into 2 cm cubes. Toast reserved squash seeds in a dry pan until golden. Set aside.
Season Squash: In a small bowl, combine cocoa powder, smoked paprika, 3 g sea salt, and black pepper. Rub this mixture evenly over both sides of the butternut squash steaks.

Roast Squash: Heat 30 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear squash steaks for 3 minutes per side until golden. Add cubed squash to the pan. Transfer pan to the preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until squash is tender.
Crisp Sage: Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Fry sage leaves until crisp. Remove and drain on paper towel.

Assemble Dish: Place a roasted butternut squash steak on each plate. Arrange roasted squash cubes around the steak. Spoon a generous portion of the fermented huckleberry-peach relish over the steak. Drizzle macadamia sauce around the plate. Garnish with crisp sage leaves and toasted squash seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Corn Velouté with Seared Scallops
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china soup bowl holds a single serving of the vibrant, creamy sweet corn velouté. The soup, a rich, golden yellow, forms a smooth, fluid base, its surface perfectly unblemished. Artistically placed in the center are three perfectly seared, plump sea scallops, each showcasing a caramelized, golden-brown crust contrasting with their pearly white interiors. A delicate swirl of emerald green chive oil encircles the scallops, adding a striking color contrast and aromatic highlight. A whisper of finely ground popcorn dust lightly sprinkles over the scallops, providing a subtle textural counterpoint. The presentation is elegant and minimalist, with abundant negative space around the bowl on a polished grey-veined marble surface. A precisely folded white linen napkin rests beside the bowl. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's sculptural quality and premium ingredients.
instructions: Prepare Chive Oil: Blanch chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze chives dry. Blend blanched chives with neutral oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth. Set aside.

Make Corn Velouté: In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add corn kernels. Sauté for 5 minutes. Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes until corn is tender.
Blend Velouté: Carefully transfer corn mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until very smooth. Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Finish Velouté: Return strained velouté to a clean saucepan. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Keep warm over low heat; do not boil.

Sear Scallops: Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Season scallops with salt and white pepper. Place scallops in hot pan without crowding. Sear for 1.5-2 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Scallops should be opaque throughout.

Assemble Dish: Ladle warm corn velouté into individual shallow soup bowls. Arrange three seared scallops artfully in the center of each bowl. Drizzle chive oil around the scallops. Sprinkle a pinch of popcorn dust over the scallops and soup. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Golden Corn Velouté with Brown Butter and Lime Crème Fraîche
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of luminous, golden corn velouté is presented in a deep, pristine white bone china bowl. The soup's surface is a velvety expanse of rich yellow. A graceful, organic swirl of bright white lime crème fraîche nestles off-center, creating a soft contrast. Around the crème fraîche, precise droplets of vibrant green chive oil are artfully dotted, their verdant hue popping against the golden base. The composition is elegantly minimalist, emphasizing abundant negative space within the bowl. The dish rests on a cool, grey-veined Carrara marble surface, beside a crisp white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the soup's luxurious sheen and the meticulous plating. The background is utterly minimalist, allowing the dish to command full attention.
instructions: Melt 20g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced shallots and cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add corn kernels to the saucepan. Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-12 minutes until corn is tender.

Carefully transfer the corn mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until exceptionally smooth and creamy. Pass the velouté through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Return the smooth velouté to low heat. Stir in heavy cream. Season with sea salt and white pepper to taste. Keep warm, do not boil.

For the brown butter: Melt remaining 40g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook, swirling occasionally, until the butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Immediately remove from heat. Stir half of the brown butter into the velouté.
For the lime crème fraîche: In a small bowl, combine crème fraîche with a squeeze of fresh lime juice. Stir well.

For the chive oil: Combine chopped chives and neutral oil in a small blender or food processor. Blend until vibrant green and smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for a clear oil. Discard solids.

To serve, ladle the golden velouté into warm, deep bowls. Drizzle or dot the surface with the remaining brown butter. Add a graceful swirl of lime crème fraîche. Finish with precise droplets of chive oil.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Corn Velouté with Brown Butter and Lime Espuma
recipes.visual_description: The Smoked Corn Velouté is presented in a deep, elegant bone china bowl. The pale golden soup, perfectly smooth with a velvety sheen, fills one-third of the bowl, allowing ample negative space. A delicate, abstract swirl of amber-brown butter artfully drizzles across the surface. Nestled off-center is a cloud-like dollop of pristine white lime espuma, its airy texture contrasting the soup's richness. A few precisely placed, golden-brown toasted corn kernels are scattered near the espuma for subtle texture. A tiny sprig of vibrant green micro cilantro rests on the espuma, adding a fresh pop of color. The minimalist composition is exquisitely balanced. The bowl sits on a polished white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by a perfectly folded white linen napkin and a minimalist silver spoon. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Melt 30g butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced shallots. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add sliced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add corn kernels. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Simmer for 15 minutes, until corn is tender.
Remove 1 tablespoon of corn kernels. Pan-toast them lightly for garnish.
Carefully transfer remaining soup mixture to a high-speed blender.
Add heavy cream and liquid smoke. Blend until perfectly smooth.
Pass the velouté through a fine-mesh sieve. Press solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Return velouté to a clean pot. Gently reheat. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.
Melt 60g butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Cook, swirling occasionally, until butter solids turn golden brown and smell nutty. Immediately remove from heat. Pour into a small heatproof bowl.
Combine lime juice, water, and soy lecithin in a tall, narrow container.
Use an immersion blender to blend at an angle, incorporating air, until a stable foam forms on top.
Pour warm Smoked Corn Velouté into individual deep soup bowls.
Drizzle a small amount of Brown Butter artfully over the surface.
Carefully spoon a dollop of Lime Espuma onto the center of the velouté.
Garnish with a few toasted corn kernels and micro cilantro sprigs.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the velouté is extremely smooth by blending thoroughly and passing through a fine-mesh sieve.
The liquid smoke should be used sparingly to impart a subtle smokiness, not overpower the corn.
Achieve a stable lime espuma; adjust soy lecithin if needed, but 1g is usually sufficient for this volume.

recipes.recipe_name: Estofado de Ternera con Garbanzos y Pimentón Ahumado
recipes.visual_description: A robust, rustic Spanish beef stew, meticulously plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The centerpiece is a generous portion of tender, fork-tender beef chuck chunks, showcasing their rich, braised texture and deep reddish-brown hue. Interspersed among the beef are vibrant orange carrot rounds and creamy white chickpeas, all enveloped in a thick, savory sauce infused with smoked paprika. The sauce has a glossy sheen, naturally pooling around the ingredients. Large, rustic potato wedges are nestled among the other components, showcasing their soft, cooked texture. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, providing a vibrant color contrast and fresh aroma. The overall presentation is organized yet naturally flowing, avoiding rigid arrangements. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a small piece of crusty Spanish bread. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pan de pueblo) for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Tempranillo or Garnacha.
Enjoy as a hearty main course, often part of a larger family meal.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and cut into 2 cm thick rounds

ingredients.name: Smoked paprika (Pimentón de la Vera, sweet)
Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and cut into 3 cm wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, smoked paprika, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add carrot rounds and potato wedges to the pot. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef is fork-tender and vegetables are cooked through.
Stir in drained and rinsed chickpeas during the last 15 minutes of cooking.
Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle the stew into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, prepare the stew a day in advance. Flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust the amount of smoked paprika to your preference; Pimentón de la Vera offers a distinct, authentic flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Clarified Corn Essence with Silken Corn Custard and Brown Butter Crumble
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a sophisticated minimalist composition within a pristine white bone china bowl. A perfectly formed, pale yellow silken corn custard, cut into a precise small cube, rests centrally. Around it, a crystal-clear, golden-hued clarified corn essence shimmers, filling the bowl with abundant negative space. A delicate scattering of golden-brown brown butter crumble adds a subtle textural contrast atop the custard. Several vivid emerald green drops of chive oil are artfully dotted on the essence, providing a burst of color. The bowl sits on a polished white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, focused lighting creates elegant shadows, highlighting the dish's refined simplicity and flawless execution.

ingredients.name: leek, white part only, thinly sliced

instructions: Prepare Clarified Corn Essence:
Combine corn kernels from 8 cobs, reserved cobs, 1.5 litres water, 5g salt, and 2g white peppercorns in a large pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook 20 minutes.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Cool corn liquid completely.
Whisk 4 egg whites with sliced leek until frothy.
Add egg white mixture to cold corn liquid. Heat slowly over medium-low heat, stirring constantly until raft forms. Stop stirring. Simmer gently 20 minutes without disturbing.
Carefully ladle clear essence through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Do not disturb raft. Keep essence warm.
Prepare Silken Corn Custard:
Blend corn kernels from 2 cobs with 150ml heavy cream until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids.
Whisk corn cream with 2 egg yolks, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of white pepper.
Pour mixture into small, heatproof molds (e.g., ramekins or silicone molds).
Steam molds in a steamer or bain-marie at 85°C for 15-20 minutes, or until just set but still silken. Cool.
Carefully unmold custards. Cut into small, precise cubes or discs.
Prepare Brown Butter Crumble:
Melt 50g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Continue cooking until butter browns and smells nutty.
Add 30g panko breadcrumbs. Toast until golden brown and crispy.
Remove from heat. Stir in 2g flaky sea salt. Spread on parchment paper to cool.
Prepare Chive Oil:
Blanch 30g chives in boiling water 10 seconds. Immediately plunge into ice water. Drain well. Squeeze excess water.
Blend blanched chives with 100ml grapeseed oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter for a clear oil.
Assemble and Serve:
Place one piece of silken corn custard in the center of each shallow soup bowl.
Gently pour warm clarified corn essence around the custard.
Sprinkle a small amount of brown butter crumble over the custard.
Drizzle a few drops of chive oil precisely around the essence. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Broccoli Velouté, Parmesan Risotto Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, halved diagonally to reveal its tender, moist interior, rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate. Its golden-crisp skin contrasts beautifully with a vibrant, emerald-green broccoli velouté, artfully swirled or pooled beside it. A delicate, irregular Parmesan risotto crisp, a pale golden-brown, leans subtly against the chicken or velouté, adding architectural interest and crunch. A few precise drops of clear, golden garlic oil dot the negative space. A solitary sprig of micro basil or chervil provides a final, verdant accent. The plate is positioned on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts soft, intentional shadows. A crisply folded white linen napkin completes the ultra-minimalist, sophisticated presentation.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts completely dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Set aside.

For Garlic Oil: Place 3 garlic cloves and 50ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Heat gently over very low heat for 20 minutes until garlic is tender and fragrant. Do not brown. Strain oil; discard or reserve garlic for another use. Set oil aside.
For Broccoli Velouté: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli florets for 2 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well.

In a small saucepan, melt 10g butter. Sauté minced shallot and 1 minced garlic clove until softened, about 3 minutes. Add blanched broccoli and 100ml chicken stock. Simmer 2 minutes. Transfer to a blender. Add heavy cream. Blend until perfectly smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For Parmesan Risotto Crisps: In a small saucepan, melt 10g butter. Add Arborio rice; toast for 1 minute. Add 200ml chicken stock, a ladleful at a time, stirring until absorbed. Cook until rice is al dente, about 12-15 minutes. Stir in 50g grated Parmesan. Spread mixture very thinly (about 2mm) onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Break into irregular, delicate pieces. Set aside.

For Pan-Seared Chicken: Heat 20ml olive oil and 20g butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deep golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

To Plate: Spoon a smooth, flowing pool of broccoli velouté slightly off-center on each plate. Slice each chicken breast diagonally into two thick pieces. Place chicken artfully on top of or beside the velouté. Arrange one or two irregular Parmesan risotto crisps delicately against the chicken or velouté. Drizzle garlic oil sparingly around the plate. Garnish with a few micro basil or chervil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Moldavian Chicken Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Moldavian Chicken Pilaf is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pilaf forms a natural mound, showcasing fluffy, separate grains of long-grain rice interspersed with vibrant, diced orange carrots and red bell pepper. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, about 3-4 cm, are visibly mixed throughout the rice. The dish is generously garnished with fresh, finely chopped green dill, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with golden hues from the chicken and rice, complemented by the earthy tones of vegetables and bright green herbs. The texture is soft and inviting. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a crisp white cotton napkin is neatly folded. A small, simple white bowl holds a dollop of creamy white sour cream, ready to accompany the pilaf. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a clean, unobtrusive background that suggests a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of fresh sour cream (smântână) on the side.
Offer a side of pickled vegetables (murături), such as pickled cucumbers or cabbage.
Accompany with fresh, crusty bread.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4cm chunks.
Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. Drain well.
Dice onion, carrot, and red bell pepper. Mince garlic.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sweet paprika to the vegetables. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add rinsed rice. Stir well to combine all ingredients.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add salt and black pepper. Stir gently to distribute ingredients.
Bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly.
Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not stir during simmering.
Remove pot from heat. Let pilaf rest, covered, for 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Fluff pilaf gently with a fork. Serve hot. Garnish generously with fresh chopped dill.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not lift the lid or stir the rice during simmering to ensure even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Orchard Fruit Medley
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic arrangement on a matte cream-colored ceramic bowl, showcasing the vibrant natural hues of the fruit. Quartered fresh strawberries and halved fresh banana slices are interspersed with dark, glossy fermented cherry halves. A light scattering of roughly chopped, toasted hazelnuts provides textural contrast. A delicate drizzle of clear, golden banana peel honey syrup glistens over the fruit. The presentation is clean, with ample negative space around the central fruit mound. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A natural undyed linen napkin is subtly placed to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh, unforced beauty of the ingredients against a simple, uncluttered background with hints of green foliage.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cherries: Combine 200g destemmed, pitted cherries with 250ml filtered water and 5g salt in a clean jar. Seal. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate after 3 days.

Make Banana Peel Honey Syrup: Wash banana peels from 1 banana thoroughly. Chop finely. Combine chopped peels, 200ml water, and 40g honey in a small saucepan. Simmer 15 minutes. Strain, discard peels. Stir in 5ml lemon juice. Cool.
Toast Hazelnuts: Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread hazelnuts on a baking sheet. Toast 8-10 minutes until fragrant. Cool. Roughly chop.
Prepare Fresh Fruit: Halve remaining 100g fresh cherries. Quarter strawberries. Dice 1.5 bananas into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss fresh fruit with remaining 10ml lemon juice and 40g honey.
Assemble Medley: Gently combine fresh fruit mixture with fermented cherries.
Plate and Serve: Divide fruit medley among 4 bowls. Drizzle generously with banana peel honey syrup. Sprinkle toasted hazelnuts over each portion.
notes: For optimal flavor, ensure fermented cherries are prepared at least 2-3 days in advance.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single serving of chicken and rice is casually plated on a round, off-white ceramic dinner plate. Diced, seared chicken chunks are nestled within fluffy, golden-hued long-grain rice, which is interspersed with bright red diced tomatoes and flecks of sautéed onion. The rice has a natural, slightly uneven texture. Alongside, a generous portion of vibrant green broccoli florets, roasted to a tender-crisp texture with subtle char marks, is arranged naturally, slightly overlapping the rice. The dish is presented on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, natural overhead light. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. The scene is homely and inviting, focusing on comforting, well-prepared food without any pretense.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if needed. Remove chicken from skillet. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C when fully cooked.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add chopped onion. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried herbs. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to skillet. Stir gently.
Cover skillet tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Bake 20-25 minutes, until rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
While skillet bakes, toss broccoli florets with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast in oven for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Remove skillet from oven. Let rest 5 minutes, covered.
Fluff rice with a fork. Serve chicken and rice mixture alongside roasted broccoli.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso-Glazed Chicken Thigh with Dashi-Braised Root Vegetables and Silken Tofu Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine, matte white bone china plate with a subtle, organic rim. A generous, artfully curved sweep of luminous silken tofu emulsion forms the base. Centered on this, a single, perfectly seared miso-glazed chicken thigh rests, its skin deeply golden and caramelized. Beside the chicken, a sculptural arrangement of dashi-braised root vegetables: thick-cut carrot batons, elegant potato wedges, and tender onion segments, all retaining their distinct shapes and subtle sheen. A tall, irregularly shaped crispy garlic rice cracker leans against the chicken, providing textural contrast and height. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the clean lines and deliberate placement of each element. A few finely sliced vibrant green scallion rings are scattered over the chicken and vegetables as a precise garnish. The setting features a grey-veined marble surface, a pair of dark wood chopsticks resting on a ceramic chopstick rest, and a crisp white linen napkin folded precisely. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a pair of elegant chopsticks.
Offer a small, delicate ceramic cup of warm, clear dashi broth on the side for sipping.
instructions: Prepare dashi stock using kombu and katsuobushi. Set aside.
Peel carrots and cut into 2 cm thick batons. Peel potatoes and cut into 2 cm thick wedges. Cut onion into 1.5 cm thick wedges.

In a saucepan, combine 400ml dashi, 15ml soy sauce, 15ml mirin, and 5g sugar. Bring to a simmer. Add carrots, potatoes, and onions. Cook gently until vegetables are tender, about 15-20 minutes. Keep warm.

For the miso glaze, combine 60g white miso, 15ml soy sauce, 15ml mirin, 30ml sake, and 10g sugar in a small saucepan. Whisk well. Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened. Remove from heat.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat with a little neutral oil.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until the skin is golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken thighs. Transfer the skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 10-12 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Brush a generous amount of miso glaze over the chicken thighs. Let rest for 5 minutes.
For the silken tofu emulsion, combine 200g silken tofu, 150ml dashi, and a pinch of salt in a blender. Blend until perfectly smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning. Keep warm.

For the crispy garlic rice cracker, finely mince 2 garlic cloves. In a bowl, mix 150g cooked short-grain rice with minced garlic and a pinch of salt.
