Press the rice mixture very thinly onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, forming four rectangular or irregular crackers. Shallow fry in neutral oil until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.

To plate, create a sweeping line or organic pool of silken tofu emulsion on each plate. Place one miso-glazed chicken thigh prominently. Artfully arrange a few pieces of dashi-braised carrot, potato, and onion next to the chicken. Lean one crispy garlic rice cracker against the chicken or place it nearby for height. Garnish with a few very thinly sliced scallion rings.
notes: Authentic dashi stock provides the best flavor foundation for this dish. Use kombu and katsuobushi for traditional preparation.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso Glazed Chicken and Tofu with Dashi-Simmered Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Miso Glazed Chicken and Tofu with Dashi-Simmered Vegetables is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Large, rustic chunks of chicken thigh, seared to a golden-brown crust, are coated in a rich, glossy dark amber miso glaze and arranged slightly overlapping on one side. Beside the chicken are thick, pan-fried rectangles of firm tofu, boasting a light golden crust. On the other side, dashi-simmered potato chunks, carrot batons, and onion wedges are neatly arranged, their natural colors vibrant and inviting, with a subtle sheen from the dashi. A small pool of dashi broth collects beneath the vegetables. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of thinly sliced bright green scallions. A separate small, white ceramic rice bowl, filled with perfectly steamed, fluffy Japanese short-grain rice, is placed beside the main plate. The setting features a simple light wooden table, with chopsticks resting on a small, elegant chopstick rest and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a modern Japanese bistro atmosphere. The presentation is clean, professional, and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks.
Offer a small side of tsukemono (Japanese pickles) for palate cleansing.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. Drain. Cook rice in a rice cooker or pot with 360 ml water. Set aside, keep warm.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 large, rustic chunks. Pat dry.
Drain tofu. Press gently to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 8 cm x 4 cm x 2 cm thick rectangles.
Peel and crush garlic cloves. Mince finely.
In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, mirin, sake, soy sauce, sugar, and minced garlic. This is the miso glaze.
Peel potato. Cut into large, irregular chunks (about 4 cm). Soak in cold water for 10 minutes to remove excess starch. Drain.
Peel carrot. Cut into 1 cm thick batons.
Peel onion. Cut into thick wedges.

Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces, skin-side down. Sear until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip. Cook other side for 3 minutes. Reduce heat to medium. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Keep warm.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the same pan. Add tofu rectangles. Pan-fry until golden brown and crisp on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from pan. Keep warm.
Deglaze pan with a splash of dashi if needed. Add potato, carrot, and onion to the pan. Pour in dashi stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover. Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until vegetables are tender-crisp.
While vegetables simmer, return chicken to the pan. Brush chicken generously with miso glaze. Cook over medium heat, turning, until glaze is thick and glossy, about 2-3 minutes. Do not burn.
Thinly slice green onions.

To serve, place dashi-simmered vegetables on a clean white porcelain plate. Arrange glazed chicken chunks and pan-fried tofu rectangles beside the vegetables. Garnish with sliced green onions. Serve with a separate bowl of hot rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Clasico
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo Clasico is presented in a shallow, white porcelain bowl. The rice is a vibrant reddish-orange, moist and tender, with individual grains visible. Large, succulent chunks of golden-brown seared chicken are nestled throughout the rice, not fanned. Diced red and green bell peppers are integrated, adding pops of color and texture. The dish is generously garnished with fresh, bright green chopped cilantro. A lime wedge rests on the rim of the bowl. The setting is a simple wooden table. Beside the bowl, a small stack of warm corn tortillas sits on a rustic plate. A small traditional Mexican ceramic bowl holds a vibrant salsa roja. A folded cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of salsa roja or pico de gallo.
Provide lime wedges for fresh acidity.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into large 4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot pan. Sear until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced bell peppers. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in chili powder and ground cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes to toast the rice grains.
Pour in chicken broth and canned diced tomatoes. Stir well. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pan. Nestle chicken into the rice mixture.
Cover the pan tightly. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift lid during cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Stir in half of the fresh cilantro.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Baked Chicken and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of hearty baked chicken and root vegetables is casually arranged on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is positioned slightly off-center, its rich color contrasting with the earthy tones of the vegetables. Around the chicken, roasted potato chunks, with their slightly crusted exteriors and soft interiors, are interspersed with tender, caramelized carrot rounds. The garlic cloves, softened and golden, are visible among the vegetables. A scattering of fresh green chopped parsley provides a touch of vibrant color and freshness. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. A plain, light-colored cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen, emphasizing the comforting and home-cooked nature of the meal. A standard fork and knife rest beside the plate. The overall scene is natural and unpretentious, showcasing a satisfying, expertly prepared home meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken thighs. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes and cut into 2-3 cm chunks.
Peel carrots and cut into 2 cm thick rounds.
Peel and smash garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine potatoes, carrots, olive oil, dried thyme, and smashed garlic. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Place chicken thighs on top of the vegetables, skin-side up.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Stir-fry with Fermented Black Beans and Cloud Ear Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: Chicken pieces are velveted, then quickly stir-fried to a tender finish with a light golden crust. Red bell pepper squares are briefly stir-fried, retaining a slight crispness. Rehydrated cloud ear mushrooms provide a contrasting chewy texture. All ingredients are coated in a glossy, dark, savory fermented black bean sauce. The dish is arranged cleanly on a white porcelain plate, with moderate negative space. Cubed chicken, vibrant red bell pepper, and dark, wavy cloud ear mushrooms are artfully combined. A sprinkle of bright green scallion pieces provides a fresh garnish. The presentation is simple, professional, and highlights the dish's rich colors and varied textures. It is served alongside a small white rice bowl filled with fluffy steamed white rice, accompanied by a pair of wooden chopsticks on a simple wooden table with natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
Offer chopsticks for authentic dining.
instructions: Rehydrate cloud ear mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes. Drain and rinse. Remove any tough stems. Cut into bite-sized pieces.
Rinse fermented black beans. Roughly chop them.
Cut chicken into 2.5 cm cubes. In a bowl, combine chicken with 5 ml Shaoxing wine, 5 ml light soy sauce, 5 ml cornstarch, and a pinch of white pepper. Mix well. This is velveting the chicken.
Cut red bell pepper into 2.5 cm squares.
Mince ginger and garlic. Cut scallions into 2.5 cm lengths.

Prepare sauce: In a small bowl, combine remaining Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, and remaining 10 g cornstarch with 120 ml water or chicken broth. Mix until smooth.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking.
Add velveted chicken. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly golden. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced ginger, garlic, and chopped black beans. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add red bell pepper and cloud ear mushrooms. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until bell pepper is slightly tender-crisp.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Stir continuously as sauce thickens, about 1 minute.
Add scallions. Stir to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Torta della Nonna
recipes.visual_description: A generous wedge of golden-brown Torta della Nonna rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The rustic shortcrust pastry is visibly golden, topped with a scattering of toasted pine nuts and a delicate, even dusting of white powdered sugar. The cut side reveals the rich, pale yellow pastry cream filling, its smooth texture contrasting with the flaky crust. The plate is set on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, lived-in kitchen environment. A casually folded beige linen napkin and a classic silver fork are placed beside the plate. Soft, warm natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and inviting colors of the dessert, evoking a traditional Italian home.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature.
Often enjoyed with a small cup of espresso.
Can be paired with a dessert wine like Vin Santo.
instructions: Combine 200g flour, 70g sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in 100g cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add 1 egg and zest from 1/2 lemon. Mix until dough forms a ball.
Wrap dough in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat 250ml milk with zest from 1/2 lemon until simmering. Remove from heat.
Whisk 2 egg yolks and 60g sugar until pale.
Whisk in 20g flour until smooth.
Slowly pour hot milk into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick.
Remove pastry cream from heat. Cover surface directly with cling film. Cool completely.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Divide chilled pastry into 2/3 and 1/3 portions.
Roll out the larger pastry portion. Line a 20cm tart tin with the pastry. Trim excess.
Pour the cooled pastry cream into the pastry-lined tin.
Roll out the smaller pastry portion. Place it over the cream filling.
Pinch the edges of the top and bottom pastry layers to seal.
Sprinkle 20g pine nuts evenly over the top crust.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown.
Cool the tart completely on a wire rack.
Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Frango Ensopado com Feijão e Pimentão
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of "Frango Ensopado com Feijão e Pimentão" served in a rustic, slightly irregular off-white ceramic bowl. The stew fills the bowl, showcasing tender, irregular chunks of stewed chicken, dark black beans, and vibrant pieces of red and green diced bell pepper and softened diced onion, all bathed in a rich, reddish-brown, comforting sauce. The surface is generously sprinkled with bright green chopped fresh parsley and cilantro, adding a pop of color and freshness. The stew appears hearty and wholesome, with natural textures. The bowl sits on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table. Adjacent to the bowl, a small separate pile of fluffy white rice is casually placed, ready to accompany the stew. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl, and a casually folded, slightly textured off-white cloth napkin is placed nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, natural light, creating a cozy and inviting family kitchen atmosphere with a subtly blurred background suggesting a lived-in space. The entire plate and its immediate surroundings are visible, showing a modest, approachable, and comforting home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fluffy white rice.
Serve with farofa (toasted cassava flour).
Serve with a simple green salad.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and anchovy paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Stir in cumin and paprika. Cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Add drained and rinsed black beans.
Season with salt and black pepper. Stir well.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and tender. The sauce should be slightly thickened.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and/or cilantro.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The anchovy melts into the sauce, adding a savory depth without a strong fishy taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cabbage Rolls with Savory Mushroom & Lentil Filling
recipes.visual_description: Two plump cabbage rolls are gently nestled on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate, showcasing their soft, tender, pale green exterior. The filling, a rich blend of finely diced mushrooms and lentils, peeks subtly from the ends. A light, savory broth pools around the rolls. A small, vibrant mound of translucent quick-pickled shredded cabbage rests beside the rolls, offering a textural contrast. Fresh, bright green parsley leaves are scattered thoughtfully. The plate sits on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a natural beige undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's earthy tones and simple elegance. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Carefully remove 8-10 large outer leaves from the cabbage. Blanch these leaves in boiling salted water for 3-5 minutes until pliable. Drain.
Shred approximately 100g of remaining cabbage for a quick pickle garnish. Combine shredded cabbage with 100ml white vinegar, 50ml water, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp sugar. Set aside.
Rinse 200g green lentils. Cook in 600ml water until tender, about 20-25 minutes. Drain any excess liquid.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large pan. Add 1 finely diced onion, 2 finely diced carrots, and 2 finely diced celery stalks. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add 3 minced garlic cloves and 400g diced mixed mushrooms (including stems). Cook until mushrooms release liquid and brown, about 10-12 minutes.
Stir in 50g tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add cooked lentils to the pan. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir in 2 tablespoons fresh chopped parsley. Mix well.
Lay each blanched cabbage leaf flat. Place 2-3 tablespoons of filling near the stem end. Fold in the sides, then roll tightly from the stem end. Repeat for all leaves.

Arrange rolls snugly in a large pot or oven-safe dish. Pour 500ml vegetable broth over the rolls. Bring to a simmer on the stovetop. Cover and cook over low heat for 30-40 minutes, or bake at 180°C for 45-60 minutes, until cabbage is very tender.
Carefully transfer two rolls per plate. Spoon some cooking liquid over the rolls. Garnish with a small mound of the quick-pickled cabbage and extra fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Compressed Brioche, Confit Garlic-Shallot Marmalade, Whipped Ricotta Crème
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve perfectly square, lightly golden compressed brioche cubes are artfully arranged on a pristine, large white Carrara marble slab, leaving abundant negative space. Each brioche cube, precisely cut to 2cm, serves as a minimalist base. A delicate, airy dollop of off-white whipped ricotta-cheddar crème is elegantly piped onto each cube. Nestled atop the crème is a small, glossy, deep amber-brown dot of confit garlic-shallot marmalade, catching the light. A single, vibrant green micro chive or a tiny, pale purple edible flower petal is meticulously placed on each marmalade dot as a precise garnish. The composition is natural and flowing, avoiding rigid geometric patterns. Dramatic professional lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing the textures and depth. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the food’s sophisticated simplicity and flawless execution.

ingredients.name: Micro chives or edible flower petals

instructions: Prepare Confit Garlic and Shallot Marmalade: Peel garlic cloves and finely dice shallots. Combine garlic, shallots, and olive oil in a small saucepan. Cook over very low heat for 45-60 minutes until garlic is tender and shallots are deeply caramelized. Drain excess oil. Transfer to a blender. Add a pinch of sugar, salt, and pepper. Blend until a coarse, jam-like marmalade forms. Set aside.

Prepare Compressed Brioche: Slice brioche into 1 cm thick slices. Place slices between two flat trays or cutting boards. Apply light weight on top. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to compress. Remove brioche. Trim crusts. Cut brioche into precise 2 cm x 2 cm cubes. Lightly toast cubes in a dry pan or oven until golden and slightly crisp on all sides. Set aside.

Prepare Whipped Ricotta-Cheddar Crème: Grate aged white cheddar finely. In a cold bowl, combine fresh ricotta, grated cheddar, and heavy cream. Season with salt and white pepper. Whip with an electric mixer until light, airy, and smooth. Do not overmix.

Assemble Canapés: Arrange 8-12 toasted brioche cubes artistically on a large serving platter or individual appetizer plates. Using a small piping bag with a plain tip, pipe a delicate dollop of whipped ricotta-cheddar crème onto each brioche cube. Top each crème dollop with a small, precise amount of confit garlic and shallot marmalade. Garnish each canapé with a single micro chive or a tiny edible flower petal.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Sausage Mousse, Potato Mille-Feuille, Broccoli Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine white bone china plate presents a meticulously composed starter. Centered on the plate is a perfectly formed, smooth quenelle of light brown smoked sausage mousse, its surface subtly glistening. Beside it, two precisely cut, golden-brown potato mille-feuille rectangles are stacked, revealing delicate layers. A vibrant green swipe of velvety broccoli puree extends elegantly from one side, adding a contrasting pop of color. Delicate drops of bright green pea coulis are artfully placed around the mousse, providing freshness and visual interest. One or two thin, golden-amber aged cheddar crisps stand upright, adding architectural height and a crisp texture. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the clean lines and sophisticated arrangement of each element. The setting is a polished white Carrara marble surface, with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic, focused lighting creates subtle shadows, enhancing the dish's contours against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: For the Smoked Sausage Mousse: Remove casing from sausage. Finely dice onion and garlic. Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and sauté for 1 minute more. Add sausage meat and break apart. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Transfer sausage mixture to a food processor. Add 50 ml heavy cream. Process until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Chill for 30 minutes to firm slightly.

For the Potato Mille-Feuille: Preheat oven to 180°C. Peel potatoes. Slice potatoes very thinly, 1-2 mm thick, using a mandoline. Melt 30 g butter. Arrange potato slices overlapping in a small, oven-safe rectangular mold or on a parchment-lined baking sheet, brushing each layer lightly with melted butter and seasoning with salt and pepper. Press firmly. Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until tender and golden. Cool completely. Press under a weight for 1 hour. Cut into precise 2x2 cm squares or 2x4 cm rectangles.

For the Broccoli Puree: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli florets for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp and bright green. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Blend blanched broccoli with 50 ml chicken stock and 50 ml heavy cream until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

For the Green Pea Coulis: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add green peas and blanch for 1 minute. Drain immediately and transfer to an ice bath. Drain well. Blend peas with 50 ml chicken stock until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

For the Aged Cheddar Crisps: Preheat oven to 160°C. Grate cheddar cheese finely. On a parchment-lined baking sheet, spread small mounds of grated cheddar, leaving space between them. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Remove from oven. Immediately drape over a rolling pin or dowel to create a curved shape, or let cool flat for irregular crisps. Once cool, they will be brittle.

To Assemble: Place a quenelle or small mold of chilled smoked sausage mousse slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange two potato mille-feuille pieces beside the mousse. Create a swoosh or a few precise dots of broccoli puree. Add a few drops or a delicate drizzle of green pea coulis. Finish with one or two aged cheddar crisps, standing upright or leaning against the mousse for height and texture. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Turkey Burgers
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty Classic Turkey Burger is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The toasted golden-brown burger bun is topped with a thick, pan-fried turkey patty, which is well-cooked with a light char and covered with a melted, slightly glossy slice of bright yellow cheddar cheese. Beneath the patty, a crisp green lettuce leaf is visible. On top, vibrant red tomato slices and thinly sliced white red onion rings add fresh color and texture. Two bright green dill pickle slices are nestled alongside the burger on the plate. The overall plating is natural and inviting, suggesting a comforting home-cooked meal. The scene is set on a warm-toned wooden kitchen table, with soft, natural lighting creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of potato chips or crispy french fries.
Offer condiments like ketchup, mustard, and mayonnaise for personal preference.
Enjoy with a cold beverage, such as soda or iced tea.
instructions: Combine ground turkey, diced onion, minced garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide mixture into 4 equal portions. Form each portion into a 2 cm thick patty.
Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Place patties in the hot pan. Cook for 6-8 minutes per side. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
During the last minute of cooking, place a cheese slice on each patty. Cover pan to melt cheese.
Toast burger buns lightly on a separate pan or toaster.

Assemble burgers: Place a cooked patty with melted cheese on the bottom half of each toasted bun. Add lettuce, tomato slices, red onion slices, and dill pickle slices. Top with the other half of the bun.
notes: Avoid overworking the turkey mixture to keep the patties tender.
For extra flavor, add a dash of Worcestershire sauce to the patty mixture.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken, Potato, and Macaroni Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown Chicken, Potato, and Macaroni Gratin is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin is a substantial square cut, showcasing a creamy interior with tender, thinly sliced potato rounds, diced chicken pieces, and small elbow macaroni pasta. The top crust is deeply golden and bubbly, with visible melted Parmesan cheese, hinting at its rich, savory flavor. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered on top as a simple, aromatic garnish. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware (fork and knife) are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting casual bistro atmosphere, with a blurred, unobtrusive background. The gratin maintains its structural integrity, yet conveys a tender, comforting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish or individual ramekins.
Often accompanied by a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts

instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, 7-9 minutes, ensuring internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove, let cool slightly, then dice into 1.5 cm cubes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Peel potatoes. Using a mandoline or sharp knife, slice potatoes into thin 2-3 mm rounds. Place in cold water to prevent browning.
Cook macaroni according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.

Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Stir in flour to form a roux; cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.

Gradually whisk in milk, ensuring no lumps. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, whisking, until sauce thickens. Remove from heat. Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Stir in grated Gruyère, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until cheese melts and sauce is smooth.

Lightly grease a 20x30 cm baking dish. Drain potato slices. Layer half of the potato slices evenly in the bottom of the dish. Top with half of the cooked macaroni and half of the diced chicken. Pour half of the béchamel sauce over the layers. Repeat with remaining potato, macaroni, chicken, and sauce. Sprinkle evenly with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until potatoes are tender, sauce is bubbly, and top is golden brown. If top browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil. Let rest 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C.
Do not overcrowd the baking dish for even cooking and browning.
traditional_techniques: Gratin technique (layering and baking to create a golden crust)

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Fermented Tomato Puree and Root Vegetable Medley
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate on a light bamboo surface. A vibrant, reddish-orange fermented tomato puree forms a natural base. A single, golden-brown slow-cooked chicken thigh, skin crispy, rests atop the puree, a whole piece. Around it, roasted root vegetables – carrots, parsnips, celeriac – are arranged organically. Carrots are deep orange, parsnips creamy white, celeriac pale beige, all with caramelized edges. Vegetables are rustic 3cm chunks. A small, fresh thyme sprig garnishes. Plating emphasizes negative space; composition is clean, unforced, minimalist, highlighting pure beauty and natural colors. An undyed linen napkin is folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing textures. Background is clean, with a hint of natural plant greenery, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme sprigs or parsley leaves

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Puree (at least 3-5 days in advance): Combine chopped tomatoes, 10g sea salt, sugar (if using), and 50ml water in a clean glass jar. Ensure tomatoes are submerged. Seal with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Blend into a smooth puree. Strain if desired. Store refrigerated.

Prepare Zero-Waste Chicken Stock: Place chicken bones, trimmings, vegetable peels, bay leaf, and 5 black peppercorns in a saucepan. Add 1 litre filtered water. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook gently for 1-2 hours. Skim any foam. Strain stock, discard solids. Set aside.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with 5g sea salt and 2g black pepper.
Sear Chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken.

Slow Cook Chicken: Pour 200ml of the prepared chicken stock into the pan with the seared chicken. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Keep warm.

Roast Root Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss chopped carrots, parsnips, and celeriac with 15ml olive oil, 3g sea salt, and 1g black pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.

Assemble Dish: Spoon a generous dollop of fermented tomato puree onto the center of each plate. Arrange one slow-cooked chicken thigh on top of the puree. Artfully place a portion of roasted root vegetable chunks around the chicken.
Garnish: Garnish with a small sprig of fresh thyme or a few parsley leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe embraces sustainability through fermentation for flavor depth and preservation, and zero-waste practices by utilizing chicken bones and vegetable scraps for a nourishing stock. Focus on seasonal, local produce for best flavor and environmental impact.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Ham, Gherkin, and Mustard Composition with Lemon
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, matte white bone china plate, set against a pristine white Carrara marble surface. The composition features several artfully folded, thin slices of premium smoked ham, showcasing its delicate pink hue. Adjacent to the ham, a precise, small mound of vibrant green cornichon brunoise adds a crisp textural contrast. A single, elegant quenelle of pale yellow mustard emulsion provides a creamy element. Bright yellow lemon suprêmes are strategically placed for visual pop and acidity. A light scattering of finely snipped chives and a few whole grain mustard seeds complete the minimalist presentation. Abundant negative space surrounds the central composition, emphasizing each element’s intentional placement. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting subtle shadows, and features a precisely folded white linen napkin and a single, modern silver fork, embodying luxury and restraint.
instructions: Prepare the ham: Gently fold or roll each thin slice of smoked ham into an elegant, organic shape. Arrange on a plate.
Prepare the cornichons: Finely dice the cornichons into small, uniform cubes (brunoise). Set aside.
Make the mustard emulsion: In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, a squeeze of lemon juice, and slowly drizzle in olive oil until emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.
Segment the lemon: Cut the lemon into suprêmes (skinless, seedless segments). Collect any juice.
Assemble the dish: Place a small, precise mound of diced cornichons beside the ham. Add a delicate dot or quenelle of the mustard emulsion.
Garnish: Scatter a few whole grain mustard seeds. Place 1-2 lemon suprêmes artfully on the plate. Finely snip chives and sprinkle sparingly over the composition.
Finish: Drizzle a few drops of reserved lemon juice and a hint of olive oil over the ham.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Pork and Green Pea Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single serving of Spanish Pork and Green Pea Stew presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Tender, rustic pork chunks, approximately 3cm cubes, are submerged in a rich, reddish-brown tomato-based sauce. The sauce is thick, revealing softened small-diced onion and minced garlic. Bright, plump green peas are generously interspersed, providing vivid color contrast. The pork pieces exhibit subtle browning from initial searing. The stew's texture is comforting and spoonable. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a final touch of green. The bowl is centered on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin rests beside the bowl, with a silver fork and spoon to the right. A small slice of crusty bread, ideal for dipping, sits near the bowl. Natural, even light from the side illuminates the dish, creating soft highlights and shadows, while the background remains subtly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the stew's sauce.
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot.
Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return pork to pot. Add crushed tomatoes, broth, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 60-90 minutes, or until pork is very tender.
Stir in green peas. Cook 5 minutes until heated through.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet, skin-on and crisp, rests atop a bed of deeply caramelized, golden-brown onion half-moons. The salmon showcases its rosy-orange flesh and a perfectly seared, slightly charred skin. A light, glossy pan sauce, infused with herbs and lemon, is gently drizzled around the base of the salmon and onions, creating a subtle sheen. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A fresh lemon wedge and a vibrant green sprig of thyme or rosemary serve as a simple, elegant garnish, adding a pop of color. The overall composition is balanced, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a folded linen napkin, and classic silver flatware, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting from a restaurant-style background.

ingredients.name: Dry white wine or chicken stock

instructions: Slice onions thinly into half-moons.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large sauté pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions.
Cook onions slowly, stirring occasionally, for 30-40 minutes until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Season with salt.
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place salmon fillets skin-side down.
Sear salmon for 4-5 minutes until skin is crisp and golden. Do not move salmon during this time.

Flip salmon fillets. Add remaining 15g butter, minced garlic, and two thyme sprigs to the skillet. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, basting with melted butter, until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove salmon from skillet. Deglaze the skillet with white wine or chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 1 minute until slightly reduced.
Squeeze half a lemon into the pan sauce. Stir well.
To plate, spoon a generous portion of caramelized onions onto the center of each plate. Place one salmon fillet on top of the onions. Drizzle the pan sauce around the base of the salmon.
Garnish each plate with a fresh lemon wedge and a sprig of thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Risotto with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken Risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is fluid and spreads slightly, showcasing its rich texture. Visible throughout the creamy, off-white rice are golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2 cm). Integrated within the risotto are softened, translucent pieces of diced onion. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley and a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese, adding subtle pale yellow highlights. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space on the plate, allowing the dish to be the focal point. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro. Standard silver flatware (a fork and a spoon) are neatly placed beside the plate. A folded neutral-colored cotton napkin rests adjacent to the plate. The lighting is natural and even, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere, with a subtly blurred background indicative of a casual restaurant setting. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the balanced and appealing composition.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Dice the onion. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook over medium heat until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.

Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful (approx. 120ml) at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy. This is the 'mantecare' step.
Fold in cooked chicken cubes.
Ladle risotto into warm bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna with Spicy Gochujang Mayo and Asian Carrot Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared Tuna with Spicy Gochujang Mayo and Asian Carrot Slaw is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The seared tuna, cut into thick, succulent chunks, shows a beautiful seared crust on the outside with a vibrant pink-red interior, indicating a perfect medium-rare doneness. It is arranged neatly on one side of the plate. Beside the tuna, a mound of bright orange julienned carrot slaw provides a crisp textural contrast. The slaw is lightly dressed, maintaining its fresh appearance. A creamy, reddish-orange spicy Gochujang mayo is artfully drizzled over the tuna chunks and around the plate, creating subtle lines and pools. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, adding color and a nutty aroma. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the fresh ingredients and refined presentation. Chopsticks rest beside the plate, and a small, simple ceramic dish suitable for soy sauce or extra mayo sits nearby, complementing the Asian-inspired dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice on the side
Offer additional small dishes of kimchi or pickled daikon for extra crunch and fermented flavor
Provide a small bowl of miso soup as a starter
instructions: Prepare carrot slaw: Peel carrots. Julienne carrots into thin matchsticks. Set aside in a bowl.
Make slaw dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together rice vinegar, 15 ml soy sauce, 10 ml sesame oil, and sugar until sugar dissolves.
Toss julienned carrots with slaw dressing. Mix well. Set aside.
Prepare spicy Gochujang mayo: In a separate bowl, combine mayonnaise, Gochujang, remaining 15 ml soy sauce, and remaining 5 ml sesame oil. Stir until smooth. Adjust spice level if desired.
Prepare tuna: Pat tuna steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat cooking oil in a large non-stick or cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering and almost smoking.

Carefully place tuna steaks in hot skillet. Sear for 1-2 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Ensure internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare, or 75°C (167°F) for well-done.
Remove tuna from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Slice tuna into thick chunks or medallions, approximately 2-3 cm thick. Do not fan out slices.

To plate: Arrange a bed of Asian carrot slaw on one side of each white porcelain plate. Place seared tuna chunks beside the slaw. Drizzle spicy Gochujang mayo generously over the tuna and around the plate.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: For food safety, ensure tuna reaches an internal temperature of at least 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare. For well-done, cook to 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Breast, Whipped Ricotta, Sweet Pea Purée, Caramelized Pearl Onions, Jalapeño Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated, minimalist composition on an elegant bone china plate. A vibrant, smooth sweep of bright green sweet pea purée anchors one side. Adjacent, a perfectly seared, golden-skinned chicken breast, crisp and taut, serves as the focal point. Beside it, a cloud-like dollop of airy, whipped ricotta adds creamy contrast. Artfully scattered around the chicken are translucent, amber caramelized pearl onions. A delicate drizzle of golden-green jalapeño vinaigrette weaves across the plate. Minimal, precise garnishes include paper-thin pickled jalapeño slices and crispy shallots, adding visual and textural interest. Abundant negative space emphasizes the individual beauty and sophisticated simplicity of the artfully arranged elements. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a single, refined portion.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal chicken breasts. Cook sous vide at 63°C for 1.5 hours. Remove from bag, pat very dry.
Peel pearl onions. Sauté in 10g butter until lightly browned. Add 50ml white wine and 50ml chicken stock. Simmer until tender and liquid reduces to a glaze.

Blanch green peas in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well. Blend peas with 50ml chicken stock, 10g butter, and a few mint leaves until very smooth. Season with salt. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Place ricotta in a fine-mesh sieve over a bowl for 30 minutes to drain excess liquid. Transfer drained ricotta to a bowl. Whip with a whisk until light and airy. Season lightly with salt.
Finely dice 2 pickled jalapeño chilies. Whisk together 30ml olive oil, 15ml apple cider vinegar, 5ml honey, and diced jalapeño. Season with salt and pepper.
Grate Parmesan cheese finely. Spoon small mounds onto a non-stick baking mat. Bake at 180°C until golden and crisp (approx. 5-7 minutes). Cool on a wire rack.

Heat 10ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp. Flip and sear flesh side for 1-2 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
Thinly slice shallots. Fry in a small amount of oil until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towel. Season with salt.

Spoon a sweep of pea purée onto each plate. Place one seared chicken breast beside the purée. Add a generous dollop of whipped ricotta. Arrange caramelized pearl onions around the chicken. Drizzle jalapeño vinaigrette over and around the chicken. Garnish with a few thin slices of pickled jalapeño, crispy shallots, and a parmesan tuile.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Stuffed with Jalapeño Cream Cheese, Pea Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, is presented as two thick, tender medallions, showcasing its creamy, molten jalapeno-cheese filling. The chicken rests on a generous bed of pale green, flowing pea and caramelized onion risotto. The risotto is creamy, with visible vibrant green peas and soft, translucent onion pieces. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes both the chicken and risotto, adding a pop of color. The dish is served on a clean white round porcelain plate, leaving moderate negative space. The composition is balanced and inviting, highlighting the refined textures and natural colors of the ingredients. It is set on a simple wooden table, with standard silver flatware and a cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Combine cream cheese, finely diced pickled jalapeños, shredded cheddar, and minced small onion in a bowl. Mix well.
Spoon filling into each butterflied chicken breast. Fold chicken over to enclose filling. Secure edges with toothpicks.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While chicken bakes, prepare risotto. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in a separate saucepan over medium heat.
Add finely chopped medium onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add hot chicken broth, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding more.
Continue adding broth for 15-20 minutes, until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in green peas for the last 3 minutes of cooking.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in remaining 20g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Remove toothpicks.
Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick medallions.
Serve chicken medallions over a generous portion of pea and caramelized onion risotto. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Jalapeno Cream and Pea Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast rests slightly off-center on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Adjacent to the chicken, a generous, gently mounded portion of creamy, off-white green pea risotto is neatly placed. The risotto features vibrant green whole peas and finely diced onion. A rich, pale yellow creamy jalapeno sauce is artfully drizzled over the chicken and around the plate, creating subtle pools, with visible flecks of bright green and orange from the finely diced pickled jalapenos. A light scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley or cilantro garnishes the chicken and risotto. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is positioned to the left. Standard polished silver flatware is placed to the sides. Natural, even overhead lighting illuminates the scene. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant ambiance.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside. Keep warm.
In the same skillet, melt 15 g butter with remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast lightly.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add chicken broth 120 ml at a time. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed before adding more. Continue for 20-25 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in green peas and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook 2 minutes until peas are tender. Stir in remaining 15 g butter. Season risotto with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the sauce, return the skillet to medium heat. Add heavy cream and cream cheese. Whisk until smooth. Add finely diced pickled jalapenos. Stir until combined. Season with salt and pepper.

To serve, place a portion of pea risotto on each plate. Top with a pan-seared chicken breast. Spoon creamy jalapeno sauce over chicken and around the plate. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions and Chicken with Creamy Garlic Parmesan Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared Beef Medallions and Chicken with Creamy Garlic Parmesan Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine forms a loose, appealing nest in the center. Two golden-brown seared beef medallions, approximately 2.5 cm thick, are positioned alongside several succulent, seared chicken chunks. Both meats exhibit a beautiful, caramelized crust. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the pasta. The dish is garnished with a scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. The background features a modern bistro setting with a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and subtle, natural even lighting. The scene is clean, professional, and inviting, highlighting the dish as the focal point. Beef is presented as thick medallions, chicken as substantial chunks.
instructions: Pat beef tenderloin dry. Cut into 2.5 cm thick medallions. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef medallions 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Remove beef from skillet. Set aside. Keep warm.

Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add chicken chunks. Cook 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside with beef.
While meat cooks, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine. Cook according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add butter. Mince garlic. Add garlic to skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in heavy cream and chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add cooked fettuccine to the sauce. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Divide pasta among four plates. Arrange seared beef medallions and chicken chunks over the pasta.
Garnish each plate with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Szechuan Lamb & Arame Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Szechuan Lamb & Arame Rice Bowl is presented in a clean, wide white porcelain bowl, resting on a light, natural wooden table surface. The base of the bowl holds a generous mound of fluffy white jasmine rice. On top of the rice, a vibrant mix of crumbled, browned lamb sausage and dark, rehydrated arame seaweed is neatly mounded. The lamb is in irregular, well-cooked chunks, and the arame forms dark, glossy strands intertwined with the lamb. The lamb and arame mixture is coated in a glossy, reddish-brown Szechuan sauce, showing hints of its spicy richness. A creamy, pale yellow savory mayonnaise is artfully drizzled in a zig-zag pattern over the lamb and arame, creating visual contrast and a soft texture. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green spring onions, scattered lightly over the top for freshness and color. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space around the central dish. Beside the bowl, a set of dark, simple chopsticks rests on a small ceramic chopstick rest. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. The background is a softly blurred, neutral restaurant setting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with chopsticks
A small side dish of pickled daikon or kimchi can accompany the bowl
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice. Combine rice and water in a pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Place dried arame in a bowl. Cover with warm water. Let soak 10 minutes until soft. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop if strands are too long.
Remove lamb sausage from casings.
Heat neutral oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add lamb sausage. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned and crumbled, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the pan with lamb. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add rehydrated arame. Stir to combine.
Pour Szechuan sauce, soy sauce, and rice vinegar into the pan. Stir well. Cook 2-3 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly and coats lamb and arame. Stir in sesame oil.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise and finely chopped fresh savory. Mix well.
Divide cooked rice among 4 bowls. Spoon lamb and arame mixture over rice. Drizzle with savory mayonnaise. Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions.
notes: Savory herb provides an earthy, slightly peppery note to the mayonnaise.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana Chocolate Chip Pancakes with Cottage Cheese
recipes.special_requests: I have only pan, recipe must be like for 15-20 minutes to make, i have 2 eggs, breakfast for 800 ccal, maybe some banana chocko pancakes?
recipes.visual_description: A comforting stack of three golden-brown banana chocolate chip pancakes is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The pancakes are unevenly shaped, showcasing their homemade origin. Melted butter pools slightly on the top pancake, with scattered, plump frozen blueberries peeking from between the layers and on top. The interior reveals the dark specks of cocoa and the soft texture from the mashed banana. The plate rests on a well-used wooden kitchen table. A casually placed cloth napkin and a small, traditional pitcher of maple syrup are visible nearby. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the inviting textures and homely appeal of the breakfast.
instructions: Mash banana in a medium bowl until smooth.
Add eggs, milk, and 5g melted butter to mashed banana. Whisk until well combined.
In a separate bowl, combine whole wheat flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir gently until just combined. Do not overmix. A few lumps are fine.
Fold in cottage cheese and frozen blueberries.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add remaining 5g butter to coat the pan.
Pour quarter cup portions of batter onto the hot pan. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and bubbles form on the surface. Flip and cook another 1-2 minutes.
Repeat with remaining batter. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Lamb Shanks with Red Wine and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously sized braised lamb shank, rich deep brown, rests on a creamy bed of golden polenta. The lamb, fork-tender, is coated in a glossy, dark red wine reduction. Garnished with a fresh sprig of rosemary and a few vibrant green thyme leaves. Scattered around are a few bright orange roasted carrot batons, adding color and texture. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple, light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery are neatly arranged beside the plate. The scene is lit with soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the elegantly plated dish. Portion size is for one individual, showcasing a refined yet hearty meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes, polenta, or crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Pair with a full-bodied red wine like a Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot
instructions: Pat lamb shanks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sear shanks on all sides until deep golden brown. Remove shanks and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, reducing slightly.
Add beef broth, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs. Return seared lamb shanks to the pot. Ensure shanks are mostly submerged. If not, add more broth or water.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until lamb is fork-tender and easily pulls from the bone. Turn shanks halfway through cooking.
Remove shanks from the pot. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids and herbs.
Skim any excess fat from the sauce. Bring sauce to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until slightly thickened to a desired consistency.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Return lamb shanks to the sauce or spoon sauce over shanks before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana Chocolate Chip Pancakes
recipes.special_requests: I have only pan, recipe must be like for 15-20 minutes to make, i have 2 eggs, breakfast for 800 ccal, maybe some banana chocko pancakes?
recipes.visual_description: A stack of three golden-brown pancakes, approximately 10 cm in diameter, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain breakfast plate. The pancakes are evenly cooked with a slightly crisp edge and fluffy interior, showing subtle specks of cocoa powder. A generous drizzle of golden maple syrup cascades down the sides of the stack. Scattered around the base of the pancakes and on top are vibrant, plump blue blueberries. The overall presentation is clean and inviting. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating soft shadows and highlighting the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with additional maple syrup.
Accompany with a glass of milk or coffee.
instructions: Mash banana in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs. Add cottage cheese and milk. Blend until smooth.
In a large bowl, whisk whole wheat flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt.
Pour wet mixture into dry ingredients. Add mashed banana. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Heat 10g butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour batter to form three pancakes, approximately 10 cm in diameter.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Stack pancakes on a plate. Top with frozen blueberries.
Drizzle generously with maple syrup. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe yields approximately 800 kcal.
Preparation and cooking time is approximately 15-20 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana-Blueberry Layered Crepe 'Millefoglie'
recipes.special_requests: I have only pan, recipe must be like for 15-20 minutes to make
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly stacked monoportion of Banana-Blueberry Layered Crepes, presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Three to four thin, golden-brown whole wheat banana-cocoa crepes form delicate layers, revealing creamy white cottage cheese filling and vibrant dark purple blueberry compote peeking between them. The crepes exhibit a soft, pliable texture with subtly crisp edges. A rich, glossy dark chocolate drizzle, made from cocoa powder and melted butter, is artfully zigzagged across the top crepe and allowed to gently cascade down the sides. A few plump, glistening fresh blueberries are placed thoughtfully beside the stack, adding a pop of natural color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded light grey cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Mash ripe banana well in a bowl. Add whole wheat flour, 1 egg, 40ml milk, 3g cocoa powder, and a pinch of salt. Whisk until smooth. Adjust with a few milliliters of water or remaining milk if batter is too thick; it should be thin.

Heat a small non-stick pan over medium heat. Melt 2g butter and swirl to coat the pan. Pour a thin layer of batter (approx. 40ml) to form one crepe. Cook 1-2 minutes until edges crisp and surface bubbles. Flip. Cook 30-60 seconds more. Transfer to a plate. Repeat 2-3 more times for a total of 3-4 crepes, using 2g butter for each crepe. Stack cooked crepes.
In the same pan, combine frozen blueberries and 5ml maple syrup. Cook over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until berries burst and sauce thickens slightly. Remove from pan.
In a small bowl, combine cottage cheese, remaining 10ml milk, and 10ml maple syrup. Whisk until smooth and creamy.

Assemble the 'millefoglie'. Place one crepe on a serving plate. Spread a thin layer of cottage cheese cream. Spoon a portion of blueberry compote. Top with another crepe. Repeat layers, ending with a crepe on top.

Melt remaining 7g butter with 2g cocoa powder and 5ml maple syrup in the pan for 30 seconds to create a simple chocolate drizzle. Drizzle this over the stacked crepes. Garnish with a few fresh blueberries. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana Blueberry Cocoa Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly formed mini entremet sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The entremet, approximately 7 cm in diameter and 5 cm high, is coated in a mirror-like, dark cocoa glaze, reflecting ambient light. Its sides are smooth and precise, indicative of professional molding. A few fresh, plump blueberries are artfully placed beside the entremet, providing a vibrant color contrast. The base is a thin layer of cocoa whole wheat sponge. The interior, when sliced, reveals distinct layers: a creamy, pale yellow banana cottage cheese mousse enveloping a deep purple, solid blueberry insert. Textures are harmonious: soft cake, smooth mousse, slightly firm fruit gel, and a delicate, crisp glaze. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table and a cotton napkin beside the plate, all under soft, natural lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a small baking pan (approx. 10x10 cm).
Separate one egg. Whisk 1 whole egg and 15g sugar until pale and fluffy. Sift 15g whole wheat flour, 5g cocoa powder, and baking powder into egg mixture. Fold gently.

Melt 10g butter. Combine with 10ml milk. Fold into batter. Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake 10-12 minutes, or until cooked through. Cool completely. Cut a 6 cm diameter round base for the entremet.
Bloom 1g gelatin leaf in cold water.

Combine 30g frozen blueberries, 5g sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Heat gently until blueberries soften. Mix 2g cornstarch with 5ml cold water to create a slurry. Stir into blueberry mixture. Cook until thickened.

Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into hot blueberry mixture until dissolved. Pour into a 4 cm diameter round mold or onto plastic wrap to form a disc. Freeze until solid.
Bloom 1g gelatin leaf in cold water.
Mash 50g ripe banana thoroughly. In a blender, combine mashed banana, 50g cottage cheese, 20ml milk, the remaining egg yolk, and 10g sugar. Blend until very smooth.
Gently heat a small portion of the blended mixture. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into warm mixture until dissolved. Combine gelatin mixture with remaining banana mixture.

In a separate clean bowl, whisk the remaining egg white until soft peaks form. Gradually add 5g sugar, whisking until stiff, glossy peaks form. Gently fold meringue into the banana-cottage cheese mixture.

Line a 7 cm diameter ring mold with an acetate strip. Place on a tray. Place the cocoa sponge base at the bottom of the mold. Pour half of the banana mousse over the sponge. Gently place the frozen blueberry insert on top of the mousse. Pour remaining banana mousse over the blueberry insert, filling the mold. Smooth the top. Freeze for at least 4 hours, or until completely solid.
Bloom 1g gelatin leaf in cold water.

In a saucepan, combine 10g cocoa powder, 20g sugar, and 30ml milk. Bring to a gentle simmer, whisking constantly. Cook 1 minute. Remove from heat. Stir in 15g butter until melted. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into hot glaze until dissolved. Strain glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool to 30-35°C.

Remove frozen entremet from mold. Place on a wire rack over a baking tray. Pour lukewarm cocoa glaze evenly over the entremet. Allow excess glaze to drip off. Carefully transfer the glazed entremet to a serving plate.
Thaw in the refrigerator for 1-2 hours before serving. Garnish with fresh blueberries.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana Blueberry Tartlet
recipes.visual_description: The single Banana Blueberry Tartlet is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dessert plate. Its golden-brown whole wheat crust is precisely crimped, holding a creamy, baked banana filling. The filling has a subtle golden hue, slightly puffed, with visible specks of mashed banana. A generous spooning of vibrant, dark purple blueberry compote covers the center, showcasing plump, burst blueberries glistening with their natural juices. A delicate dusting of deep brown cocoa powder lightly coats the edges of the blueberry topping and spills onto the plate's rim, providing a rich contrast. The tartlet is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a small dessert fork beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dessert, highlighting its balanced colors and inviting textures.
instructions: Prepare dough: Combine flour, cold butter, salt in a bowl. Rub butter into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add cold water. Mix until dough forms. Flatten into a disc. Chill 30 minutes.
Preheat oven: Set oven to 180°C.
Form crust: Roll dough on lightly floured surface to 3mm thickness. Cut a circle to fit a 10cm tartlet pan. Press dough into pan. Trim edges. Prick bottom with a fork.
Blind bake: Line crust with parchment paper. Fill with pie weights. Bake 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake 5-7 minutes more until light golden. Cool crust.
Prepare filling: Mash banana. In a bowl, whisk egg yolk, milk, cottage cheese, 15g sugar, and vanilla. Stir in mashed banana.
Bake tartlet: Pour banana filling into cooled crust. Bake 20-25 minutes, until filling is set and lightly golden. Cool completely.
Prepare blueberry topping: In a small saucepan, combine blueberries and 5g sugar. Cook over medium heat 5-7 minutes, until blueberries soften. Cool slightly.
Assemble: Spoon blueberry topping over cooled tartlet. Lightly dust with cocoa powder.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cheesy Chicken Thighs with Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spicy Cheesy Chicken Thighs with Brown Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of creamy, vibrant orange-hued brown rice, infused with hot sauce and melted cheddar, forms the base. Nestled atop the rice are two to three thick, golden-brown seared chicken thigh chunks, showcasing a crispy exterior and tender interior. The dish is garnished with a scattering of thinly sliced bright green onions, providing a fresh contrast in color and texture. The plating is organized and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and standard silverware beside the plate, under natural, even lighting, evoking a casual American bistro atmosphere. The focus is entirely on the food, highlighting its appealing textures and rich colors.
instructions: Rinse brown rice. Cook according to package directions using 400ml chicken broth instead of water. Set aside, keep warm.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Stir in hot sauce. Bring to a simmer.
Add cooked brown rice to the skillet. Stir well to combine with the hot sauce mixture. Remove from heat.
Stir in shredded cheddar cheese until completely melted and creamy.
Slice each chicken thigh into 2-3 thick chunks or serve whole. Do not fan slices.
Portion cheesy hot rice onto individual plates. Top with seared chicken chunks. Garnish with sliced green onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato Relish and Corn Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken thigh, skin-side up, presents a rich, golden-brown and crispy surface. It rests on a minimalist, cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate. Adjacent to the chicken is a generous, naturally mounded portion of fluffy, pale yellow corn rice, visibly studded with vibrant yellow corn kernels and flecked with bright green chopped parsley and cilantro. A spoonful of the Quick Fermented Tomato Relish, showcasing its diced red tomatoes and finely minced red onion, is artfully placed atop the chicken or beside it, adding a pop of fresh, tangy color. The plating is clean and unforced, with ample negative space. The background is a light, natural-textured surface, possibly reclaimed wood or bamboo, complemented by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the varied textures and natural colors of the ingredients. The entire plate is visible, emphasizing a refined, sustainable single-serving portion.
instructions: Prepare Quick Fermented Tomato Relish: Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Finely mince red onion. In a clean bowl, combine diced tomatoes, minced red onion, and 10g salt. Mix well. Press down to submerge. Cover loosely. Let macerate at room temperature for at least 2 hours, or ideally overnight, to draw out liquid and develop flavor. Drain any excess liquid before serving.

Prepare Corn Rice: Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Mince garlic. Heat 10ml olive oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add rinsed rice. Stir for 1 minute. Add 600ml water or vegetable stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly. Cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in corn kernels and chopped parsley and cilantro. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken thighs thoroughly dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides. Heat 20ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until the skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Continue cooking for 5-7 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest for 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon a generous portion of Corn Rice onto each of four handcrafted ceramic plates. Place one seared chicken thigh beside the rice. Spoon the Quick Fermented Tomato Relish over the chicken or alongside the rice. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Vegan Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta with Mixed Berry and Apple Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vegan vanilla bean panna cotta is centrally plated on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The panna cotta is a smooth, ivory dome, perfectly unmolded, showcasing its creamy texture. It is generously topped with a vibrant mixed berry and apple compote. The compote features ruby-red strawberry pieces, whole raspberries, and soft, translucent diced apple cubes, creating a rich, glossy, and slightly chunky texture. A few fresh green mint leaves are artfully placed on the compote, adding a pop of contrasting color. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin positioned neatly beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and refined presentation. The background suggests a casual restaurant atmosphere, minimal and unobtrusive, allowing the dessert to be the sole focus.

ingredients.name: Plant-based cream (e.g., oat or soy cream)

instructions: Slice vanilla bean lengthwise. Scrape out seeds.
Combine coconut milk, plant-based cream, sugar, vanilla bean pod, and seeds in a saucepan.
Heat mixture over medium heat until simmering. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Remove vanilla bean pod.
Whisk agar-agar powder into the hot cream mixture. Whisk constantly for 2 minutes to ensure agar-agar dissolves completely.
Pour mixture into four 150 ml ramekins or molds.
Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until fully set.
For the compote: Wash strawberries and raspberries. Hull and quarter strawberries. Peel, core, and dice the apple into 1 cm cubes.
Combine strawberries, raspberries, diced apple, and lemon juice in a separate saucepan.
Cook over medium heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Cook until fruit softens and mixture thickens slightly.
Remove from heat. Let compote cool to room temperature.
To serve: Dip bottom of panna cotta molds briefly in hot water. Invert onto individual serving plates.
Spoon cooled fruit compote generously over each panna cotta.
Garnish each with a few fresh mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Garlic Roasted Chicken Thighs with Crispy Potatoes and Garlic Herb Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Lemon Garlic Roasted Chicken Thighs with Crispy Potatoes and Garlic Herb Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, skin-on, bone-in roasted chicken thigh is the focal point, positioned off-center. Beside it, a cluster of golden-crisp smashed potatoes, showing rustic edges and soft interiors, are arranged. A mound of vibrant green garlic herb pasta, lightly coated, sits adjacent. A perfectly fried egg with a runny yolk, slightly crispy edges, rests atop the chicken. Pan juices glisten. Garnish with fresh parsley leaves and a bright lemon wedge. Colors are natural: golden, pale yellow, bright green. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are beside it. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights textures. The background is a subtly blurred, casual bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30 ml olive oil, 4 minced garlic cloves, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs skin-side up on a baking sheet. Scatter seasoned potatoes around chicken. Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Gently smash each potato with a masher or fork. Drizzle with remaining 30 ml olive oil. Return to oven.
Continue roasting chicken and potatoes for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are crispy and golden.
While chicken roasts, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.

In the empty pasta pot, melt butter over medium heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Add drained pasta. Add lemon zest, a splash of reserved pasta water (if needed), and half the chopped fresh parsley. Toss to combine.
While pasta cooks, fry or poach eggs. Cook to desired doneness.
Place a portion of garlic herb pasta on each plate. Arrange a roasted chicken thigh and a portion of crispy smashed potatoes next to the pasta. Top each dish with a cooked egg.
Drizzle chicken and potatoes with pan juices. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges and remaining chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken & Potato Tortilla
recipes.visual_description: A thick wedge of Spanish Chicken & Potato Tortilla is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The tortilla exhibits a beautiful golden-brown exterior, slightly domed, indicating a perfectly cooked crust. Its interior, revealed by the clean cut, shows tender, thinly sliced potato rounds and translucent onion intertwined with diced, pan-seared chicken cubes, all bound together by the rich, creamy egg. The texture is firm yet moist and yielding. A scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color. Beside the tortilla, a small, fresh green salad of mixed leaves with a light vinaigrette provides a contrasting crisp texture and natural color balance. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, evoking a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up any juices.
Accompanied by a simple green salad.
Often served with a dollop of aioli on the side.
Traditionally enjoyed warm or at room temperature.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Thinly slice them into 2-3mm rounds. Peel and thinly slice the onion.
