Heat 120ml olive oil in a 24cm non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add potatoes and onion. Season with salt. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until very tender but not browned, about 20-25 minutes. Drain excess oil from potatoes and onions, reserving oil if desired.
While potatoes cook, dice chicken thighs into 1.5 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt, pepper, minced garlic, and smoked paprika.
Heat 15ml fresh olive oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C), about 5-7 minutes. Set aside.

In a large bowl, whisk eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. Add cooked potatoes, onions, and seared chicken to the egg mixture. Gently fold to combine. Let sit for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Wipe the 24cm non-stick pan clean. Add 15ml fresh olive oil to the pan and heat over medium heat until shimmering. Pour the egg-potato-chicken mixture into the hot pan. Spread evenly.
Cook for 5-7 minutes without disturbing, until the edges are set and golden, but the center is still slightly runny.
Place a large flat plate (larger than the pan) over the pan. Invert the pan to flip the tortilla onto the plate.
Slide the tortilla back into the pan, uncooked side down. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, shaping the sides to create a smooth, rounded edge. Ensure the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Slide the tortilla onto a serving plate. Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing into wedges.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Ensure potatoes and onions are very tender before mixing with eggs; this is key to a creamy tortilla interior.
Do not overcrowd the pan when cooking potatoes and onions to ensure even cooking.
traditional_techniques: Frying potatoes and onions slowly until tender (confitado)
Cooking the tortilla in a pan and flipping it to cook both sides

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Broth presented in a matte, handcrafted ceramic bowl in a natural cream tone, on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The clear, golden-amber broth holds naturally settled components: tender, shredded chicken pieces, 1.5cm diced potato cubes, and individual brown rice grains. Garnish is minimalistic: a delicate sprinkle of finely chopped chives, a few paper-thin slices of quick-pickled red onion, and a single halved cherry tomato floating gently. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige rests beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting inherent textures and colors. The background is clean, with a hint of blurred greenery. The composition emphasizes purity, sustainability, and natural beauty, with ample negative space.

ingredients.name: Chicken bones (from 2 chicken thighs or 1 carcass)
Onion
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium (halved for broth, small portion thinly sliced for garnish)

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (e.g., Desiree or Yukon Gold), diced into 1.5cm cubes

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves
ingredients.quantity: 3 (2 for broth, 1 minced for fermented tomato water)

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.quantity: 1 large (quartered for broth), plus 2 small ripe cherry tomatoes (for garnish)

instructions: Prepare chicken bones, carrot, celery, 2 garlic cloves, and one quartered large tomato for broth. Place in a large pot with 1.5 L water. Add chicken breast/thigh. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 45 minutes, skimming impurities.
Remove chicken breast/thigh from broth. Set aside to cool. Continue simmering broth for another 30 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Keep broth warm.
Shred the cooked chicken into natural pieces once cool enough to handle. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.

Prepare fermented tomato water: Finely mince 1 garlic clove. Combine with 50g of tomato pulp (from the large tomato, after quartering for broth) and 5g salt. Place in a small jar. Cover with water. Let sit at room temperature for 24-48 hours until slightly bubbly and tangy. Strain liquid; this is your fermented tomato water.

In a separate pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion (from the large onion, not the sliced portion for garnish) and diced potato cubes. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until onion softens slightly.
Add the strained chicken broth and cooked brown rice to the pot with onion and potato. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in the shredded chicken and the prepared fermented tomato water. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste.

Ladle soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives or parsley, a few paper-thin slices of quick-pickled red onion, and one halved cherry tomato floating gently on the surface.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Roasted Potatoes and Cherry-Apple Chutney
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a refined single serving on a clean, white round porcelain plate, on a simple wooden surface. A perfectly seared beef medallion, displaying a rich, browned crust, is positioned centrally. Alongside, golden-brown roasted potato chunks, fluffy inside, are arranged organically. A neat mound of deeply caramelized onions, glistening with amber hues, sits near the beef. A vibrant, jewel-toned cherry-apple chutney, with visible fruit pieces, is spooned artfully, adding a pop of dark red. A small, fresh side salad of crisp mixed greens and halved bright red cherry tomatoes, lightly dressed, occupies the remaining space. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing each component to stand out. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the ingredients, set against a soft, blurred restaurant background. Simple silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin are placed beside the plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm chunks or wedges. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.

While potatoes roast, prepare caramelized onions. Thinly slice brown onions. Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden and soft.

Make cherry-apple chutney. Peel, core, and dice apples. In a saucepan, combine diced apples, pitted cherries, 15ml Worcestershire sauce, 30g sugar, 30ml red wine vinegar, and 60ml water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit is tender and liquid thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare beef medallions. Pat beef dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness. Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to the pan during the last minute of cooking. Remove beef from pan. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Prepare salad. Halve cherry tomatoes. Dress mixed salad greens and halved cherry tomatoes with a simple vinaigrette (e.g., olive oil and vinegar/lemon juice).

To plate, place one seared beef medallion on each plate. Arrange a portion of roasted potato chunks alongside. Add a dollop of caramelized onions and a spoonful of cherry-apple chutney. Serve a small side of dressed salad. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired. Serve immediately with crusty bread.
notes: Adjust beef cooking time to achieve your desired level of doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Tofu and Vegetable Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Tofu and Vegetable Stir-fry is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, suitable for a homely family kitchen setting. Golden-brown, pan-seared tofu cubes are interspersed throughout. Bright green broccoli florets, vivid red and yellow bell pepper slices, and orange carrot rounds are visible. All ingredients are coated in a glossy, dark amber stir-fry sauce. The dish is piled naturally, with ingredients overlapping, creating an inviting, abundant look. A sprinkle of white sesame seeds and thinly sliced green spring onions adds a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple white ceramic plate with a modest portion of steamed white rice is placed beside it. A pair of wooden chopsticks rests casually on the table. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene. The presentation is unpretentious and comforting, reflecting a home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of chili garlic sauce for added heat.
instructions: Press tofu for 20 minutes. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, cornstarch, and vegetable broth in a small bowl. Stir well. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes to the hot pan. Cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides. This takes about 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu from pan and set aside.
Add sliced onion and carrot rounds to the same pan. Stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add bell pepper slices and broccoli florets. Continue to stir-fry for 3-4 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the pan. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return cooked tofu to the pan with the vegetables. Stir to combine.
Stir the reserved sauce mixture again, then pour it over the tofu and vegetables. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients.
Serve immediately. Garnish with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.
notes: Pressing tofu removes excess water, allowing it to absorb flavors better and crisp up during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty beef and vegetable soup is presented in a deep, rustic off-white ceramic bowl with an irregular rim. The soup is a rich, savory brown, filled with substantial chunks of seared beef chuck (2.5 cm cubes) and tender, vibrantly colored vegetables. Visually prominent are 1 cm rounds of carrots, 1 cm pieces of celery, and 2 cm potato cubes, all retaining their distinct forms and textures. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a bright green contrast on top. The bowl sits on a warm, well-worn wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple silver soup spoon and a casually draped linen napkin. Soft, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and subtle steam. The background hints at a homely, lived-in kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with crusty bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, diced into 2.5 cm cubes
Carrots, peeled and sliced into 1 cm rounds
Celery stalks, sliced into 1 cm pieces
Potatoes, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth, diced tomatoes, bay leaf, and dried thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender.
Add diced potatoes to the pot. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For a richer flavor, brown the beef thoroughly before adding liquids. Adjust vegetable cooking time based on desired tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato Consommé, Chicken Roulade, Parmesan Tortellini
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a refined soup is presented in a wide, shallow, matte white bone china bowl. The clear, vibrant red-orange tomato consommé acts as a luminous liquid base. At the center, arranged with artistic precision, are one or two pale, thick, perfectly round medallions of chicken roulade, showcasing clean knife work. Nestled alongside are three to five delicate, pale yellow Parmesan tortellini, their handmade folds visible, and an equal number of tiny, off-white, pillowy potato gnocchi. Each element is placed with purpose, creating a natural, organic composition with abundant negative space around them. A few precise drops or a thin, elegant swirl of vibrant red chili oil float on the consommé's surface, adding a contrasting pop of color and subtle sheen. A single, fresh micro basil or micro parsley leaf is placed delicately on a chicken medallion, providing a final touch of verdant green. The bowl rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface, beside it an elegant silver soup spoon positioned on a pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle. The scene is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft, intentional shadows that enhance the dish's depth and highlight the clarity of the consommé, all set against an ultra-minimalist background with maximum negative space.

ingredients.name: Micro basil or micro parsley for garnish

instructions: Prepare Tomato Consommé: Roughly chop tomatoes, shallots, and garlic. Combine in a pot with chicken stock, half the basil, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 30 minutes. Do not boil. Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve. Pass through a coffee filter or multiple layers of cheesecloth until perfectly clear. Season to taste. Set aside.

Prepare Chicken Roulade: Pound chicken breasts to 1 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper. Finely chop remaining basil and chives. Sprinkle herbs evenly over chicken. Roll each breast tightly into a cylinder. Tie with butcher's twine. Sous vide at 65°C for 2 hours, or gently poach in water until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Chill immediately. Once chilled, remove twine and slice into 2 cm thick medallions.

Prepare Parmesan Tortellini: Sift flour onto a clean surface. Make a well in the center. Crack 1 egg and 1 yolk into the well. Mix with a fork, gradually incorporating flour to form a dough. Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes. For filling, combine grated Parmesan, ricotta, a pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Roll pasta dough very thinly (1 mm). Cut into 3 cm squares. Place a small amount of filling in the center of each square. Fold into tortellini shapes. Cook fresh in rapidly boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until al dente. Drain.

Prepare Potato Gnocchi: Wash and boil potatoes in their skins until tender. Peel immediately. Pass through a potato ricer or mash finely. Cool slightly. Mix with 50g flour, 1 egg yolk, and a pinch of salt until just combined. Do not overmix. Roll dough into thin ropes (1 cm diameter). Cut into 1 cm pieces. Cook fresh in rapidly boiling salted water for 1-2 minutes until they float. Drain.
Prepare Chili Oil: Gently heat olive oil in a small saucepan. Add chili flakes. Steep for 10 minutes over very low heat. Do not burn. Strain oil, discarding flakes. Set aside.

Assemble and Serve: Gently warm the tomato consommé. Place 1-2 chicken medallions, 3-5 tortellini, and 3-5 potato gnocchi artfully in the center of each wide, shallow serving bowl. Carefully pour warm consommé around the components, filling the bowl to just cover the elements. Drizzle a few precise drops of chili oil over the soup. Garnish with a single micro basil or micro parsley leaf placed delicately on a chicken medallion. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Red Wine and Pearl Onions
recipes.visual_description: A rich, rustic main course presented in a simple, elegant restaurant style. Large, tender chunks of braised beef, deep mahogany in color, are nestled on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef is accompanied by glistening, whole pearl onions and quartered cremini mushrooms, all coated in a thick, glossy, dark red wine reduction sauce. The sauce pools invitingly around the ingredients, showcasing its depth and richness. Scattered fresh chopped parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. The textures are soft and yielding for the beef, with a slight firmness remaining in the onions and mushrooms. The dish is centered on the plate, with moderate negative space, evoking a professional yet approachable presentation. The scene is set on a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard flatware.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with creamy potato purée or mashed potatoes.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef stock, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Liquid should almost cover the beef.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly with a lid.
Transfer the covered pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
During the last 30 minutes of braising, add pearl onions and quartered mushrooms to the pot. Stir gently.
Remove pot from oven. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Stir in butter until melted and incorporated into the sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This dish benefits from being made a day in advance, allowing flavors to meld. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the oven.

recipes.recipe_name: Sopa de Patata y Pimentón
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Paprika Potato Soup is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic bowl, reflecting traditional Spanish pottery. The rich, reddish-orange soup, infused with smoked paprika, has a creamy yet slightly chunky texture from partially mashed potatoes cut into 2cm cubes. A swirl of vibrant green fermented garlic oil glistens on the surface. Crispy, dark capers and golden-brown, 1cm cubed stale bread croutons are artfully scattered across the soup, providing textural contrast. The bowl rests on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood table. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue is folded neatly beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures. The background is minimalist, with a hint of green from a potted plant, maintaining focus on the dish's earthy, sustainable aesthetic. A small, rustic olive wood spoon rests beside the bowl, completing the authentic Spanish setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread
Pair with a dry Fino sherry

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (onion skins, potato peels, tomato cores)

instructions: Prepare Zero-Waste Broth: Combine vegetable scraps, 2 litres water, and 5ml olive oil in a large pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 45 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids.
Make Sofrito: Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 8-10 minutes until soft and translucent. Add minced fresh garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Paprika and Tomato: Stir in smoked paprika. Cook 30 seconds, stirring constantly. Add chopped fresh tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Simmer Soup: Add potato cubes and strained vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 15-20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Adjust Consistency: Remove 1/4 of potatoes. Mash or blend them. Return to soup. Stir to thicken. Alternatively, use an immersion blender to partially blend for desired consistency.
Season: Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Prepare Garnish: Heat a small pan with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry capers until crispy. Remove. Drain on paper towel. In the same pan, toast stale bread cubes until golden brown and crisp.
Prepare Fermented Garlic Oil: In a small bowl, combine 50ml olive oil with minced fermented garlic. Stir well.
Serve: Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Drizzle each serving with fermented garlic oil. Garnish with crispy capers and toasted bread croutons. Serve immediately.
notes: Fermented garlic can be made by submerging peeled garlic cloves in a 2% brine (20g salt per litre water) in a clean jar for 1-2 weeks at room temperature, then storing in the fridge. Use these fermented cloves for the oil.
Stale bread can be frozen and used for croutons later.
Vegetable scraps from other cooking can be frozen until enough are collected for broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken & Cheddar Pasta Bake
recipes.special_requests: русская, итальянская, японская, американская cuisine, кухня без сахара, правильное питание
recipes.visual_description: The Creamy Chicken & Cheddar Pasta Bake is presented in a modest, round ceramic baking dish, slightly browned and bubbling from the oven. The top crust of golden-brown panko breadcrumbs is visibly crisp, contrasting with the creamy, rich pasta and chicken beneath. Diced chicken pieces, cooked to a tender texture, are mixed throughout the elbow macaroni, which is coated in a velvety, pale orange cheddar cheese sauce. A few small, bright green flecks of chopped fresh parsley are sprinkled over the top. The dish is placed on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. Beside the dish, a simple white ceramic plate holds a single, hearty portion of the pasta bake. A silver fork rests casually on the plate. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, with warm, soft lighting emanating from overhead fixtures, casting gentle shadows. The overall scene is homey and inviting, emphasizing comfort and simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish at the family table.
Accompany with a simple green salad with vinaigrette.
Offer hot sauce on the side for those who prefer a little heat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Cook chicken until fully browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
In the same pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until sauce is smooth and thickened. Bring to a simmer.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
Add cooked chicken and drained pasta to the cheese sauce. Stir to combine.
Transfer mixture to a small oven-safe dish (approx. 500 ml capacity).
Sprinkle breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until bubbling and breadcrumbs are golden brown and crispy.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Broccoli Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Bell Pepper and Broccoli Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant mix of colors and textures. A bed of fresh, dark green mixed greens or arugula forms the base. Artistically arranged on top are tender, slightly caramelized diced red and yellow bell peppers and small, bright green roasted broccoli florets. Interspersed among the vegetables are creamy, white 1 cm cubes of fresh mozzarella, providing a soft contrast. A glistening, light olive oil vinaigrette lightly coats all components, enhancing their natural sheen. The salad is garnished with golden-brown toasted pine nuts and a few delicate fresh oregano leaves, adding subtle color and texture. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, allowing negative space around the edges of the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with natural, even lighting. Standard flatware is neatly placed beside the plate, and a crisp cotton napkin adds a refined touch. The background is a soft, blurred restaurant-style ambiance, maintaining focus on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty ciabatta bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice bell peppers into 2 cm pieces. Cut broccoli into small florets.
Toss bell peppers and broccoli florets with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
Toast pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until golden. Set aside.
For the dressing, finely mince garlic. Chop fresh oregano leaves.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 50 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, chopped oregano, salt, and pepper.
Cut fresh mozzarella into 1 cm cubes or tear into small pieces.
In a large bowl, combine roasted bell peppers, broccoli, and mozzarella.
Pour dressing over the vegetables and mozzarella. Toss gently to coat.
Arrange mixed greens or arugula on serving plates. Top with the roasted vegetable and mozzarella mixture.
Garnish with toasted pine nuts and a few fresh oregano leaves. Serve immediately or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple Cabbage Slaw
recipes.visual_description: The Fermented Apple Cabbage Slaw is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl, set on a light-toned reclaimed wood surface. The slaw forms a natural, slightly mounded pile, showcasing its vibrant yet muted, earthy colors: the pale green of finely shredded cabbage, the off-white of julienned fermented apple, and subtle orange streaks from julienned carrot. A scattering of golden-brown toasted pumpkin seeds adds textural contrast and visual warmth. A few fresh green dill sprigs are gently placed on top. The composition is clean, with ample white space around the bowl, emphasizing the pure beauty of the natural ingredients. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, crisp textures. An undyed linen napkin rests subtly to the side. The overall presentation is understated and ingredient-focused, celebrating sustainability.
instructions: Shred cabbage finely. Julienne apples and carrot.
Combine cabbage, apples, carrot, and 15g sea salt in a large bowl.
Massage mixture vigorously 5-10 minutes. Liquid will release.
Pack mixture tightly into a clean 1-liter jar. Press down firmly.
Ensure vegetables are fully submerged in liquid. Use a small weight if needed.
Cover jar loosely with lid or cloth. Place in cool, dark spot.
Ferment 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp jar daily to release gas. Taste from day 3.
Refrigerate once fermented.
To serve, drain excess liquid.
Mix with 50g toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped fresh dill.
Season with black pepper.
notes: For zero-waste, save apple cores and peels to make apple scrap vinegar.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Medallions with Caramelized Apple and Thyme Jus
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two or three thick, golden-brown pan-seared pork medallions are arranged centrally. Alongside, caramelized apple wedges, with softened texture and browned edges, are neatly placed. A rich, glossy apple cider and thyme jus is generously spooned over the pork and apples, forming a warm amber pool. Fresh thyme leaves are scattered as a vibrant green garnish. The pork medallions are whole. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. A light grey cotton napkin and standard flatware are beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a softly blurred casual restaurant background.
instructions: Prepare pork. Pat tenderloin dry. Cut into 2.5 cm thick medallions. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Prepare apples. Core apples. Cut into 1 cm thick wedges or large chunks.
Prepare aromatics. Peel and finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Sear pork. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add pork medallions. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 63°C/145°F). Remove pork from skillet. Set aside. Keep warm.

Caramelize apples. Add 15g butter to the same skillet. Add apple wedges. Cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and caramelized. Remove apples. Set aside with pork.
Sauté aromatics. Add remaining 15g butter to the skillet. Add diced shallots. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Deglaze and simmer. Pour in apple cider. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Add chicken stock and Dijon mustard. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, until sauce slightly thickens. Remove thyme sprigs.
Finish sauce. Return pork and apples to the skillet. Spoon sauce over. Simmer gently for 1-2 minutes to heat through. Taste and adjust seasoning.
notes: Serve immediately with creamy mashed potatoes or a simple green salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Carbonnade Flamande
recipes.visual_description: A deep brown, glossy beef stew served in a wide, white porcelain bowl. The dish features large, 4cm tender chunks of braised beef coated in a thick, rich sauce made with dark Belgian ale. Soft, caramelized onion strands are visible throughout the sauce. The stew is positioned centrally with moderate negative space around the edges. A small cluster of fresh parsley and a sprig of thyme garnish the top. The stew sits on a dark wooden bistro table. Beside the bowl is a small side plate with thick-cut, golden-brown Belgian fries and a small ramekin of mayonnaise. A glass of dark abbey ale stands in the background. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the meat and the sheen of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Thick-cut Belgian fries
Fresh mayonnaise
Chilled Belgian Abbey Ale
Steamed green beans
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4cm chunks.
Pat meat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned. Remove beef.
Add butter and sliced onions to the pot.
Sauté onions over medium heat until dark golden brown.
Stir in brown sugar and vinegar. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return beef and accumulated juices to the pot.
Pour in beer and beef stock. Add thyme and bay leaves.
Spread mustard onto sourdough slices. Place mustard-side down on the liquid.
Cover pot. Simmer on low heat for 2.5 hours.
Stir the dissolved bread into the sauce to thicken.
Season to taste. Remove bay leaves and thyme stems.
notes: Use a high-quality Belgian Dubbel for the best flavor profile.
Do not rush the onion caramelization; it provides the base color.
Ensure the beef is fork-tender before removing from heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Breast, Black Truffle Jus, Potato Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared golden-brown chicken breast, presented whole, rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate. Beside it, a fluid, organic swoosh of impossibly smooth, ivory potato puree creates a soft contrast. A rich, dark, glossy black truffle jus forms a deliberate, artful pool adjacent to the chicken. The dish exhibits sophisticated minimalism with abundant negative space. A few vibrant green microgreens are precisely placed on the chicken for a subtle pop of color. The setting features a cool white Carrara marble surface, a precisely folded white linen napkin, and subtle, dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, emphasizing the dish as the singular focal point. The presentation is refined and architectural, embodying ultra-sophisticated restraint.
instructions: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal each breast individually. Cook in a sous vide bath at 63°C for 1.5 hours.
Prepare ice bath. Transfer cooked chicken immediately to ice bath to chill completely. This stops cooking and ensures moisture retention.
For the potato puree: Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
Pass hot potatoes through a fine-mesh sieve or ricer into a saucepan. Add 100g butter and heavy cream. Whisk vigorously until smooth and creamy. Season with salt. Keep warm.

For the black truffle jus: Finely mince shallot and garlic. In a small saucepan, melt 20g butter. Sauté shallot and garlic until translucent. Add chicken stock and thyme. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half, skimming impurities.

Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Return to clean saucepan. Stir in remaining 30g butter until emulsified. Grate or finely chop fresh black truffle into the jus. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
To finish chicken: Remove chilled chicken breasts from bags. Pat very dry with paper towels. Heat a cast iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a splash of high smoke point oil.

Sear chicken breasts, presentation side down, until deep golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes. Flip and sear other side briefly, about 1 minute. Transfer to a wire rack. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes. Slice each breast in half on the bias, if desired, or serve whole for a bolder presentation.

To plate: Create a fluid, organic swoosh of potato puree on one side of a large plate. Place one whole seared chicken breast or two bias-cut halves beside the puree. Spoon a generous pool of black truffle jus next to the chicken. Garnish with a few delicate microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon Potatoes and Cheesy Orzo
recipes.visual_description: On a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, a golden-brown roasted chicken thigh is centrally placed. Around it, artfully arranged are rustic quartered potatoes, vibrant green broccoli florets, charred red bell pepper strips, tender onion wedges, and burst halved cherry tomatoes. Thin, slightly caramelized lemon slices rest on the chicken. Creamy, off-white feta orzo is neatly spooned to one side. The dish features rich browns, deep greens, bright reds, and creamy whites. Textures include crispy chicken skin, fluffy potatoes, and tender-crisp vegetables. Chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the entire dish. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table with a white cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware. The background suggests a casual bistro, lit with warm, natural, even light, showcasing a single, balanced restaurant-style portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in pan juices.
Accompany with a simple Greek salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Quarter potatoes. Cut onion into wedges. Roughly chop bell pepper. Smash garlic cloves. Halve cherry tomatoes.
On a large baking sheet, toss potatoes, onion, bell pepper, garlic, and cherry tomatoes with 30ml olive oil, half the dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Roast for 20 minutes.
While vegetables roast, pat chicken thighs dry. Toss chicken with remaining 30ml olive oil, remaining dried oregano, salt, pepper, and the juice of half the lemon.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Add chicken and broccoli florets to the sheet. Arrange thin slices from the other half of the lemon over the chicken.
Return to oven. Roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, cook orzo pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain well.
Stir crumbled feta cheese into the hot, drained orzo. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve roasted chicken and vegetables alongside cheesy orzo. Garnish the entire dish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Mushroom & Kale Bruschetta with White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Garlic Mushroom & Kale Bruschetta sits on an off-white, slightly irregular ceramic plate. A thick slice of rustic sourdough bread, deeply toasted to a golden-brown, forms the base. Piled high atop the bread is a savory, earthy mixture of thickly sliced, deeply browned cremini mushrooms, vibrant green, tender wilted kale, and creamy white cannellini beans. The ingredients are casually arranged, overlapping naturally, showcasing their varied textures and rich, natural colors. A light drizzle of olive oil glistens on the surface. A sprinkling of freshly chopped bright green parsley provides a fresh contrast, along with a few subtle red pepper flakes. The plate is positioned on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table, revealing the natural grain of the wood. A simple, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone rests beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, soft, natural light, creating a comforting, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The background is minimally cluttered, allowing the homely dish to be the clear focal point.

ingredients.name: Rustic bread (sourdough or ciabatta), about 2cm thick

instructions: Heat a large frying pan over medium heat. Add 30ml olive oil.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Remove mushrooms from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pan. Add minced garlic. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add chopped kale to the pan. Cook, stirring, for 3-5 minutes until kale is wilted and tender.
Return mushrooms to the pan. Add rinsed cannellini beans and vegetable broth. Stir to combine.
Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and liquid to slightly reduce.
While mixture cooks, toast bread slices until golden and crisp.
Divide mushroom, kale, and bean mixture evenly among toasted bread slices. Pile generously.
Garnish each bruschetta with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken and Sausage Orecchiette
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Tuscan Chicken and Sausage Orecchiette is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The orecchiette pasta, cooked al dente, is generously coated in a rustic, rich red tomato sauce. Visible within the sauce are irregular chunks of seared golden-brown chicken and crumbled, savory Italian sausage. Halved dark purple-black Kalamata olives are scattered throughout, adding visual contrast and briny notes. A generous sprinkle of pale yellow grated Parmesan cheese and vibrant green chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, enhancing both color and aroma. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by traditional silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar

ingredients.name: Italian sausage (mild or hot, casing removed)

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken and sausage with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage. Cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Add chicken chunks to the same skillet. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Add crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked sausage and chicken to the skillet. Stir to combine. Simmer sauce for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
While sauce simmers, cook orecchiette pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water.
Add cooked pasta, reserved pasta water, and halved Kalamata olives to the sauce. Stir well to coat pasta. Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the fresh basil and half of the Parmesan cheese. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh basil and Parmesan cheese.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality canned San Marzano tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Salmon Ceviche with Bell Pepper & Lime
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Salmon Ceviche is presented in a small, clean white porcelain bowl. Opaque, pale pink-orange salmon cubes, approximately 1 cm, are mixed with vibrant red, finely diced bell pepper cubes, approximately 0.5 cm. Scattered throughout are fine green flecks of chopped cilantro and translucent, slivered pieces of red onion. A clear, slightly milky 'leche de tigre' pools at the bottom of the bowl. The arrangement is natural and inviting, not overly structured, with moderate negative space. A small sprig of fresh cilantro is placed delicately on top, and a thin lime wheel rests on the rim of the bowl. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, beside a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh colors and textures. The background is a casual restaurant atmosphere, minimal and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately upon preparation.
Traditionally accompanied by cancha (toasted corn) or sweet potato cubes.
instructions: Dice salmon into 1 cm cubes. Place in a non-reactive bowl.
Finely dice red bell pepper into 0.5 cm cubes. Add to salmon.
Finely mince garlic cloves. Add to bowl.
Thinly slice red onion, then finely mince. Add to bowl.
Finely chop cilantro. Add to bowl.
If using, finely mince Serrano chili. Add to bowl.
Juice limes and lemon. Pour 120 ml citrus juice over ingredients. Ensure salmon is mostly submerged.
Add salt and black pepper to taste. If using, add aji amarillo paste.
Gently mix all ingredients.
Marinate in refrigerator for 10-15 minutes. Salmon should turn opaque.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.
notes: Use very fresh, sushi-grade salmon for best results.
Do not over-marinate the salmon; it should be firm but tender, not rubbery.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Rib, Mustard Jus, Barley & Brown Rice, Parmesan Parcel
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of braised beef short rib is the focal point, presented as two substantial, clean-cut chunks, deeply caramelized. Adjacent, a neat, flowing mound of al dente pearl barley and brown rice medley offers textural contrast with its golden-brown hues. A single, perfectly formed Parmesan pasta parcel, delicate and off-white, rests beside the beef. A rich, glossy mustard jus, a deep amber, is artfully spooned around the components, creating natural, organic lines across the pristine white bone china plate. A golden, irregular Parmesan crisp stands upright, adding architectural height and crisp texture. Vibrant green microgreens provide a precise color accent. The dish is centered on a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting with subtle shadows, emphasizing depth. A crisp white linen napkin, precisely folded, completes the ultra-minimalist, high-end presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Season beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed oven-safe pot over high heat. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced carrots, celery, and onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add smashed garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half. Return beef to pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.

Cover pot tightly and transfer to preheated oven. Braise for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Remove beef from pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Skim fat from braising liquid. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens into a rich jus. Whisk in Dijon mustard and unsalted butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Rinse pearl barley and brown rice separately. Cook barley in salted boiling water for 25-30 minutes until al dente. Drain. Cook brown rice in salted boiling water for 20-25 minutes until al dente. Drain.
Combine cooked barley and brown rice. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Roll out fresh pasta dough thinly. Cut into 8x8 cm squares. In a small bowl, combine ricotta cheese and 50g grated Parmesan. Season lightly.

Place a small spoonful of ricotta-Parmesan filling onto the center of each pasta square. Moisten edges with water. Fold into a parcel or ravioli shape, pressing to seal edges. Cook pasta parcels in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes until al dente. Gently remove with a slotted spoon.
For Parmesan crisps: Grate remaining Parmesan into small mounds on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Let cool.

To plate: Place a portion of combined barley and brown rice medley on one side of the plate. Arrange 1-2 generous chunks of braised short rib next to it. Place a single Parmesan pasta parcel artfully near the beef. Spoon a generous amount of mustard jus around the elements. Garnish with a Parmesan crisp and a few microgreens. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure beef reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) during braising.
The pasta dough can be made ahead or store-bought fresh pasta sheets can be used for convenience.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Karahi
recipes.visual_description: Chicken Karahi presented in a small, black cast-iron karahi bowl, centered on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, deep red-orange gravy is thick and clings to generous, tender chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm. Visible softened diced tomatoes and caramelized diced onions are integrated into the sauce. A vibrant garnish of freshly chopped green coriander and thin julienned ginger strips is generously scattered over the top, adding contrasting color and texture. The overall composition is clean and inviting. Beside the plate, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and a small stack of warm, fluffy naan bread are arranged. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple, light wooden table surface. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and authentic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with warm naan bread or basmati rice.
Accompanied by a side of sliced red onion and lemon wedges.
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai or heavy-bottomed pan.
Add diced onion. Sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides.
Stir in turmeric, red chili, cumin, and coriander powders. Cook 2 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Add 50ml water. Cover and simmer 15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in garam masala and crushed fenugreek leaves. Cook 2 minutes.
Adjust salt.
Garnish with fresh coriander and julienned ginger.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Latin American Chicken, Sausage, and Potato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Latin American Chicken, Sausage, and Potato Rice is presented in an everyday, rustic ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh, left whole, rests atop a bed of fluffy, saffron-tinged rice mixed with tender, diced potatoes, vibrant red chorizo rounds, and soft diced bell pepper and onion. The chicken shows a perfectly seared crust. The rice is moist and loosely piled, showcasing its individual grains and the various diced vegetables. A fresh lime wedge is placed on the side of the bowl. A small, simple side bowl holds a mound of fresh mixed salad greens. The setting features a casually placed cloth napkin and simple flatware, bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a lived-in, homely family dining atmosphere. The scene is uncluttered, focusing on the comforting and hearty dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for squeezing over the rice.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
Offer a side of your favorite hot sauce for an extra kick.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice chorizo sausage into thick rounds.
Dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Dice onion and bell pepper. Mince garlic.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chorizo rounds. Cook until browned and crisp, about 3-4 minutes. Remove chorizo and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pot.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the pot if needed. Add chicken thighs. Sear until golden brown on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced potatoes and rinsed rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and diced tomatoes. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs and cooked chorizo back into the rice mixture.
Cover and continue to simmer for another 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh cilantro if using.
Serve individual portions with a wedge of lime and a simple side of mixed salad greens.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
If the rice appears too dry during cooking, add a small amount of extra broth. If too wet, cook uncovered for a few more minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Poached Chicken, Fermented Tomato, Crispy Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Poached Chicken, Fermented Tomato, and Crispy Potato is artfully arranged on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone, allowing ample white space. Golden-brown roasted potato wedges are casually placed on one side of the plate. Beside them, tender, pale white thick-cut pieces of poached chicken are nestled. Glistening, halved lacto-fermented cherry tomatoes, vibrant red with occasional streaks of their brine, are spooned over the chicken and potatoes. A small, organic dollop of creamy white herb cheese sits elegantly beside the chicken. Crispy, golden-brown potato peels are scattered naturally across the dish, adding texture and visual interest. The presentation is clean, minimalist, and unfussy, highlighting the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. The plate rests on a light-colored reclaimed wood table. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded simply beside the plate. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft, natural lighting emphasizing the dish's fresh colors and textures. Subtle green foliage from a houseplant is visible in the soft-focus background, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Peel potatoes, reserving all peels. Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges or chunks.
Toss potato wedges with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking tray.
Toss reserved potato peels with 1 tablespoon olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a separate baking tray.
Roast potato wedges for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Roast potato peels for 15-20 minutes, or until crispy. Watch peels closely to prevent burning. Remove from oven and set aside.
In a deep saucepan, combine water or vegetable stock, smashed garlic, quartered onion, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Carefully add chicken breasts to the simmering liquid. Ensure chicken is fully submerged. Adjust heat to maintain a very gentle simmer, do not boil vigorously.
Poach chicken for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from liquid and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, prepare herb cheese. In a small bowl, combine fresh cream cheese, chopped parsley, chopped chives, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick pieces.

To plate, arrange roasted potato wedges on one side of a handcrafted ceramic plate. Place thick-cut chicken pieces beside the potatoes. Spoon lacto-fermented cherry tomatoes over and around the chicken.
Place a small dollop of herb cheese next to the chicken. Scatter crispy potato peels over the entire dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot Gnocchi with Sage Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-orange carrot gnocchi is naturally piled in the center of a clean, white porcelain dinner bowl. Each small, ridged gnocchi pillow is coated in a glistening, golden-brown sage butter sauce. Crispy, dark green sage leaves are scattered throughout, providing a textural contrast. A generous dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese lightly covers the top. The overall presentation is warm and inviting, showcasing the gnocchi's soft, tender texture and rich color. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and a classic silver fork are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even light highlights the dish, with a softly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel and chop carrots into 2cm pieces. Toss carrots with 15ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 25 minutes until very tender.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Pass hot potatoes through a ricer or mash thoroughly.
Pass roasted carrots through a ricer or mash thoroughly. Combine hot mashed carrots and potatoes in a large bowl. Spread mixture to cool slightly, about 10 minutes.
Add 1 large egg to the cooled carrot and potato mixture. Gradually mix in 250g all-purpose flour, adding more if needed, until a soft, pliable dough forms. Do not overmix; knead only until combined.

Divide dough into 4 portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll each portion into a 2cm thick rope. Cut ropes into 2.5cm pieces. Gently roll each piece over a gnocchi board or the tines of a fork to create ridges.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi in batches. Cook 2-3 minutes until gnocchi float to the surface and are cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon.

While gnocchi cook, melt 100g unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 15-20 fresh sage leaves. Cook until butter is golden brown and sage leaves are crispy. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cooked gnocchi directly to the sage butter sauce in the skillet. Gently toss to coat. Serve immediately. Garnish generously with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Cauliflower and Mushroom Medley with Mashed Potatoes
recipes.special_requests: Add sauce with milk or cream, use only pan and fry, all above mashed potato
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Cauliflower and Mushroom Medley is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly irregular edge. A mound of fluffy, smooth mashed potatoes forms the base. Spooned over the mashed potatoes is the rich, creamy medley of pan-fried cauliflower florets, some with golden-brown edges, alongside tender, sliced brown mushrooms, and soft, amber caramelized onion pieces. The components are naturally arranged, with the thick, off-white sauce coating the vegetables, allowing some to touch the plate. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The scene is set on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table. A metal fork and knife are casually placed to the right of the plate. A folded, unbleached linen napkin sits nearby. Warm, soft overhead kitchen light creates gentle shadows, highlighting the comforting textures and natural colors of the dish. The background is minimally blurred, showing hints of a homely kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain. Mash potatoes with 30g butter, 50ml milk, and salt until smooth. Set aside.

Slice onions thinly. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-35 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Remove onions from pan. Set aside.

Cut cauliflower into small florets. Slice mushrooms. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter to the same pan over medium-high heat. Add cauliflower florets. Pan-fry for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp and lightly browned.

Add sliced mushrooms to the pan with cauliflower. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are golden and their moisture has evaporated. Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Return caramelized onions to the pan with cauliflower and mushrooms. Pour in vegetable broth, remaining 150ml milk, and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Season the creamy vegetable medley with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of mashed potatoes onto each plate. Top with the creamy cauliflower and mushroom medley. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Cauliflower Mushroom Patties with Creamy Onion Gravy
recipes.special_requests: Add sauce with milk or cream, use only pan and fry, all above mashed potato
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of this comforting dish sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slight rim. A generous mound of creamy, smooth mashed potato forms the base. Two golden-brown, pan-fried cauliflower and mushroom patties, about 2 cm thick, are nestled on top of the mash. Scattered over the patties and spilling slightly onto the mash are tender, deeply caramelized onion slices, showcasing their rich, glossy brown hue. A velvety, pale cream sauce is generously poured over the patties and mash, glistening softly. The dish is finished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple fork and a casually folded linen napkin. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the homely textures and inviting colors.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg, peeled, cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Place potato chunks in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain well. Return potatoes to the pot. Add 50 ml milk and 25g butter. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 10g butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and very soft. Remove from pan and set aside.

In the same pan, add 1 tablespoon olive oil. Add cauliflower florets and finely chopped mushrooms. Sauté over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes until softened and any liquid from mushrooms has evaporated. Transfer to a bowl. Let cool slightly.

Once cool enough to handle, use a potato masher or fork to mash the cauliflower and mushroom mixture until mostly combined but still with some texture. Season with salt and pepper. Form into 8-10 sturdy patties, about 2 cm thick.
Heat a clean large pan over medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add patties. Fry for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and heated through. Cook in batches if necessary. Keep warm.

In the pan used for onions and vegetables (or a clean pan), melt 15g butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring. Gradually whisk in remaining 150 ml milk and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until thickened. Stir in cream. Season with salt and pepper.

Divide mashed potato among four plates. Place 2-3 cauliflower mushroom patties on top of the mash. Spoon caramelized onions over the patties. Ladle creamy sauce generously over everything. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Creamy Vegetable and Potato Skillet
recipes.special_requests: Add sauce with milk or cream, use only pan and fry
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Homestyle Creamy Vegetable and Potato Skillet is presented on an everyday, off-white ceramic plate. A substantial mound of fluffy, golden-brown mashed potatoes is dolloped atop a rich, simmering base of tender sautéed cauliflower florets, meaty sliced mushrooms, and deeply caramelized onion chunks. The creamy sauce, binding the vegetables, shows a velvety texture with hints of pale yellow. Colors are natural: earthy browns from the cooked vegetables, creamy white from the mash, and a vibrant green sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley over the potatoes. The dish is casually arranged, allowing components to naturally overlap. The entire plate is visible, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and a casually folded cloth napkin are placed beside it. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Peel and cube potatoes. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Mash with 50g butter and 200ml milk until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Slice onions thinly. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft. Remove from skillet and set aside.

Cut cauliflower into small florets. Slice mushrooms. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same skillet. Increase heat to medium. Add cauliflower and mushrooms. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp and lightly browned. Remove and set aside with onions.
Melt remaining 30g butter in the skillet. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in remaining 300ml milk and vegetable stock until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until sauce thickens. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper.
Return caramelized onions, sautéed cauliflower, and mushrooms to the skillet with the sauce. Stir to combine. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Serve the creamy vegetable mixture directly from the skillet or portion onto individual plates. Top each serving generously with a large dollop of mashed potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom & Cauliflower Skillet with Mashed Potato Topping
recipes.special_requests: Add sauce with milk or cream, use only pan and fry
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy mushroom and cauliflower skillet, topped with golden-brown mashed potatoes, served in a rustic ceramic gratin dish or a small cast-iron skillet on a worn wooden dining table. The surface of the mashed potato topping is lightly browned and textured, showing peaks from a fork or spoon, with some steam gently rising. Below, the rich, creamy sauce, studded with tender, pan-fried cauliflower florets and sliced mushrooms, is visible around the edges. Deeply caramelized diced onions are mixed throughout the vegetable base, adding a dark, savory contrast. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top. The overall presentation is warm and inviting, typical of a comforting home-cooked meal, with natural, earthy colors. A simple, everyday fork rests beside the dish on a casually placed cloth napkin.
instructions: Prepare Mashed Potatoes: Place cubed potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Mash potatoes with 25g butter and 100ml milk until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Caramelize Onions: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-low heat. Add diced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply golden brown and very soft. Remove onions from skillet and set aside.

Cook Vegetables: Add remaining 1 tbsp oil to the same skillet. Increase heat to medium-high. Add cauliflower florets. Pan-fry for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned and tender-crisp. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Make Creamy Sauce: Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 25g butter to the skillet. Once melted, stir in 2 tbsp plain flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux. Gradually whisk in 200ml vegetable stock and 50ml milk and 100ml cream until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring, until sauce thickens.

Combine and Assemble: Return caramelized onions to the skillet with the cauliflower and mushrooms. Stir well to coat all vegetables in the creamy sauce. Season the vegetable mixture with salt and pepper to taste.
Top with Mash: Spoon the mashed potatoes evenly over the vegetable mixture in the skillet, spreading to cover. Create peaks and swirls with a fork.

Finish: If desired, place the skillet under a preheated broiler for 5-7 minutes until the mashed potato topping is golden brown and slightly crisp. Alternatively, cover and heat through on the stovetop over low heat for 5-10 minutes. Serve immediately.
Garnish: Sprinkle with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Vegetarian Shepherd's Pie
recipes.special_requests: Add sauce with milk or cream
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Creamy Vegetarian Shepherd's Pie rests in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The mashed potato topping, golden-brown and lightly textured from fork peaks, covers a creamy, rich vegetable filling. Hints of the tender cauliflower florets and sliced mushrooms, bound in a light brown, herbaceous sauce, peek out from under the mashed potato. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, everyday ceramic plate, a metal fork, and a casually placed cloth napkin complete the setting. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and natural colors of the home-cooked meal.
instructions: Peel and chop potatoes into large chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Mash with 30g butter and 100ml milk until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Slice onions thinly. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelised and golden-brown. Set aside.
Cut cauliflower into small florets. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms. Cook until browned. Add cauliflower florets and minced garlic. Cook for 5 minutes until slightly tender.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in vegetable stock and remaining 50ml milk and cream. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Stir in caramelised onions and chopped fresh thyme. Season filling with salt and pepper. Pour vegetable filling into a 2-litre ovenproof dish.
Spoon mashed potato evenly over the filling. Create rough peaks with a fork. Bake in a preheated oven at 190°C for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden-brown and the filling is bubbling.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Cauliflower Mushroom Hash with Creamy Mashed Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Crispy Cauliflower Mushroom Hash rests on an off-white, rustic ceramic plate. The hash is a hearty mix of golden-brown cauliflower florets and deeply browned mushroom slices, intertwined with soft, amber caramelized onions. The cauliflower shows some crisp edges, contrasting with the tender mushrooms. A large, dollop of creamy, off-white mashed potato, visibly smooth with a few small lumps, sits beside the hash. A small scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley is sprinkled over both the hash and the mashed potato, adding a pop of color. The plate is placed on a well-used, warm-toned wooden kitchen table, showing slight wear. Standard, well-worn metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a home kitchen, creating a lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Slice onions thinly. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deep golden brown and very soft. Set aside.

Peel potatoes and cut into 2 cm cubes. Place potato cubes in a large pot. Cover with cold water and add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain well.
Return drained potatoes to the hot pot. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Cut cauliflower into small florets. Slice mushrooms thinly. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.

Add cauliflower florets to the hot pan. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp and lightly browned. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their moisture and are deeply browned.
Stir the caramelized onions into the cauliflower and mushroom mixture. Season the hash generously with salt and black pepper. Cook for 2-3 minutes to heat through and combine flavors.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Ladle the crispy hash onto individual plates. Serve a generous scoop of creamy mashed potatoes alongside the hash. Garnish both with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Cauliflower and Mushroom Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Savory Cauliflower and Mushroom Bake is presented in a rustic, oval ceramic baking dish, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The mashed potato topping is golden brown and slightly peaked, with visible texture from oven baking. Underneath, a hearty mix of roasted cauliflower florets, sautéed sliced mushrooms, and rich caramelized onions peeks out from the sides, bound in a deep brown savory gravy. The colors are warm and earthy: golden potatoes, deep browns of mushrooms and onions, and the creamy white of cauliflower. A scattering of fresh chopped parsley provides a simple green garnish. The setting is cozy, with soft, warm kitchen lighting. An everyday ceramic plate with a simple fork and a casually folded cloth napkin completes the homely scene. The overall impression is comforting and inviting, a true centerpiece of a family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender. Drain well.
Mash potatoes with 30 g butter and milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Cut cauliflower into 3 cm florets. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread cauliflower on a baking tray. Roast for 20 minutes until tender and slightly browned.
Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
In a large pan, melt remaining 30 g butter over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms and cook until browned and softened. Stir in minced garlic for 1 minute.
Add caramelized onions to the pan with mushrooms. Stir to combine.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to cook flour.
Gradually whisk in vegetable broth until sauce thickens and is smooth. Season with thyme, salt, and pepper.
Gently stir in roasted cauliflower. Transfer vegetable mixture to a 20x25 cm ovenproof dish.
Spread mashed potato evenly over the top of the vegetable filling.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and filling is bubbly.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Home-Style Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Hearty Home-Style Shepherd's Pie rests on a simple, round ceramic plate. The mashed potato topping is deeply golden-brown, forming a comforting, rustic crust with fork tines visible. Beneath, the rich, dark vegetable filling, featuring tender cauliflower florets, earthy sliced mushrooms, and glistening caramelized onions, peeks out, hinting at its hearty depth. A few fresh thyme sprigs are casually placed on top. The plate sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table, suggesting a warm, inviting family setting. Soft, natural overhead lighting enhances the dish's comforting appeal. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a metal fork lie beside the plate, completing the homely scene. The portion is ample and satisfying.
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.

While potatoes boil, thinly slice onions. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 30-40 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Remove from pan and set aside.
Cut cauliflower into small florets. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic. Chop fresh thyme.

In the same pan, add remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cauliflower florets. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until lightly browned and tender-crisp. Add minced garlic and chopped thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 1 minute. Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir to coat. Cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Return caramelized onions to the pan. Season filling with salt and pepper to taste. Simmer 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to 190°C. For mashed potatoes, add 60 g butter and 100 ml milk to the drained potatoes. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the vegetable filling into a 20x20 cm oven-safe dish or individual ramekins. Spread mashed potatoes evenly over the filling. Create peaks with a fork. If desired, sprinkle with grated cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the potato topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbly. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of creamy garlic Parmesan chicken pasta is centrally plated on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente fettuccine, coated in a rich, velvety off-white cream sauce, is loosely mounded. Interspersed throughout the pasta are golden-brown, irregular chunks of seared chicken breast, each about 2-3 cm in size. The chicken pieces show a slight char from searing, adding visual texture. Bright green flecks of fresh chopped parsley are sprinkled over the top, providing a vibrant color contrast. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese rests atop the dish. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with some sauce pooling slightly at the base. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Cook pasta according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 125 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Add cooked pasta and grated Parmesan cheese to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the skillet. Toss gently to combine.
Season with more salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked thoroughly to 75°C internal temperature.
Do not overcook the pasta; it should be al dente.
Freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts better and provides superior flavor compared to pre-grated.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Parmesan Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, generous individual portion. The rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, pale yellow Parmesan sauce. Scattered throughout are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm in size, exhibiting a slight crisp exterior. Finely diced onion and minced garlic are visible within the sauce, contributing to its texture. The dish is garnished with a scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware is arranged to the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the focal point while maintaining a clean, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Cut chicken breasts into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. This takes about 6-8 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add finely diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
